text:
The National Consumers League reported that the most popular scam on the Internet is the pyramid scheme.
In a pyramid scheme, early investors are paid with deposits from later investors.
The National Consumers League is a non-profit consumer advocacy group.
The League tracks web scams through a site called Internet Fraud Watch, established in February.
Internet Fraud Watch collects reports directly from consumers.
Law enforcement agencies have praised the Internet Fraud Watch site.
Jodie Bernstein is the director of the Federal Trade Commission's Bureau of Consumer Protection.
The FTC has used reports from Internet Fraud Watch to identify scams in their early stages.
In May, the FTC shut down a site run by Fortuna Alliance that had taken in over $6 million.
The second-most-popular Internet scam involves the sale of bogus Internet services.

The Internet Society has backed away from a proposal to expand the number of addresses on the global computer network.
The Internet Society announced it will form a nine-member committee to study the issue instead of moving ahead with the proposal.
The proposal was unveiled in August and aimed to address disputes over desirable address names.
Don Heath, president of the Internet Society, stated that there has been considerable international debate on the proposal with no consensus.
Heath mentioned that it is in the best interest of the Internet's evolution to air and resolve these issues.
Disputes over Internet names are increasing as more companies seek to market their products online.
Viacom Inc.'s MTV cable music channel had a dispute with an employee over the registration of 'mtv.com' and regained control through an out-of-court settlement.
Every site on the World Wide Web must have a unique address name.
Most addresses end with three-letter designations known as top-level domains, such as 'com', 'gov', and 'edu'.
The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority announced it would oversee the creation of up to 150 new top-level domains.

The Supreme Court justices questioned rules governing derivative investments and foreign currency trading.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has traditionally prosecuted fraudulent investments.
Sophisticated investors, such as big banks, have been allowed to trade similar financial instruments with little direct regulation.
Defendants accused of fraud by the CFTC have sought to rely on an exemption from regulation established by a 1974 amendment to the Commodity Exchange Act.
The 1974 amendment was added at the request of the Treasury Department to protect sophisticated investors from unnecessary regulation by the CFTC.
Lower courts have made conflicting rulings about the 1974 amendment.
The Supreme Court decided to hear the case of William Dunn, who was charged with fraud by the CFTC after losing $95 million of clients' money.
Jeffrey Minear defended the CFTC's prosecution of Dunn, arguing that the 1974 exemption did not cover Dunn's trading in foreign currency options.
Justice Antonin Scalia noted inconsistencies in the language used in commodity laws passed in 1974.
Gary Stumpp, Dunn's lawyer, argued that other federal agencies might have jurisdiction over fraudulent foreign exchange trading, but not the CFTC.

The government released a report on Thursday regarding Internet business and taxation.
The Treasury Department believes that new technologies should not justify new taxes.
Treasury is not considering any type of value added tax, 'bit tax,' or other new excise tax on electronic commerce.
The current tax system should evolve to tax income from all sources consistently.
The overall tax policy goal should maintain neutrality, fairness, and simplicity.
Kent Johnson is the head of sales and transaction tax practice at KPMG Peat Marwick.
Johnson stated that state governments do not share the same views as the federal government regarding taxation.
Market researchers at Jupiter Communications estimate that about $1 billion of goods and services will be sold online this year, growing to over $7 billion by the year 2000.
Tax laws and regulations may not keep pace with the growth of the worldwide computer network.
The Treasury Department is concerned that tax evaders could use Internet anonymity to avoid reporting income.

The Clinton administration will revise export rules for computer encoding technology.
A meeting was held with computer and telecommunications companies to discuss these changes.
Under Secretary of Commerce William Reinsch stated that the revisions are a work in progress.
The administration circulated a draft of new rules to overhaul Cold War era export limits on encryption products.
There is a growing demand for encryption-capable products due to the growth of the Internet and online commerce.
Coded messages can protect confidential business communications and consumer information.
The meeting was described as civil and constructive by Reinsch.
Industry officials expressed concerns that the draft rules were unclear or unworkable.
Ambassador David Aaron attended the meeting as a special envoy for cryptography.
The draft rules implement an executive order signed by President Bill Clinton.

The Federal Reserve rejected a request from the Justice Department to allow U.S. banks to collect data about borrowers.
The decision was unanimous and placed the Federal Reserve at the center of a national debate on discouraging discrimination.
Proponents of data collection believe it can help identify discrimination, while opponents view it as inherently discriminatory.
The Justice Department, supported by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, requested a change to a regulation that prohibits banks from collecting certain data.
The Justice Department argued that the lack of data hinders its ability to evaluate racial discrimination in lending to small businesses.
The Federal Reserve's board voted against changing Regulation B, citing a potential lack of authority without new legislation from Congress.
Fed Governor Lawrence Lindsey stated that the issue is part of an ongoing debate about public policy regarding individual characteristics.
Regulation B was established in 1977 to discourage discrimination by prohibiting banks from collecting data on race, gender, and age.
Fed Governor Edward Kelley described the proposed regulatory change as a significant social policy issue.
Associate Attorney General John Schmidt stated that changes to the regulation would help combat discrimination and improve understanding of the problem.

The Federal Reserve voted to allow banks to increase the percentage of revenue bank subsidiaries may earn from underwriting and dealing in securities from 10 percent to 25 percent.
The Fed Board of Governors voted unanimously on this decision.
Bank subsidiaries have previously been limited to earning 10 percent of their revenue from underwriting.
The Fed cited Swiss Bank Corp. for exceeding the 10 percent cap earlier this year.
The American Bankers Association managing director Larry LaRocca stated that the new rule is a boost for banks that underwrite securities.
Securities firms expressed dissatisfaction with the new rule, with Steve Judge from the Securities Industry Association comparing it to Santa Claus delivering gifts to only one house.
The 1933 Glass-Steagall Act generally prohibits banks from engaging in non-bank activities, but allows banks to affiliate with firms not primarily engaged in such areas under section 20.
Currently, there are 41 bank 'Section 20' subsidiaries authorized to engage in underwriting.
The Fed's action is expected to increase pressure on Congress to review financial sector regulation.
Robert Litan from the Brookings Institute noted that raising the revenue cap only partially addresses the issue and that other industries will seek to level the playing field.

House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach introduced a bill on Tuesday to change the regulatory framework for banking and financial services in the United States.
A similar bill introduced by Leach in the previous Congress did not pass due to opposition from the insurance industry and House Democrats.
Analysts believe this year's bill may have a better chance of passage, but Leach's opposition to Newt Gingrich's reelection as Speaker of the House could affect support for the bill.
Leach stated that the bill would provide expanded powers for the banking, securities, and insurance industries, with consumers being the ultimate beneficiaries.
The bill aims to increase the availability of products for banking customers and reduce costs through efficiencies.
If passed, the bill would eliminate legal barriers established after the Great Depression between banks, securities firms, and insurance companies.
The Federal Reserve voted on December 20 to allow bank subsidiaries to earn more revenue from underwriting activities.
The Comptroller of the Currency's office announced it would permit banks to enter various non-bank markets.
Leach's bill would repeal Section 20 of the Glass-Steagall Act and amend Section 32 to permit the merger of commercial and investment banks.
The bill would allow bank subsidiaries to engage in securities dealing and insurance activities, while abolishing the federal charter for thrifts.

A study by a group of Internet and computer companies claims that Internet users pose little threat to the phone system.
The coalition presented the report to counter studies by local phone companies that justified new access fees on Internet usage.
Local phone company studies claimed that Internet usage threatened to overwhelm the system.
Harris Miller, president of the Information Technology Association of America, stated that the Internet is not crashing the telephone network.
Miller claimed that the phone companies created a 'problem' to protect their own interests.
The Federal Communications Commission tentatively decided not to impose access fees on Internet providers similar to those paid by long-distance companies.
Lee Selwyn, one of the study's authors, stated that claims of phone network congestion from Internet traffic are greatly exaggerated.
Selwyn claimed that ordinary consumers using the Internet already pay enough to cover the cost of increased use.
In 1995, consumers paid more than $1.4 billion for installation and use of 6 million second phone lines for Internet access.
Local phone companies disputed Selwyn's conclusions, stating that there is a real problem with network capacity.

An influential economic research group is preparing guidelines on computer encryption for its member countries.
The guidelines will avoid some contentious issues related to encryption.
The Clinton administration sought support for its policy on exporting encryption products but did not receive an endorsement from the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
The draft guidelines do not take a position on a U.S. policy requirement for data-scrambling encryption programs to allow law enforcement access to keys.
The draft report suggests that governments should weigh the costs and benefits of key recovery without implying that legislation should or should not be initiated.
John Dryden, head of the OECD's Information, Computer and Communications Policy division, stated that member countries have differing views on controversial areas.
Some countries view encryption as a means to protect privacy and encourage global commerce, while others see it as a potential obstacle to law enforcement.
The guidelines recommend that encryption users have access to products that meet their needs and that government controls should be minimal.
The draft guidelines do not aim to reconcile differing views but instead outline competing interests and approaches.
The guidelines suggest that encryption standards and usage should be determined by the market in an open and competitive environment.

The debate over reforming America's financial services sector began on a Tuesday.
Congress and the Clinton administration prioritize reforming the financial services sector.
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato introduced his own version of comprehensive reform.
The proposed bills aim to repeal the Glass-Steagall Act, which separates banking from other financial activities.
Most members of Congress and financial service companies agree on the need for reform.
At a House Banking subcommittee hearing, representatives from various financial sectors supported allowing a single entity to operate across all financial services.
Subcommittee Chairwoman Marge Roukema noted that details of the reform are important.
The Supreme Court has removed many state insurance restrictions on banks.
The Federal Reserve increased the revenue limit for banks from securities activities from 10 percent to 25 percent.
The comptroller of the currency announced that national banks could enter non-banking businesses.

Internet access providers and others fear Congress will negatively impact cyberspace.
Company representatives met with members of the Congressional Internet Caucus to discuss legislation governing cyberspace.
Tom Evslin, vice president of AT&T Corp.'s WorldNet Internet service, believes it is inevitable that bills will be introduced to legislate Internet content.
Evslin stated that preventing Congress from making mistakes will be as difficult as getting them to address issues proactively.
Bill Schrader, president of Internet provider PSINet Inc., warned that careless legislation could destroy the Internet industry.
Members of Congress at the meeting pledged to protect the Internet.
Representative Rick White acknowledged the challenges ahead regarding various Internet-related issues.
Senator Conrad Burns warned that government legislation will lag behind private sector developments.
Last year, Congress passed the Communications Decency Act, which was opposed by online companies and civil libertarians.
Congress also defeated measures that would have imposed liability on Internet providers for copyright infringement.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has no authority over most foreign currency transactions, according to a Supreme Court ruling.
The Supreme Court issued a unanimous decision regarding the CFTC's oversight of foreign currency derivatives.
The court ruled that a 1974 law exempting some foreign currency transactions from CFTC oversight also applies to some foreign exchange derivatives.
The CFTC regulates trading of derivatives such as futures and options on various commodities and financial instruments.
Trading of regulated derivatives must occur on recognized exchanges like the Chicago Board of Trade or the New York Mercantile Exchange.
An amendment added by Congress in 1974 permits off-exchange trading in foreign currency without CFTC regulation.
The Treasury Department requested the 1974 amendment to avoid overregulation of the developing foreign currency market.
The inter-bank foreign exchange market has grown to $40 billion a day in total trading.
The CFTC has prosecuted fraudulent foreign exchange investment schemes, known as 'bucket shops.'
William Dunn argued that the 1974 Treasury amendment applied to his trading of foreign exchange options, and the Supreme Court largely agreed.

The Czech Republic and Spain played a scoreless draw in a World Cup group six qualifier on Wednesday.
The match did not meet expectations.
The Czech Republic faced their first significant test since reaching the Euro 96 final.
Real Madrid's teenage striker Raul was making his first full international appearance.
Both teams won their previous World Cup matches against weaker opponents.
Spain won 6-2 against the Faroe Islands.
The Czech Republic won 6-0 against Malta.
Yugoslavia and Slovakia had already secured wins against the same teams.
Both teams started the match tentatively, looking for mistakes from the other.
Czech striker Pavel Kuka had a cross that found Karel Poborsky, who failed to score.

East European bourses were mostly higher this week.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange reached a 30-month high before easing slightly due to profit-taking.
Budapest, Zagreb, Bratislava, Ljubljana, and Sofia posted gains.
Markets in Prague and Bucharest lost ground in listless trading.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) dipped 0.29 percent to 1,486.55 points.
Polish shares extended falls on Friday due to profit-taking after a four-session rise of 2.7 percent.
Analysts predict the market could slip below 14,800 points before improving next week.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed at 14,920.4 points, up 1.7 percent from Friday's close.
The Prague Stock Exchange has not recorded an advancing session in October.
The PX50 index closed at 542.4 on Friday, down 2.36 percent.

Boris Becker withdrew from the Czech Indoor Open due to a recurring wrist injury.
Goran Ivanisevic lost to Petr Korda with a score of 7-6 6-2.
Boris Becker tore a ligament in his right wrist at the Wimbledon championships this year.
Becker experienced pain after training and withdrew from his scheduled match against Martin Damm.
ATP Tour Supervisor Gayle Bradshaw stated that Becker's wrist was too sore for him to play.
Becker held his wrist several times during his victory over Frederik Fetterlein.
Becker attempted to return to the circuit last month but had to retire from the first round in Bucharest.
Becker also lost in the second round in Basle and withdrew from Lyon two weeks ago.
Becker's absence has affected his chances for a record 12th appearance at the ATP Tour championship.
Wayne Ferreira currently holds the eighth and final spot for the ATP Tour championship.

Wayne Ferreira and Todd Martin lost in the quarterfinals of the $475,000 Czech Indoor Open.
Wayne Ferreira lost to Tim Henman with a score of 6-4, 6-3.
Todd Martin lost to David Prinosil with a score of 7-6, 7-6.
Tim Henman is seeded seventh in the tournament and ranked 26th in the world.
Wayne Ferreira is ranked seventh in the world.
Tim Henman broke Wayne Ferreira late in both sets.
Wayne Ferreira did not gain a single break point in his match against Tim Henman.
Todd Martin is currently 199 points behind Wayne Ferreira in the race for the final spot at the ATP Tour Championships.
David Prinosil is ranked 58th in the world.
Boris Becker's wrist injury forced him out of the Ostrava tournament after the first round.

The Prague Stock Exchange closed higher for the third consecutive session on Tuesday.
The PX50 index increased by 2.5 points, or 0.47 percent, to 537.1.
Komercni Banka, IPB, Ceska Sporitelna, and Zivnostenska Banka all gained in value.
The Reuters RPIX index rose five points to 1,095.
A total of 188 shares rose, 121 shares lost value, and 74 shares remained steady.
The total trading volume was 701,356 shares with a turnover of 721.14 million crowns.
IPB's share price increased by 15 crowns to 331, marking its second consecutive five percent gain.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik indicated that a strong foreign strategic partner would likely benefit from the privatization of IPB.
Nomura and ING Bank have been rumored as potential bidders for IPB.
The government holds approximately a 30 percent stake in IPB.

The Czech monthly trade deficit in September was 10.5 billion crowns.
The trade deficit in August was 14.5 billion crowns.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported that the January-September trade shortfall reached 110.7 billion crowns.
The January-September trade shortfall surpassed the full year deficit of 95.7 billion crowns recorded in 1995.
Analysts were surprised by the decrease in the trade deficit for September.
A Reuters survey forecasted a monthly trade gap of 13-15 billion crowns.
Martin Kupka, an economist at Patria Finance, expressed optimism about the September figure but did not revise the full year forecast.
Patria Finance forecasted a year-end deficit of 150-160 billion crowns.
Imports rose by 15.2 percent year-on-year in September, while exports rose by 5.9 percent.
Machinery and transport equipment imports accounted for 38.3 percent of total imports.

Czech telephone operator SPT Telecom a.s. reported a nine-month gross profit of 6.0 billion crowns.
SPT Telecom's revenues for the first three quarters totaled 23.3 billion crowns.
SPT Telecom's total revenues for 1995 were 26.4 billion crowns.
SPT Telecom's full year gross profit for 1995 was 7.0 billion crowns.
All financial figures are calculated according to International Accounting Standards (IAS).
SPT shares closed down six crowns at 2,879 on the Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday.
The results were released after trading ended for the day.
The number of lines installed by SPT Telecom reached 272,000 lines year-to-date.
The overall installed base of lines for SPT Telecom is 2.67 million lines.
SPT Telecom aims to achieve a target of over 400,000 new set lines in 1996.

Sepap Group a.s. reported a nine-month net profit of 188.4 million crowns, down from 520.4 million crowns in the same period in 1995.
Revenues for Sepap fell to 3.94 billion crowns from 5.34 billion crowns over the same nine-month period.
The shutdown of Sepap's main paper mill and a downturn in the paper cycle negatively impacted its profits.
The Steti mill, which generates approximately 75% of Sepap's revenues and profits, reported a pre-tax profit of seven million crowns.
The gross profit for the Steti mill in the nine-month period of 1995 was approximately 95 million crowns.
Sepap's third quarter results stabilized after a downturn in the first half of the year.
The planned annual shutdown of the Steti mill is expected to increase maintenance costs.
Sepap anticipates a slight improvement in year-end earnings compared to third quarter levels.
ROTO, Sepap's second largest subsidiary, reported a nine-month pre-tax profit of 149 million crowns on sales of 1.25 billion crowns.
Michael Dingman controls 48% of Sepap through Daventree Ltd, while Assidoman holds a 39% stake in the company.

Czech equity and forex markets increased on Monday.
The increase was influenced by the Civic Democratic Party's performance in the first round of Senate elections.
Analysts cautioned that profit taking and uncertainty before the second round of voting may limit gains.
The Prague Stock Exchange rose by 10.1 points, or 2.08 percent, to 496.8.
Domestic investors were primarily responsible for the market gain, rather than foreign investors.
Jan Sykora from Wood and Co. noted a lack of foreign institutional buying due to the elections.
Lubomir Vystavel from ING Barings suggested that the market upsurge could continue if the ODS maintains its position in the second round.
The Czech crown strengthened by around 0.3 percentage points against its dollar/mark basket in early trading.
Petr Korous from Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka indicated that some profit taking led to a slight drop in the crown's value.
The ODS party received 36.47 percent of the first round vote, while the opposition Social Democrats received 20.27 percent.

Sweden beat the Czech Republic 3-0 in a World Cup ice hockey game on Thursday.
The victory set up a matchup for European group supremacy against Finland.
Sweden's offense was effective, forcing the Czechs to take several early penalties.
Mats Sundin scored the first goal for Sweden midway through the first period.
Calle Johansson scored the second goal for Sweden early in the second period.
Jonas Bergqvist scored the final goal for Sweden, making it 3-0.
The Czech Republic lost their first two games of the tournament.
The Czech team included players like Jaromir Jagr, Petr Nedved, and Martin Rucinsky.
The match took place at Prague's Sports Hall, marking the Czechs' first home game since winning the world championship.
Czech fans expressed their frustration by throwing beer cans at the Czech bench near the end of the game.

The Prague Stock Exchange reached a new year-high on Thursday.
Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna both posted strong gains.
The PX50 index increased by 3.3 points, or 0.58 percent, to a high of 574.9.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining issues by 320 to 298, with 192 remaining steady.
Total trading volume was 916,194 shares with a turnover of 648.3 million crowns.
Komercni Banka's stock price increased by 99 crowns to close at 2,439 crowns.
Ceska Sporitelna's stock price increased by 16 crowns to 351 crowns.
Jaroslav Klapal, CEO of Ceska Sporitelna, announced an expected net profit of 2.1 billion crowns for 1996.
Klapal also stated that gross profit for 1996 is expected to be at least 6.1 billion crowns.
Sporitelna's 1995 after-tax profit decreased to 263 million crowns from 980 million crowns.

The Czech trade deficit increased by nearly 16 billion crowns in October.
Analysts are not alarmed by the rise in the trade deficit as it aligns with their full year forecasts.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported that the trade gap for the first 10 months of the year reached a record 125.5 billion crowns.
The trade deficit for January-September was revised to a shortfall of 109.6 billion crowns.
The Czech Statistical Bureau, the Ministry of Industry and Trade, and most analysts predict the deficit will reach 150-160 billion crowns by year-end.
Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka, stated that the year-end deficit will be 150-160 billion crowns.
Imports rose by 14.4 percent year-on-year for the 10-month period, while exports rose by 5.2 percent.
Imports of machinery and transport equipment grew by 19.1 percent year-on-year and accounted for 38.3 percent of total imports.
Boris Gomez, an analyst at ING Barings, noted that imports are necessary for industrial restructuring.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that the record trade deficit is not tragic and is partly due to a temporary foreign investment wave.

Liberty International launched a new subsidiary to change the British pensions market.
Liberty International Pensions will target retail pensions and money purchase pension schemes.
Liberty International is 69 percent owned by South Africa's Liberty Life.
The British Telecom Pension Scheme will pay five million pounds for 10 percent of Liberty International Pensions equity.
Liberty's move into the British pensions market reflects a global shift from defined benefit to defined contribution principles.
There is an urgent need for quality privatized retirement savings in Britain.
Liberty partnered with fund management group Hermes to form Hermes Liberty International Pensions.
The BT Pension Scheme will transfer 1.5 billion pounds in assets to the Hermes Liberty joint venture.
Hermes will serve as the fund manager for the new pensions venture.
Regulatory approval is required before the new group can begin operations.

Cable & Wireless, NYNEX Corp, and Bell Canada International announced the formation of a new British cable company by merging their British subsidiaries.
The merger includes C&W's Mercury, Videotron, Bell Cablemedia, and NYNEX CableComms.
Videotron is being acquired by Bell Cablemedia in a deal valued at approximately $1.09 billion.
Cable & Wireless is making a $338 million equity investment in Bell Cablemedia as part of the acquisition of Videotron.
Cable & Wireless will own 52.6 percent of the new company, called Cable & Wireless Communications.
NYNEX will own 18.5 percent and Bell Canada will own 14.2 percent of the new company.
The remaining 15 percent of the new company will be floated.
The new company will provide integrated telecommunications, information, and entertainment services.
Cable & Wireless Communications will serve around six million homes and businesses in Britain.
The company plans to list its shares in London and New York in about six months.

Halifax Building Society is Britain's largest home loan lender.
Halifax Building Society plans to float on the stock market and shed mutuality for bank status in June.
David Gilchrist is the director of corporate affairs at Halifax.
Halifax Building Society is currently owned by its savers and borrowers.
The conversion and flotation could be worth 10 billion pounds ($16 billion).
Nine million members of Halifax will vote on the conversion early next year.
The conversion is being promoted as the largest single extension of private share ownership in Britain.
Halifax will lose five-year protection against takeover due to its conversion method.
The flotation will place Halifax in the top 25 companies of London's FTSE 100 stock index.
Halifax members will receive details of the conversion plans and share distribution scheme in January.

Britain's Invesco Plc agreed to merge with AIM Management Group Inc. in a deal valued at $1.6 billion.
The merger will create one of the world's largest investment management businesses.
The deal is the largest in U.S. fund history, according to industry experts.
The combined group will be called Amvesco Plc and will manage around $150 billion.
The merger will be financed with about $1.1 billion in new stock and the remainder in cash and debt.
Invesco's chief financial officer, Bob McCullough, stated that the merger is a prototype company for the future.
Invesco Chairman Charles Brady will lead the combined group.
AIM shareholders will own around 45 percent of the merged company.
Invesco plans to issue 290 million new shares to AIM shareholders, valued at about $1.1 billion.
McCullough indicated that there would be no culture clash between the two companies.

Greycoat Plc is a British property company.
A group of shareholders is calling for Greycoat Plc to be broken up.
Greycoat Plc is confident it will receive support from its institutional shareholders to reject the breakup plan.
Peter Thornton is the chief executive of Greycoat Plc.
Thornton stated that he would be surprised if institutional shareholders supported a closing down sale.
Thornton described the liquidation proposal by the UK Active Value Fund as ill-conceived and failing to secure shareholder value.
Greycoat Plc urged its shareholders to reject a resolution proposed by Brian Myerson at an extraordinary general meeting on November 14.
Brian Myerson is a rebel shareholder and advises the UK Active Value Fund through Active Value Advisors Ltd.
Myerson claimed there was considerable support for the proposal to dispose of Greycoat's assets.
Greycoat Plc reported a rise in interim pre-tax profits to 3.8 million stg.

Lloyd's of London declared that over 90 percent of its members had accepted a settlement offer for its recovery plan.
Lloyd's reported a significant increase in acceptances from U.S. investors after a U.S. appeals court overturned a ruling that threatened its survival.
As of Wednesday afternoon, 66.7 percent of U.S. members had accepted the recovery plan.
Lloyd's chairman David Rowland stated that the level of acceptances indicated members' clear views on the reconstruction of Lloyd's.
A Lloyd's spokesman noted that acceptances from U.S. Names had increased significantly overnight.
Only 53 percent of U.S. Names had accepted the plan by Tuesday.
A Baltimore appeals court overturned a ruling by U.S. judge Robert Payne that had granted U.S. Names more time to consider the plan.
The deadline for accepting the recovery plan was extended to allow all members a chance to respond.
Lloyd's proposed that Names pay to help reinsure billions of pounds in liabilities into a new company called Equitas.
Lloyd's problems began in the 1980s due to negligent underwriting and poor investment advice.

Greycoat is a British property company facing a break-up demand and a merger proposal from Moorfield Estates.
Greycoat shareholders postponed a vote on a proposal to sell the company's 500 million pounds portfolio for three weeks.
Moorfield Estates is run by two former Goldman Sachs property analysts.
Greycoat has not yet received concrete proposals from Moorfield.
A Greycoat spokesman stated that they have only seen one page of vague bullet points from Moorfield.
The rebel investment fund shareholders proposing the break-up resolution include UK Active Value Fund, IMP UKAV Inc, and Chaddesley Investments.
These shareholders control 11 percent of Greycoat's shares and are advised by Brian Myerson's Active Value Advisors.
At an extraordinary general meeting, Brian Myerson asked shareholders to postpone a vote on their proposals for a controlled programme of disposals.
Greycoat's chairman Michael Beckett requested Moorfield to provide a full and detailed proposal.
The vote on postponement passed with 53 million shares in favor and about 42 million shares against.

Robert Fleming announced increased pre-tax profits for the first half of the year.
Robert Fleming reported a 16 percent increase in pre-tax profit to 92.2 million pounds.
The previous year's pre-tax profit was 79.4 million pounds.
A spokesman stated that the results demonstrate the bank's commitment to remaining independent.
Flemings has been considered a potential takeover target by larger foreign investment banks.
Chief executive John Manser described the results as a 'very good start.'
Manser noted that new businesses were contributing to profitability.
Flemings acknowledged challenges in the second half due to flat Asian markets and competitive pressures.
The joint venture Jardine Fleming faced regulatory issues leading to fines and compensation of nearly $20 million.
Flemings reported a 'marginally lower' interim result for Jardine Fleming compared to the previous year.

Coopers & Lybrand issued third party proceedings against nine former directors and employees of Barings bank.
Coopers & Lybrand stated that it is not responsible for the collapse of Barings but faces a substantial claim.
Coopers & Lybrand believes it is perceived to have deep pockets available to those who lost money from Barings' collapse.
Coopers & Lybrand may take additional third party proceedings against other members of Barings management in the future.
Coopers & Lybrand was the auditor for Barings Plc, the parent company of Barings bank.
Barings bank collapsed in February 1995 under losses of approximately $1.4 billion due to unauthorized derivatives trades by Nick Leeson.
Nick Leeson is serving a six-and-a-half year jail sentence in Singapore for his role in Barings' downfall.
Ernst & Young issued claims of negligence in audits against Coopers & Lybrand and Deloitte & Touche.
Some commentators estimate the total amount of writs against Coopers & Lybrand to be around 1.0 billion pounds ($1.68 billion).
A Coopers & Lybrand official stated that no amount had been specified on the writ issued against it.

British property group MEPC reported a rise in pretax profits for the year.
MEPC's net asset value (NAV) fell to 450 pence per share from 457 pence.
James Tuckey is the chief executive of MEPC.
MEPC announced a 14 percent increase in pretax profit for the year to 140 million stg from 122.6 million stg.
Earnings per share rose nine percent to 22.9 pence.
The NAV fall was attributed to a marginal decline in values in Britain and elsewhere.
The NAV drop was less than the relevant indices.
MEPC's UK portfolio accounts for 70 percent of the group.
The valuation date for the NAV was August 31.
Tuckey indicated that a revaluation on December 1 would likely yield a different result.

Klesch & Co stated that the debt restructuring package between Eurotunnel and its creditors may not withstand additional financial demands from a recent fire.
The fire onboard a Eurotunnel HGV shuttle raised fundamental safety concerns with potentially unquantifiable long-term implications.
Klesch & Co reported that the events call into question the adequacy of the financial restructuring package as proposed.
Klesch & Co acknowledged that the immediate impact on Eurotunnel's revenues is likely to be minor.
The debt restructuring package left Eurotunnel with a contingency reserve of 600 million pounds, or approximately 67 million pounds per year over nine years.
Any development that impacts future revenues or operating efficiency could threaten the sufficiency of the financial restructuring package.
Passenger car shuttle services resumed through the tunnel three weeks after the fire closed the undersea link.
The fire destroyed a freight vehicle and damaged a section of the tunnel, resulting in 34 injuries.
Rail services for passengers between Paris and London and Brussels and London resumed last week.
The Channel Tunnel Safety Authority will need to consider the design and operation of the open-lattice freight carriers in the aftermath of the fire.

A survey by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and property consultants Grimley indicates that one third of British companies expect to raise property holdings over the next six months.
Sudhir Junankar, associate director of economic analysis at the CBI, stated that business confidence has strengthened compared to six months ago.
Junankar noted that companies expect further improvement in business, driven by domestic demand.
The survey found that 32 percent of companies expect to increase property holdings, 26 percent expect a reduction, and 41 percent do not expect any change.
Stuart Morley, Grimley's head of research, mentioned that the net balance on the survey is plus six percent over the next six months, the highest result of the five surveys conducted so far.
The report identified the distribution, metal manufacturing, chemical processing, transport, and communications sectors as likely to see the largest increases in property holdings.
Larger companies are most likely to increase their property holdings, indicating a reversal of a declining trend over the last six months.
Morley suggested that the period of large-scale restructuring for companies may have ended, as they are now looking to expand their holdings.
Companies are more optimistic about employment prospects than in previous surveys, which is contributing to increased property demand.
The retail sector has seen the largest net increase in property holdings over the past six months and is expected to continue this trend.

European privatisations in 1997 could total $53 billion.
The telecommunications and utilities sectors are expected to dominate privatisation activity in Europe.
J.P. Morgan reported that Italy has the most ambitious privatisation programme, estimated at $20 billion.
European governments may feel pressure to accelerate privatisation programmes to meet the Maastricht three percent deficit criterion.
Proceeds from privatisations could be used to reduce government financial debt but cannot be counted when calculating the deficit.
European privatisations in 1996 totalled $43 billion, a 30 percent increase from the previous high in 1994.
The total value of the European privatisation programme so far is $230 billion.
The total estimate for privatisation proceeds through the end of the century could reach $118 billion.
The utility sector had a completion rate of only 20 percent for scheduled privatisations in 1996.
The energy sector accounted for a larger than expected portion of offerings in 1996.

China's propaganda officials have removed all novels and two films by writer Wang Shuo.
The state-owned Hua Yi publishing house has stopped publishing a four-volume collection of Wang's novels.
Wang Shuo stated that he was reported to the Propaganda Department for having reactionary works.
Wang acknowledged that his works contain vulgar language and themes.
Hua Yi was forced to write a self-criticism for publishing Wang's books.
Wang claimed that no other publishing house will publish his works due to the ban.
Hua Yi has published about 200,000 copies of the 'Collected Works of Wang Shuo' since 1992.
Wang earns over 100,000 yuan annually from reprints of his works.
Military-owned bookstores have been banned from selling Wang's books.
Pirated copies of Wang's works have reportedly appeared in the market.

Wang Dan is a prominent Chinese dissident and former student leader.
Wang Dan is charged with plotting to overthrow the government.
The trial of Wang Dan is expected to be held behind closed doors.
The Beijing Number One Intermediate People's Court has not informed Wang's family of the trial date.
The court is expected to limit attendance to selected individuals to exclude foreign reporters and fellow dissidents.
A family member stated that the trial will not be open to the public despite being labeled as such.
Wang Dan has been detained since May 1995.
The charge against Wang Dan carries a maximum penalty of death and a minimum of 10 years in prison.
Wang's mother, Wang Lingyun, has expressed her intention to defend him in court.
Chinese law allows family members to defend the accused, but only lawyers can meet detained defendants.

Deng Xiaoping, China's paramount leader, is reported to be in fragile health.
Deng was absent from a rally on Tuesday that paid tribute to him and other survivors of the Long March.
Deng, aged 92, is one of about 700 surviving veterans of the Red Army who completed a 9,650 km trek across China.
Deng has not been seen in public since early 1994.
His health is a subject of speculation in China, Hong Kong, and the Asian region.
The official statement claims that Deng is in good health for his age.
Preparations were made for Deng to attend celebrations for the 50th anniversary of the World War Two victory, but he canceled at the last minute.
The Long March rally was interpreted by some analysts as a show of support for Jiang Zemin, Deng's successor.
Jiang Zemin urged the Communist Party to inherit the spirit of the Long March during the rally.
The Long March reduced the Red Army's numbers from about 100,000 to approximately 7,000.

A group of foreign legal experts has requested permission from China to observe the trial of detained dissident Wang Dan.
Wang Dan faces the capital charge of plotting to overthrow the government, which carries a maximum penalty of death and a minimum sentence of 10 years in prison.
The legal team includes French senator Robert Badinter, former U.S. attorneys-general Nicholas Katzenbach and Richard Thornburgh, and former Canadian solicitor-general Warren Allmand.
Human Rights Watch stated that the request aims to ensure Wang Dan's right to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal is respected.
Wang Dan, who has been detained since May 1995, is expected to plead not guilty at his trial, which opens on Wednesday.
Human Rights Watch indicated that the chances of China allowing foreign legal experts to observe the trial are slim.
The courtroom is often closed to journalists and other outsiders, with claims that it is too small.
Wang's mother, a museum researcher with no legal background, will attend the trial as one of two defense lawyers.
Wang's family has found a lawyer willing to defend him after being given only one day to do so.
Wang has previously served four years in prison for counter-revolutionary crimes related to pro-democracy demonstrations.

China began the trial of Wang Dan on the charge of plotting to overthrow the government.
The trial started at 9:00 a.m. local time on Wednesday.
A court official from the Beijing People's Intermediate Court confirmed the start of the trial.
Security was tight around the court building in western Beijing, with police preventing public access.
Wang Dan's father, Wang Xianzeng, protested his son's innocence before the trial began.
Wang Xianzeng stated that the outcome of the trial depended on the government's decision to convict Wang Dan.
Wang Dan's mother, Wang Lingyun, attended the trial as one of the defense lawyers.
Wang Dan faces a minimum sentence of 10 years and a maximum penalty of death.
Human Rights Watch stated that the chances of acquittal for Wang Dan were slim due to inadequate defense preparation.
Human Rights Watch criticized the trial as indicative of the Chinese leadership's increasing intolerance of dissent.

Chen Ziming, a leading Chinese dissident, is under tight police surveillance after his release on medical parole.
Chen Ziming needs permission from the police to consult a doctor.
Chen Ziming's sister, Chen Zihua, stated that his conditions after parole are not as good as when he was in prison.
Chen Ziming is unable to go downstairs to get sunlight or fresh air at his home.
Chen Ziming has heart, liver, and digestion problems and had been treated for cancer.
Chen Ziming is barred from talking to foreign reporters.
Police prevented reporters from approaching Chen Ziming's home and that of his parents.
Chen Ziming was sentenced to 13 years in prison in 1991 for engaging in counter-revolutionary activities during the Tiananmen Square protests.
Chen Ziming was released on medical parole in 1994, which was seen as an effort by Beijing to maintain trade relations with Washington.
Chen Ziming was returned to prison in 1995 after advocating for the release of political prisoners.

Kao Ching-yuan is a Taiwanese business leader and vice-chairman of President Enterprises.
Kao urged Beijing to resume talks with Taiwan to maintain investor confidence.
Kao stated that political friction could lead to higher risks for Taiwanese investors in China.
Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanqing stated that no one could obstruct direct trade and transport links between China and Taiwan.
Kao is leading a delegation of nearly 80 Taiwanese business leaders and politicians in Beijing.
Taiwan's economic officials are visiting China in a private capacity.
Kao called for the resumption of talks that were suspended after President Lee Teng-hui's trip to the United States.
Beijing considers Taiwan a rebel province and seeks to isolate it diplomatically.
Taiwan's economic planners have prepared measures to restrict investment in China if relations deteriorate.
Indirect trade and transport links between Taiwan and China have been allowed since the late 1980s.

China announced that a court rejected the appeal of Zhou Beifang, a son of a politically powerful family.
The court upheld a suspended death sentence for Zhou Beifang for bribery.
Zhou Beifang is 43 years old and was the former chairman of Hong Kong-listed affiliates of Capital Iron and Steel Corp (Shougang).
The court showed leniency to Zhou Beifang because he expressed remorse.
Zhou's death sentence was suspended for two years, which usually indicates it will not be carried out if he repents and cooperates with authorities.
Zhou Beifang is considered one of China's 'princelings', children of the ruling party elite.
The Zhou family has close ties to the family of Deng Xiaoping.
Zhou voluntarily returned ill-gotten wealth before prosecutors obtained evidence against him.
Zhou was convicted of accepting bribes totaling 9.28 million Hong Kong dollars ($1.2 million) between June 1993 and April 1994.
Zhou was also found guilty of paying 1.2 million yuan ($144,600) in bribes to facilitate his wife and daughter's move to the British colony.

A Chinese court rejected the appeal of dissident Wang Dan and upheld an 11-year prison sentence for subversion.
The verdict was announced four days before the arrival of U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
Family members protested for one hour in front of the Beijing Higher People's Court after the court's decision.
Wang Dan's mother, Wang Lingyun, expressed anger and described the verdict as unfair.
Wang Dan was not allowed to speak during his appeal hearing.
Wang Dan was convicted of plotting to subvert the government by publishing articles and receiving funds from hostile overseas organizations.
Wang Lingyun stated she would petition the appeals court, but it would not involve a new trial.
The state media did not report on Wang Dan's conviction.
Police restricted access to the court building and the family's home.
Wang Dan had previously served four years in prison for his involvement in the 1989 student demonstrations.

Bankruptcies in China are expected to more than double in number this year.
Authorities in China are trying to shed hopelessly indebted firms.
The number of bankruptcies is expected to rise further next year as officials become more determined not to subsidise loss-making state firms.
More than 5,200 Chinese companies were expected to go bankrupt in 1996, up from 2,200 in 1995.
Cao Siyuan, architect of China's bankruptcy law, stated that the increasing rate of bankruptcies is unavoidable.
In the first half of this year, 1,692 enterprises declared bankruptcy, an increase of more than 107 percent compared to the previous year.
A total of 1,625 firms declared bankruptcy in 1994, up from 710 in 1993.
China passed a bankruptcy law in 1988 to address issues with state-owned enterprises.
China is expected to accelerate bankruptcies and mergers of state firms next year to reduce the burden on state finances.
Cao Siyuan indicated that the current bankruptcy rate is less than 0.1 percent of the total number of firms in China.

A seven-year-old boy has been chosen by China as Tibet's second holiest monk.
The boy attended a ritual in Beijing to celebrate the first anniversary of his enthronement.
Monks performed traditional activities such as pounding drums, ringing bells, and chanting Buddhist scriptures during the event.
The boy is recognized by Beijing as the reincarnation of the Panchen Lama.
The Dalai Lama has named another boy as the reincarnation of the 10th Panchen Lama, who died in 1989.
Many Tibetans view the Chinese-sanctioned child, Gyantsen Norpo, as a pretender.
Chinese state media has promoted Beijing's choice to convince Tibetans of his legitimacy.
The boy has been seen blessing believers and preaching from the seat reserved for the 10th Panchen Lama.
Chinese sources state that the boy lives in Beijing under state protection.
Western human rights groups have accused Beijing of detaining the boy recognized by the Dalai Lama.

China pledged to curb provincial investments in high-profile industries.
Economists stated that defiance from regional authorities would hinder the central government's economic restructuring efforts.
The People's Daily reported that many new state enterprises were doomed due to blind investment in provinces.
The newspaper claimed that many enterprises entered a cycle of high investment, high resource consumption, low production efficiency, and poor management.
Many old enterprises struggle to upgrade technology and lose their competitive edge, according to the newspaper.
The newspaper cited 22 provinces that listed car production as a pillar industry in their Five-Year Plans from 1996 to 2000 and for 2010.
Twenty-four provinces listed electronics as a pillar industry through 2000, and 16 provinces focused on machinery and chemicals.
Economist Mao Tianqi stated that blind investment has been a major problem for China's economy.
Blind investment has led to monopolies and local protectionism, with provinces banning competitive products from neighboring regions.
The central government plans to restructure the economy next year to improve efficiency and curb concentration in high-profile industries.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) warned of a subdued profit outlook for the 1996/97 year and beyond.
CBA cited a competitive housing market, falling margins, and higher wage costs as reasons for the profit outlook.
CBA chairman Tim Besley stated that nothing had changed in the first three months of the year to alter earlier forecasts of flat profits.
Besley indicated that the 1996/97 financial year would be as challenging as previously anticipated.
The home loan market is described as intensely competitive by Besley.
CBA reported a net profit of A$1.12 billion for the 1995/96 year, an increase from A$983 million in 1994/95.
CBA expected earnings to be flat in 1996/97 when it released its results in August.
Besley mentioned that CBA's directors aimed to maintain the ratio of dividends per share to earnings per share at around 80 percent in 1996/97.
Besley noted that banking industry profits could decline over the long run and that CBA must work to ensure its profit declines are less than those of other banks.
CBA Managing Director David Murray interpreted Besley's comments as indicating a fall in the growth rate of profits.

Rupert Murdoch reported that News Corp. Ltd. performed below expectations in the first quarter.
Murdoch stated that News Corp. is still on track for a 20 percent profit rise this year.
Murdoch is the chairman and chief executive of News Corp.
Murdoch announced a more conservative approach to financing new acquisitions.
Murdoch expressed confidence in achieving a 20 percent increase in profit for the year.
Analysts viewed Murdoch's comments as disappointing and became more skeptical about the 20 percent profit pledge.
Traders on the Australian share market sold News Corp. shares, which closed at A$7.20 ($5.69).
In the 1995/96 year, News Corp's net profit decreased to A$1.02 billion ($806 million) from A$1.37 billion in 1994/95 ($1.08 billion).
Murdoch indicated that revenues at the Fox U.S. television business began slowly due to the Atlanta Olympic Games.
Murdoch stated that Australian newspaper revenues would be flat in 1996/97.

Rupert Murdoch stated that The News Corp Ltd's first quarter performance was below expectations.
Murdoch expressed confidence in a 20 percent profit rise for the year 1996/97.
In the 1995/96 year, News Corp's net profit decreased to A$1.02 billion from A$1.37 billion in 1994/95.
Murdoch indicated that revenues at the Fox U.S. television business started slowly in 1996/97 due to the Atlanta Olympic Games.
He mentioned that Australian newspaper revenues would be flat in 1996/97.
Murdoch reported that News Corp's British newspapers were performing well, with increased circulation at The Sunday Times.
News Corp had US$2.5 billion in cash after recent U.S. bond issues.
Murdoch announced plans to fund future expansion from cash flow where possible.
News Corp planned to float its British digital media technology company, Digital Media Services, within two to three weeks.
Digital Media Services would operate in Britain and Israel and produce technology for digital television.

QBE Insurance Group Ltd is based in Australia.
QBE Insurance Group Ltd announced that profit growth for the full 1996/97 year is likely to surge into the high teens.
QBE managing director John Cloney expressed confidence that profit growth will be in the teens, possibly in the high teens.
QBE reported a first quarter net profit of A$28.5 million, a slight increase from A$28.0 million a year earlier.
QBE's full year net profit rose 15.1 percent to A$123.3 million for the year ending June 30, 1996.
Analysts noted that the first quarter result may have been disappointing due to costs associated with a new computer system.
First Pacific insurance analyst Greg Galton stated that a 15 percent profit growth per annum is still favorable.
QBE's share price increased by 15 cents to A$6.70 following Cloney's comments.
Cloney indicated that QBE expects reduced expense ratios in 1996/97 due to improved productivity from new computer systems.
QBE aims for double digit premium growth from existing lines and lower acquisition costs.

Email Ltd reported a lower half year net profit and dividend on Monday.
Email forecasted that recent restructuring and a seasonal lift would boost profits in the second half.
The environment for industrial activities remained difficult according to Email.
Recent economic forecasts have deferred the timing of an upturn in the building sector.
Email reported a pre-abnormal net profit of A$27.26 million for the first half to September 30.
Email's net profit fell to A$23.85 million from A$26.61 million the previous year due to abnormal losses of A$3.41 million.
Email cut its interim dividend to eight cents from 11.5 cents a year earlier.
Email Managing Director John Hanna stated that pre-tax profits for the second half of the 1996/97 year would be above those in the second half of 1995/96.
Analysts noted that the result was within expectations despite the dividend cut.
Email's share price was unchanged at A$3.55 at 1.10 p.m. on light volumes.

Westpac Banking Corp Ltd is expected to report a net profit growth of 10 percent for the 1995/96 year.
The slower profit growth is attributed to an increasingly competitive home loan sector and a slower economy.
Analysts are focused on the impact of increased competition and cuts in home lending margins on Westpac's profits for 1996/97.
Morgan Stanley banking analyst John Hobson stated that the full impact of sliding home loan margins will be seen for the year ending September 1997.
Hobson indicated that there will be a moderating influence on profits that will intensify throughout 1997.
Cautious statements are expected to be made at the briefing following the profit report.
The median forecast in BZW's BARCEPs analyst survey predicts a net profit before abnormals of A$1.12 billion for the year ending September 30, 1996.
This forecast represents an increase of about 10 percent from A$1.02 billion in 1994/95.
The profit growth of 10 percent for 1995/96 is significantly lower than the 44 percent rise recorded between 1993/94 and 1994/95.

British Airways Plc (BA) is unlikely to increase its airfares by the full three percent agreed to by the world's airlines.
BA chairman Sir Colin Marshall made this statement on Monday.
The world's airlines proposed a three percent fare increase due to a 40-percent surge in fuel prices this year.
The proposal was made by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) in Geneva.
Marshall stated that BA was not as severely affected by fuel prices due to the strength of sterling against the U.S. dollar.
He noted that aviation fuel is priced in U.S. dollar terms, making exchange rates important for individual carriers.
Marshall indicated that it is likely BA will not pass on the full three percent increase agreed to in Geneva.
BA had previously increased its prices by about one percent before the Geneva resolution due to the strong currency.
IATA's proposed fare increase is subject to government approvals and would apply to fares from December 15.
Marshall expressed confidence that the European Union would not block BA's plan to form an alliance with American Airlines.

An official inquiry into Australia's financial system was established by the conservative government after its March election.
The inquiry will consider recommending a relaxation of rules that prevent big bank mergers and foreign bank takeovers.
The inquiry outlined various options for reform in a discussion paper without stating its own preferences.
The inquiry noted majority industry support for abolishing rules that stop mergers and foreign bank takeovers.
The inquiry prefers an anti-monopolies system that treats the banking sector the same as other sectors.
The government currently has the final say on bank mergers, rather than the anti-monopolies watchdog.
Analysts expect the inquiry's final report to recommend allowing bank mergers and new foreign investment.
Shares in big banks vulnerable to takeover have increased since the beginning of the year.
Possible takeover targets include Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp Ltd.
The National Australia Bank Ltd is seen as the main predator in potential bank mergers.

Brambles Industries Ltd is a transport equipment hire and logistics firm based in Australia.
Brambles reported a 15.8 percent profit increase for the 1995/96 year.
The profit increase occurred despite flat economies in Australia and Europe.
Profits from Brambles' U.S. and European CHEP pallet hire joint venture with GKN Plc contributed to the profit increase.
Brambles' net profit rose to A$215.1 million for the year ending June 30, up from A$97.7 million in 1994/95.
The previous year's profit was affected by an abnormal loss of $112.3 million.
Stripping away abnormal losses, profit for 1995/96 was A$214.8 million.
Pre-tax profits rose 13 percent from Europe and 30 percent from the United States, while Australian profits rose eight percent.
Brambles plans to look for further acquisitions outside Australia due to strong performance from non-Australian operations.
Brambles expects strong contributions from the United States and Europe to continue offsetting soft conditions in Australia.

AWA Ltd announced its intention to acquire up to 75 percent of the Totalisator Agency Board (TAB), which is owned by the New South Wales government.
The estimated value of the acquisition is around A$750 million.
AWA managing director John Rouse stated that the company is considering a major recapitalisation to fund the acquisition.
AWA is examining the privatisation model used for the Victorian TAB, where the racing industry purchased a 25 percent stake.
Rouse indicated that AWA might raise capital through financial institutions and existing shareholders, with plans to later offer a portion of the stake to the public.
The New South Wales Labor government has not publicly confirmed whether it will privatise the TAB but is expected to announce a plan within several months.
Bidders are seeking assurances from the government regarding the tax and licensing regime for a privatised TAB.
Rouse mentioned that there is a public desire for shares in any privatised NSW TAB to be offered to the public.
Rouse expressed that a trade sale might be preferred over a public float for the privatisation process.
AWA's share price closed at 91 cents, down two cents on Wednesday.

Intellect Holdings Ltd announced its bid for Techway Ltd on Tuesday.
Intellect aims to launch a product for secure Internet payments through the acquisition of Techway.
Intellect has pioneered EFTPOS technology and systems in Australia.
Intellect sells EFTPOS hardware and software to 20 banks outside Australia and five or six large banks in Europe.
All banks are seeking greater service and lower costs through the Internet, according to Intellect executive chairman Ross Leighton.
Finding a secure method for Internet payments is a significant challenge for programmers.
Secure payment systems are expected to increase the volume of financial transactions online.
Techway's Web Australia unit developed the software used for Internet banking by Advance Bank Ltd.
Intellect's takeover offer for Techway is a counter-bid to a previous offer by Nova Pacific Capital Ltd.
The bid values Techway at A$4.9 million and offers one Intellect share for every 2.5 Techway shares.

TNT Ltd reported that it is well positioned for strong profit growth in the 1996/97 year.
TNT Ltd plans to sell its unprofitable non-core assets.
David Mortimer is the Managing Director of TNT Ltd.
Mortimer stated that profit growth should be strong relative to the previous year's position.
TNT's non-core activities that affected earnings in 1995/96 included its general freight business in Australia and its Brazilian operations.
TNT has closed its Less Than Container Load business and sold its Brazilian operations.
Mortimer indicated that other non-core activities would be considered for sale if they do not perform well.
TNT holds a 50 percent interest in Ansett Worldwide, with News Corp Ltd owning the other half.
Mortimer mentioned that Ansett Worldwide's capital base needs restructuring for better access to capital.
Ansett's GD Express operation in Europe has improved over the past year.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corp reported a lower than expected profit for the first half of 1996/97.
News Corp expressed confidence in achieving a 20 percent profit boost for the full year.
Net profits before abnormals increased by 10.3 percent to A$731 million (US$561 million).
Abnormal losses of A$41 million reduced final first half profits to A$690 million from A$702 million a year earlier.
The reported profit was below analyst forecasts of A$735 million to A$775 million.
A Sydney analyst noted disappointment regarding the results.
Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse, described the result as moderate.
News' shares fell 16 cents to A$6.60 after the result but closed at A$6.76.
News Corp had previously stated it expected strong movie and television revenues to increase profits by at least 20 percent in 1996/97.
Operating income from News' Fox Filmed Entertainment unit increased to A$202 million for the first half of 1996/97.

Trans World Airlines Inc. is seeking a new chief executive officer.
Jeffrey Erickson, the current CEO, will leave the company in January.
Erickson has led the company for the past two years.
The departure of Erickson follows the exit of Chief Financial Officer Robert Peiser four months earlier.
Industry analysts believe the speed of finding a new CEO will impact the airline's financial stability.
TWA reported a $14.3 million loss in the third quarter.
The airline's yield, a measure of fares, decreased in the same quarter.
TWA's unions have four seats on the company's board of directors.
The board is expected to select a well-respected airline manager as Erickson's successor.
Higher fuel costs and the crash of Flight 800 have negatively affected TWA's performance.

Security First Network Bank is based in Atlanta and is the world's first Internet bank.
James Mahan III is the Chief Executive Officer of Security First Network Bank.
Security First Network Bank opened its virtual doors a year ago.
Security First plans to open small offices in Atlanta, Cambridge, Massachusetts, and Silicon Valley, California.
James Mahan III believes having a physical presence will help market the bank more effectively.
Security First is one of five banks in the United States that operates directly on the Internet.
Security First can be accessed at www.sfnb.com.
Most customers of Security First have a money market account and a demand deposit account.
Customers can open a checking account with a minimum deposit of $100.
Security First offers electronic bill payment, certificates of deposit, and Visa cards.

William Kerr is the newly appointed chief executive officer of Meredith Corp.
Meredith Corp is beginning to see prices for television stations peak and come down.
William Kerr stated that Meredith Corp could make an acquisition sometime in 1997.
Meredith Corp owns seven television stations and may acquire about five more in the next few years.
Kerr believes it may be easier to make an attractive acquisition in calendar 1997 than in calendar 1996.
Kerr described an attractive acquisition as a VHF network affiliate in the 10th to 40th largest U.S. markets.
Meredith Corp publishes magazines including Better Homes and Gardens and Ladies' Home Journal.
Kerr stated that Meredith Corp will not seek publishing acquisitions but plans to launch new titles.
Family Money magazine is expected to be launched in the first half of 1997.
Publishing currently makes up about 54 percent of Meredith's earnings, while broadcasting makes up about 43 percent.

H&R Block Inc. reported a net loss of $74.1 million for the second quarter ended Oct. 31.
H&R Block's loss per share was 71 cents in the latest quarter.
In the same quarter of 1995, H&R Block reported a loss of $8.3 million, or 8 cents a share.
Revenues for H&R Block increased to $253.4 million from $221.0 million.
H&R Block attributed its losses mainly to its CompuServe unit, which posted a $58 million loss.
H&R Block owns 80.1 percent of CompuServe after selling the rest of the stock in April.
Plans to spin off CompuServe were suspended in August due to poor earnings and projected losses.
Analysts previously advocated for a spinoff of CompuServe, believing it was holding back H&R Block's value.
H&R Block cut its quarterly dividend to 20 cents a share from 32 cents.
H&R Block's president stated that the decision to cut the dividend was prudent due to CompuServe not contributing to profitability.

Retail malls are implementing various strategies to attract customers during the holiday season.
These strategies include free gift wrapping, valet parking, sweepstakes, and private visits with Santa.
Mall operators reported double-digit sales increases on Black Friday.
Robert Michaels is the president of General Growth Properties Inc., which operates 120 retail centers.
Traffic patterns at malls varied, with some reporting close to 10 percent increases and others seeing flat traffic.
Sarah Liddle is the associate marketing director of Newport Centre Mall in Jersey City, N.J.
Liddle noted that shoppers were more willing to buy this year compared to last year.
Billie Scott is a spokeswoman for Simon DeBartolo Group Inc., which owns Newport Centre and has interests in 185 properties.
Scott stated that traffic was at or above last year's levels, but the difference was that people were buying.
Real estate investment trusts (REITs) do not generate as much revenue during the holiday season as retailers.

First Chicago NBD Corp is open to acquisitions to expand its banking network.
First Chicago expects to cut more retail branches over time due to increased electronic banking and supermarket banking.
Verne Istock, chief executive of First Chicago, stated that more brick and mortar branches will be removed as customers use alternative banking channels.
First Chicago does not plan to make drastic cuts to its branches like KeyCorp, which announced the closure or sale of nearly 280 branches.
First Chicago has closed about 25 branches since merging with NBD Bancorp a year ago.
The merger created the ninth largest bank holding company in the United States, with $106.7 billion in assets.
First Chicago is interested in expanding its retail customer base through acquisitions in the greater Midwest.
Istock mentioned that any acquisition could only dilute earnings for a short time, if at all.
First Chicago has not had discussions with Firstar Corp regarding a potential acquisition.
Istock indicated that acquisitions could occur outside of traditional banking as regulatory lines between banking and other financial businesses are erased.

Mercantile Bancorp Inc plans to purchase Roosevelt Financial Group Inc for $1.07 billion.
Analysts consider the purchase price and an expected merger-related charge of $25-$30 million reasonable for an in-market deal.
Mercantile Bancorp Inc is based in St. Louis.
Roosevelt Financial Group Inc is a $9 billion thrift holding company also located in St. Louis.
Roosevelt has 83 branches, 73 of which overlap with Mercantile.
Mercantile expects to eliminate 50 overlapping branches by the middle of 1998.
Mercantile anticipates cutting 37 percent of Roosevelt's pre-tax cost base by 1999.
The $1.07 billion price tag is about 11 times 1997 earnings estimates for Roosevelt.
Mercantile plans to acquire Mark Twain Bancshares Inc for $855 million.
Once both deals close, Mercantile will have $30 billion in assets, making it the largest financial institution in Missouri.

Magna Group Inc. has a definitive agreement to acquire Homeland Bankshares Corp. for about $216 million.
Magna will issue 5 million shares of its common stock and pay $92 million in cash for all outstanding Homeland common shares.
Homeland shareholders can exchange each of their shares for about 1.55 Magna shares, a comparable amount in cash, or a combination of both.
Magna plans to repurchase about 600,000 shares of its stock under its current repurchase plan.
G. Thomas Andes, Magna chairman, stated that they will consider buyback programs beyond the current plan, but nothing has been approved.
Homeland Bankshares Corp. has assets of $1.2 billion and operates four commercial banks and one savings bank in Iowa.
Magna has $5.35 billion in assets and is the third-largest banking institution in the St. Louis metropolitan area.
After the acquisition, Magna would have about 55 percent of its assets in Illinois, 25 percent in Missouri, and 20 percent in Iowa.
The acquisition is subject to approval by Homeland shareholders and regulators.
Magna expects the acquisition to boost earnings within 12 months and save about $8 million through centralization of systems and procedures.

The U.S. economy is expected to show steady growth in 1997, similar to 1996.
Economists for Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp forecast vehicle sales between 15 million and 15.5 million in 1997.
Chrysler Corp's economist predicted vehicle sales of 15.2 million in 1997.
Vehicle sales were approximately 15.4 million in 1996.
The forecasts were presented to the Society of Automotive Analysts.
Chrysler's W. Van Bussmann stated that the market is likely to see more of the same growth.
General Motors' G. Mustafa Mohatarem indicated no significant changes in fiscal or monetary policy.
Ford's Martin Zimmerman expressed optimism about continued growth into 1998.
All three economists expressed concern about the weakening of the yen against the dollar.
Analysts expect the yen to stabilize and strengthen against the dollar this year.

Equity Residential Properties Trust is a real estate investment trust led by Sam Zell.
Equity Residential agreed to buy Wellsford Residential Property Trust in a deal valuing Wellsford at $1 billion.
The acquisition will make Equity Residential the second largest real estate investment trust in any category.
Sam Zell stated that consolidation of the industry is critical for its evolution.
The deal values Wellsford at about $29.61 a share, which is an 18.7 percent premium over its recent stock price.
Equity Residential expects to reduce annual general and administrative expenses by about $3.1 million after the deal closes.
The merger is expected to add 10 cents to 13 cents a share in annualized funds from operation for Equity Residential.
After the deal closes, Equity Residential will own and operate 317 properties with 90,873 units.
The acquisition will add properties in the Pacific Northwest and West Coast, where rental demand is strong.
Equity Residential will exchange each Wellsford share for 0.625 share of Equity Residential and one share of Wellsford Properties Inc.

Intuit Inc launched its new banking system called BankNOW on America Online Inc's online computer system.
Several large banks in the United States have agreed to use Intuit's BankNOW.
BankNOW will be part of America Online's Banking Center, alongside products from CheckFree Corp, Online Resources, and Visa Interactive.
BankNOW is designed for customers who want to conduct online banking transactions without using Intuit's Quicken software.
Fourteen U.S. financial institutions, including First Chicago NBD Corp and CoreStates Financial Corp, are currently using BankNOW.
An additional eight financial institutions have committed to using BankNOW.
Nineteen financial institutions provide banking services on America Online's system.
The BankNOW software can be downloaded for free from America Online.
Financial institutions charge their customers for using BankNOW.
First Chicago will charge $3.95 a month for online banking and $9.95 a month for online banking and bill paying.

Mercury Finance Co.'s agreement to buy a consumer finance business was terminated after the company reported inflated earnings due to phony bookkeeping entries.
Mercury Finance Co. fired its chief accountant in connection with the inflated earnings.
The officer responsible for the overstated earnings may be cooperating with federal authorities.
BankBoston Corp. terminated its agreement to sell its Fidelity Acceptance Corp. unit to Mercury Finance for 32.7 million shares of Mercury stock.
When the deal was announced, the stock was valued at approximately $458 million.
Mercury Finance stock closed at $14.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday and has not traded since.
Traders reported that Mercury Finance stock was changing hands at $4.25 overseas, valuing the 32.7 million shares at about $139 million.
BankBoston stated that recent events regarding Mercury Finance constituted a breach of their agreement.
Analysts indicated that BankBoston would likely find another buyer for Fidelity Acceptance Corp.
Mercury Finance announced that its 1996 earnings would be restated to $56.7 million from $120.7 million.

Bob Dylan's song 'The Times They Are a-Changin' is being used in a commercial for the Bank of Montreal.
The Bank of Montreal is the third biggest bank in Canada.
The commercial features children running in nature while a choir sings Dylan's song.
The commercial concludes with the Bank of Montreal logo and an announcement date of October 16.
Some fans of Bob Dylan are upset that the bank is using a protest song for commercial purposes.
George Bothwell, a senior vice-president at the bank, stated that Dylan's lyrics reflect the bank's need to change.
Listeners on a Toronto radio show expressed outrage over the ad campaign.
One female caller criticized the bank for misunderstanding the spirit of the song.
Dylan still owns the copyright to the song but did not provide a comment on the commercial.
Some younger listeners suggested that baby boomers have compromised their ideals.

Jimmy Kemp is the youngest son of Jack Kemp.
Jimmy Kemp plays as a quarterback for the Saskatchewan Roughriders in Canada.
Jimmy Kemp prefers to be known for his own identity rather than as Jack Kemp's son.
Jimmy Kemp is 25 years old.
He is finishing his third year in the Canadian Football League.
Jimmy Kemp was traded to the Saskatchewan Roughriders after playing for the Montreal Alouettes and the San Antonio Texans.
The local press in Regina has kept Jimmy Kemp's connection to his father private.
Before joining the Roughriders, Jimmy Kemp considered quitting football to help with his father's campaign.
Jack Kemp encouraged his son to continue playing football.
Jimmy Kemp had a successful game where he passed for three touchdowns against Hamilton.

Anti-government protests occurred in Toronto on Friday.
Demonstrators shut down the transit system and disrupted businesses.
Protesters attempted to break into the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Thousands of union workers, civil servants, and citizens participated in the protests.
Over 1 million commuters stayed at home or used alternative transportation due to the shutdown of subway and bus services.
City officials announced that transit services would resume early Saturday.
Commuter trains and service at Pearson Airport were not disrupted.
Toronto police reported no major acts of violence, though some arrests were made for misconduct.
The protests were organized by labour unions in response to budget cuts by Ontario's Conservative government.
Some critics claimed the protest did not succeed in shutting down the city.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Index reached its 50th record close of 1996 on Thursday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 8.01 points to close at 5598.82.
The TSE 300 Composite Index surpassed a streak of 45 record finishes in 1987.
The Index set an intraday high of 5601.88.
Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president and director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc, stated that this record would not be the last.
Toronto's record-setting run was led by banking, communications, conglomerates, and technology issues.
Of the TSE's 14 sub-groups, 10 finished higher.
The rally was restrained by a 162-point loss in golds.
113.8 million shares exchanged hands for a value of C$1.6 billion.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 538 to 434 with 294 issues unchanged.

Fidelity Investments announced that Canadian regulators are investigating trades made by Veronika Hirsch.
Veronika Hirsch is the manager of Fidelity's new Canadian equity fund.
Hirsch's promotional road show for Fidelity's True North fund has been postponed due to the regulatory review.
The road show was scheduled to begin on Monday.
A spokesman for Fidelity's Canadian subsidiary stated that Hirsch was contacted by a regulatory agency regarding her personal investments before joining Fidelity.
The British Columbia Securities Commission is reportedly looking into the matter.
Hirsch previously worked as a fund manager at AGF Management Ltd. in Toronto.
