During her time at AGF, Hirsch purchased 65,000 special warrants of Oliver Gold Corp. through a private placement.
Hirsch paid C$1.53 per warrant for the Oliver Gold shares.
The AGF Growth & Income Fund, managed by Hirsch, later bought 295,000 special warrants at a price of C$3.60 per warrant.

Toronto stocks reached new highs on Wednesday due to increased foreign investment in Canada's financial markets.
Falling interest rates and a recovering economy attracted foreign investors to Canada.
Shares in Canada's big six banks hit 52-week highs on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The Toronto Stock Exchange achieved its 53rd record close of 1996.
The Canadian dollar reached its strongest level in a year this week.
Economists noted that declining interest rates, low inflation, and falling budget deficits have made Canada attractive to investors.
Michael Gregory, an economist with Lehman Brothers, stated that foreign investors are increasingly interested in Canada as an investment destination.
The Toronto Stock Exchange index of 300 stocks increased by 85.45 points to close at 5,749.92.
The index has gained over 20 percent this year, outperforming the Dow Jones industrial average and the Standard & Poor's 500 index.
The Bank of Canada is anticipated to cut interest rates again soon, having already cut rates 19 times since May 1995.

Two major shareholders in Canada's Altamira Management Ltd. have set a mid-December deadline to resume court action against a C$660 million takeover bid by Manufacturers Life Insurance Co. Ltd.
Rick Leckner is a spokesman for Almiria Capital Corp., which owns 30.5 percent of Altamira.
Leckner stated that the preference is to resolve the dispute quickly, but a court battle may be necessary if negotiations fail.
Manufacturers Life Insurance Co. Ltd. has offered C$32 a share for Altamira, which is Canada's 12th-largest mutual fund company.
T.A. Associates Inc. has launched a rival bid of C$38 a share, or C$767 million, for Altamira.
Manufacturers Life Insurance Co. Ltd. already owns 30.5 percent of Altamira and has support from a group of 40 Altamira fund managers who are shareholders.
The bid from Manufacturers Life is opposed by Almiria and a group led by Altamira Chairman Ron Meade, which holds about 11 percent of Altamira.
A lawsuit launched by Almiria and Meade's group was scheduled to proceed in an Ontario court, but the parties agreed to negotiate a settlement.
Negotiation talks have not yet begun as of Thursday, and court action is set to resume on December 18.
T.A. Associates is one of the largest private equity investors in the United States.

Bank of Montreal is Canada's third biggest bank.
The bank reported annual profits exceeding C$1 billion ($750 million).
Net income for the year ended Oct. 31 increased by 18.4 percent to C$1.17 billion ($873 million).
The bank's return on equity rose to 17 percent from 15.4 percent the previous year.
Chairman Matthew Barrett stated that the results represent the seventh consecutive year of record earnings.
Bank of Montreal is the third bank to surpass the C$1 billion profit threshold in recent years.
The bank attributed its record earnings to higher fees, volume growth, and the acquisition of a 16 percent stake in Grupo Financiero Bancomer SA de CV.
In fiscal 1996, approximately 47 percent of the bank's total income came from operations outside of Canada.
Net income from U.S. operations rose 6 percent to C$390 million ($291 million).
Earnings from Mexico increased by 4 percent to C$57 million ($42 million).

Royal Bank of Canada is Canada's biggest bank.
Royal Bank of Canada reported a net income of C$1.43 billion for the year ended Oct. 31, 1996.
This net income increased from C$1.26 billion in 1995.
Royal Bank of Canada raised its quarterly dividend by C3 cents to C37 cents a share.
This was the third dividend increase in the past 15 months.
Royal Bank of Canada was the third Canadian bank to raise its dividend during the current earnings reporting season.
Royal Bank of Canada was the fourth of Canada's Big Six banks to report a third consecutive year of record profits.
The provision for credit losses fell to C$440 million in 1996.
Return on equity rose to 17.6 percent in 1996.
Royal Bank of Canada's fourth-quarter earnings were C$1.09 a share, up from C90 cents in the same period in 1995.

Profits at Canada's six big banks exceeded C$6 billion ($4.4 billion) in 1996.
The combined profit of the six banks was C$6.26 billion ($4.6 billion) for the fiscal year ending October 31, 1996.
The profits in 1996 surpassed the previous year's record of C$5.2 billion ($3.8 billion).
CIBC reported a 35 percent increase in net income, reaching C$1.36 billion ($1 billion) in fiscal 1996.
CIBC increased its quarterly dividend by C5 cents (3.6 cents) to C50 cents (37 cents) in 1996.
Royal Bank reported a net income of C$1.43 billion ($1.05 billion) in 1996, marking the highest corporate profit in Canadian history.
Bank of Nova Scotia and Bank of Montreal both reported net incomes exceeding C$1 billion in 1996.
National Bank reported a 30 percent increase in net income to C$318 million ($234 million) in 1996.
The banks attributed their strong performance to lower credit losses and robust commercial and personal banking.
CIBC's Wood Gundy Inc. investment arm reported a 122 percent increase in earnings to C$528 million ($389 million) in 1996.

Shares in Laidlaw Inc, a Canadian waste and transportation firm, increased on Tuesday.
Investors and analysts praised Laidlaw's major moves in ambulance services and waste management worth over $2 billion.
Laidlaw's stock reached new heights on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
CEO James Bullock stated that the company is positioned for strong growth following two significant deals announced after the market closed on Monday.
Laidlaw plans to acquire American Medical Response Inc for $1.12 billion in cash and merge it with its MedTrans ambulance services unit.
Laidlaw signed a letter of intent to sell its Environmental Services unit for $1 billion to Rollins Environmental Services Inc.
Laidlaw will own 66 percent of the new combined company, Laidlaw Environmental Services Inc.
Laidlaw Environmental Services Inc will be a dominant player in North American hazardous waste management.
Laidlaw completed the $1.65 billion sale of its solid waste management business to Allied Waste Industries Inc a few weeks prior.
Laidlaw's class B stock closed at a 52-week high of C$18 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Veronika Hirsch, a Canadian stock picker, left Fidelity Investments on Tuesday.
Fidelity spokesman Chethan Lakshman stated that the company wishes Hirsch well in her future endeavors.
Hirsch was hired by Fidelity last summer to lead its efforts in the Canadian market.
Hirsch was removed from her portfolio in November due to controversy over personal trades made before joining Fidelity.
Hirsch's lawyer, Tom Lockwood, mentioned that she is considering options including offers for public speaking or writing a book.
Hirsch purchased 65,000 special warrants of Oliver Gold through a private placement while at AGF Management Ltd.
Shortly after Hirsch's purchase, her AGF Growth & Income Fund bought 295,000 special warrants of Oliver Gold at a higher price.
Fidelity removed Hirsch from her True North Equity Fund after Canadian securities regulators confirmed an investigation into her personal investments.
Hirsch was previously the focus of a multi-million dollar advertising campaign at AGF, making her a prominent fund manager in Canada.
Fidelity ranks ninth in Canada with C$8.2 billion in assets, while Canadians have over C$211 billion in mutual funds.

Canada's major banks are seeking tax relief from Finance Minister Paul Martin.
Last year, Paul Martin rejected the banks' request for expanded powers in insurance.
Paul Martin extended a capital tax on the banks for another year.
Bankers argue that they face one of the heaviest tax burdens in corporate Canada.
Mark Weseluck is the vice-president of banking operations for the Canadian Bankers Association.
The Big Six banks in Canada include Royal Bank of Canada, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, Bank of Montreal, Bank of Nova Scotia, Toronto-Dominion Bank, and National Bank of Canada.
The Big Six banks earned a combined C$6.26 billion in 1996, a 21 percent increase from the previous year.
The banks paid record taxes of more than C$5.5 billion in 1996.
The Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives proposed an 'excess profits' tax on banks totaling C$496 million for 1997/98.
The Ontario government imposed a 10 percent capital tax surcharge on the banks in last spring's budget.

The strike against General Motors in Canada is entering its second week.
Analysts predict that GM's losses will increase as its U.S. plants are forced to shut down.
The Canadian Auto Workers union's walkout will expand to two key components plants in Windsor, Ontario.
The shutdowns of GM's U.S. assembly plants could begin by early next week.
GM's core North American automotive business could be significantly affected if the strike is not resolved within two weeks.
Wesley Brown, an analyst at CSM Forecasting, stated that shutting assembly plants leads to rapid shutdowns of other plants.
The Cadillac luxury car plant in Hamtramck, Mich., is expected to be one of the first affected.
The Oklahoma City plant is launching two new mid-size sedans, the 1997 Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass.
GM is also launching a new Pontiac Grand Prix sedan and three new minivans.
Analysts believe the Canadian strike will disrupt production and marketing launches, benefiting competitors like Chrysler and Ford.

Ford Motor Co. will pay $40 million for naming rights to the future home of the Detroit Lions.
The new stadium will be built in downtown Detroit and will have a capacity of 70,000 seats.
The total cost of the stadium project is $225 million.
The stadium will host the Detroit Lions, other athletic events, entertainment events, and conventions.
The stadium will be located adjacent to a new $240 million open air ballpark for the Detroit Tigers.
Ford has not yet chosen a formal name for the stadium.
The deal leaves stadium backers about $10 million short of their fundraising goals.
Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer expressed confidence in meeting funding conditions before the Nov. 1 deadline.
Detroit area voters will vote on Nov. 5 to approve new taxes to help finance the project.
William Clay Ford Jr. stated that he and his father did not participate in board discussions regarding the deal.

Chrysler Corp. plans to increase its annual production capacity to over 4 million vehicles.
Chrysler aims to capture 20 percent of the U.S. car and truck market.
Chrysler's top executives believe they can improve financial performance through cost cuts, engineering innovations, new products, and other initiatives.
Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton stated that an 18 percent to 20 percent market share is achievable.
Chrysler held a 16.2 percent market share during the first nine months of 1996.
Chrysler's management is focusing on long-term growth after rebuilding its product line and operations following financial crises in 1980 and 1991.
Chrysler President Bob Lutz stated that the company no longer needs to worry about its future.
Eaton believes Chrysler can remain profitable even with a 10 percent to 20 percent drop in production.
Chrysler plans to increase its production capacity to 3.765 million vehicles by the year 2000.
Chrysler is working on a new Dodge sport utility vehicle expected to be called the Dodge Durango.

The United Auto Workers union is discussing a potential five- or six-year contract with major automakers.
The union is open to a longer contract if it includes significant job security guarantees.
Carl Dowell is the president of UAW Local 862 in Louisville, Kentucky.
Contract negotiations with General Motors Corp., Ford Motor Co., and Chrysler Corp. resumed on Monday.
UAW President Stephen Yokich met with the automakers' chairmen last week.
The UAW has not yet selected a company for a pattern agreement.
Yokich delayed the selection of a strike target to facilitate negotiations with all three companies.
No decision on a target company is expected this week.
The current contract covering about 400,000 U.S. hourly workers expires on September 14.
Ford suggested negotiating a longer-term contract to stabilize future costs.

The United Auto Workers union set a Sunday night deadline for a strike against General Motors Corp.
UAW President Stephen Yokich stated that union negotiators were not optimistic about reaching a new contract deal by the deadline.
The deadline for the contract agreement is 11:59 p.m. EST Sunday.
The UAW has notified GM that it will terminate its extended 1993 contract if no agreement is reached by the deadline.
The UAW typically does not work without a contract.
UAW members have been advised to continue working unless notified otherwise by their local union.
The UAW bargaining team will continue efforts to achieve a new agreement.
GM recently settled a 20-day strike with the Canadian Auto Workers union.
UAW negotiations with GM are at odds over employment guarantees and GM's desire for flexibility in parts work.
Ford Motor Co. and Chrysler Corp. have agreed to guarantee jobs for 95 percent of their current workforces over the next three years.

Negotiators for General Motors Corp. and the United Auto Workers adjourned their talks on Saturday evening.
There are less than 30 hours remaining before a midnight Sunday strike deadline.
UAW President Stephen Yokich led the bargaining team.
The union announced it will cancel its contract with GM at 11:59 p.m. EST Sunday.
GM spokesman Charles Licari did not comment on the progress of the talks.
The negotiations aim to establish a new national labor agreement for GM's 215,000 UAW workers.
This is the first time the UAW has threatened a strike in its 1996 negotiations with Detroit's Big Three automakers.
The UAW's negotiations have been characterized by a conciliatory tone and secretive discussions.
Two days prior, GM's 26,000 Canadian Auto Workers members returned to work after a three-week strike.
The UAW's demands include job security, while GM seeks to maintain flexibility in outsourcing.

General Motors Co. and the United Auto Workers recessed contract negotiations early Monday after their existing contract expired.
Union officials indicated that talks were likely to resume later in the day.
UAW President Stephen Yokich stated that union members continued working despite the impasse.
Bargaining between GM and the UAW recessed around 3 a.m. EST after the contract expired.
The existing contract covers 215,000 UAW members working at GM's U.S. facilities.
Yokich did not mention possible selective strikes at GM plants during a news conference.
Negotiators talked for about 17 hours on Sunday and early Monday morning.
GM vice president of personnel Gerald Knechtel described the talks as constructive and stated that significant progress had been made.
The UAW has reached a new three-year contract with Ford Motor Co. and Chrysler Corp. covering about 171,000 UAW members in the United States.
The UAW is facing challenges in forcing GM to accept job guarantee patterns similar to those agreed upon by Ford and Chrysler.

The United Auto Workers union initiated two local strikes against General Motors Corp.'s truck operations.
About 2,750 members of UAW Local 23 struck at GM's Indianapolis metal stamping plant at approximately 6 p.m. EST.
An hour later, 4,800 workers struck at GM's Janesville, Wisconsin, truck assembly plant.
The strikes could disrupt much of GM's light truck production, which is a significant source of profits for the company.
The Janesville plant manufactures the Chevrolet Tahoe, Suburban, and GMC Yukon sport utility vehicles.
The Indianapolis plant provides doors, fenders, hoods, and other sheet-metal stampings to nine North American truck assembly plants.
GM spokesman Jerry Holmes stated that the automaker had no formal response to the strikes but confirmed that negotiations were ongoing.
UAW President Stephen Yokich indicated that local strikes were a possibility after negotiations over the weekend did not yield an agreement.
The expiration of GM's national contract covering 215,000 UAW workers allowed local unions to strike for local issues.
UAW regional director Ron Gettelfinger stated that the Indianapolis strike was called to address local issues.

Local strikes in Wisconsin and Indiana are impacting General Motors Corp. truck operations.
The walkout at GM's Indianapolis metal stamping plant began on Tuesday night.
The strike forced GM to lay off 2,250 workers at its Fort Wayne, Indiana plant.
Production of full-size Chevrolet and GMC pickup trucks has been halted due to the strike.
The Indianapolis plant supplies major body panels that are essential for truck production.
The strike has stopped shipments to nine of GM's eleven North American truck assembly plants.
Negotiations between GM and the United Auto Workers union are ongoing.
The strikes involve 2,750 workers in Indianapolis and 4,800 workers at the Janesville, Wisconsin plant.
The shutdown of the Janesville plant could cost GM $50 million a week in pre-tax profits.
GM makes approximately $9,000 in variable profits on each truck produced.

General Motors Corp. and the United Auto Workers union did not reach a national contract deal after nearly 32 hours of talks.
GM spokesman Charles Licari stated that talks in specific areas would continue Thursday night.
Full negotiations are scheduled to resume Friday morning.
Harley Shaiken, a professor of labor relations at the University of California-Berkeley, noted that talks have faced several setbacks in the past week.
The pressure on negotiations has increased due to two plants currently on strike.
Local union officials reported that nearly 21,000 workers could be idled by strikes in Indianapolis and Janesville, Wisconsin, by Saturday.
GM truck plants in Moraine, Ohio, and Flint, Michigan, are expected to run out of parts from the Indianapolis stamping plant by late Thursday night.
Flint employs about 2,000 workers and produces crew-cab and heavy-duty full-size pickup trucks.
Moraine employs about 4,000 workers and produces Chevrolet Blazer and GMC Jimmy compact sport utility vehicles.
GM's Shreveport, Louisiana, compact pickup truck plant is scheduled to shut down Friday, affecting 2,500 workers.

General Motors Corp. experienced production losses due to strikes.
The United Auto Workers (UAW) canceled a Saturday meeting of plant-level leaders.
The UAW's National GM Council, consisting of 250 members, is scheduled to meet on November 6 in Chicago.
The UAW is negotiating a tentative agreement covering 215,000 GM workers.
The cancellation of the meeting is viewed as a negative sign for labor contract talks.
Local strikes in Indiana and Wisconsin have idled over 19,000 workers.
2,750 workers struck at GM's Indianapolis metal stamping plant.
4,809 workers struck at the Janesville, Wisconsin, truck assembly plant.
GM's Shreveport, Louisiana, compact pickup truck plant shut down, idling 2,400 workers.
GM's Linden, New Jersey, plant was expected to run out of parts on Friday night.

Investors pushed General Motors Corp. shares higher on Monday.
General Motors signed a new national labour agreement with the United Auto Workers union.
GM's shares traded up $1.50 at $55.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The agreement allows GM to reduce its hourly workforce by 30,000 or more over the next three years.
The pact contains a nominal guarantee for GM to maintain employment of about 95 percent of its current workforce.
The agreement allows GM to exit unprofitable parts businesses and sell certain components plants.
David Cole believes the pact will help GM boost efficiency.
A strike at GM's Janesville, Wisconsin truck assembly plant involves 4,809 workers.
UAW Local 95 demands that GM hire more workers in Janesville.
UAW Local 23 members returned to work at a metal stamping plant in Indianapolis after ratifying a new local contract.

Imperial Tobacco Group will split from Hanson Plc on October 1.
Imperial Tobacco Group is Britain's second-biggest tobacco firm after B.A.T Industries.
Imperial Tobacco Group's brands include Embassy, John Player Special, Superkings cigarettes, Panama, and Castella cigars.
Hanson Plc has reduced Imperial's brands from 150 to 33 and increased productivity by 195 percent since acquiring it 10 years ago.
Imperial's profits in 1995 were 348 million pounds on 3.6 billion pounds of sales.
Analysts are concerned that Imperial's shares may struggle once listed in London due to litigation threats against tobacco firms.
Tobacco stocks have recently been affected by litigation and regulatory changes in the United States.
Analysts believe that the litigation threat could impact Imperial's attractiveness as a takeover candidate.
Britain accounts for 87 percent of Imperial's profits.
Gareth Davis, Imperial's chief executive, stated that the company aims to increase exports to Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.

Wickes Plc is a British Do-It-Yourself retailer.
Wickes Plc reported a 51 million pounds write-off for which its ex-chairman accepted responsibility.
The accounting irregularities resulted in profits being overstated by 51 million pounds over recent years.
The restatement of accounts will reduce operating profit by 26 million pounds for 1995, 14 million pounds for 1994, and 11 million pounds for earlier years.
Profits for 1995 will also be affected by a two million pounds charge against shareholder funds related to European businesses and a 10 million pounds charge from property interests.
Finance director Bill Hoskins expects another one-off charge against 1996 results related to restructuring and investigation costs.
Hoskins estimated this additional charge to be around 10 million pounds.
Wickes Plc will undergo a refinancing rights issue, with 30 million pounds considered a good starting point to reduce its debt-to-equity ratio.
New chairman Michael von Brentano stated that former chairman Henry Sweetbaum accepted ultimate responsibility and will repay his 1.2 million pounds in bonus payments.
Former finance director Trefor Llewellyn has agreed to repay his 485,000 pounds bonus for 1995.

AMEC Plc is exploring a possible investment in Spie Batignolle's electrical and construction businesses.
The aim of the investment is to widen AMEC's international exposure.
AMEC is in talks with Spie management about taking a minority stake that could be raised to a majority stake.
The current parent group of Spie is Schneider SA.
If the deal is completed, it would create a major European player with around five billion pounds in sales.
The sales distribution would be 40 percent in Britain, 30 percent in France, and the rest worldwide.
Peter Mason is the chief executive of AMEC.
Mason stated that there is little overlap between AMEC and Spie.
Mason acknowledged that the market conditions in France are tough but believes AMEC is 'buying at the bottom'.
The new deal could allow AMEC to enter new markets including oil and gas and pharmaceuticals.

Wolseley Plc reported a one percent decrease in year pretax profits.
Pretax profits for the year ended July 31 fell to 242.9 million pounds from 245.4 million pounds.
Sales increased to 4.31 billion pounds from 3.78 billion pounds.
The dividend was raised to 10.35 pence from 9.80 pence.
Wolseley has 50 percent of its sales in the U.S.
Chairman Richard Ireland attributed lower profits to poor economic conditions in mainland Europe and volatile lumber prices in the U.S.
Chief financial controller Stephen Webster stated he does not foresee an upturn in the next 12 months in France, Austria, or Germany.
Webster noted that the UK market showed signs of recovery in home repair and maintenance spending.
Webster expressed concern about the potential impact of an interest rate hike in the U.S.
Wolseley's shares were down 13 pence at 494 by 1045 GMT.

Millennium Chemicals will be spun off from Hanson conglomerate in October.
William Landuyt is the chief executive and chairman of Millennium Chemicals.
Millennium Chemicals had sales of two billion pounds and profits of 588 million pounds in 1995.
Landuyt stated that Millennium is a growth company and not a dividend yield stock.
The demerger of Hanson Plc will create four companies: Millennium, Imperial Tobacco, Energy Group, and a building firm retaining the Hanson name.
There has been takeover interest in all four companies being spun off from Hanson.
Millennium received approaches for its three units: Quantum, SCM, and Glidco, all of which were rebuffed.
Hanson's chemicals arm was considered a potential takeover candidate by analysts.
Millennium has implemented a 'poison pill' strategy to deter potential takeover attempts.
Hanson's group share price was downgraded by analysts following the revelation of the poison pill.

Imperial Tobacco Group Plc demerged from Hanson Plc in October.
Imperial Tobacco Group Plc aims to reduce debt levels while investing in export growth.
Gareth Davis is the chief executive of Imperial Tobacco Group Plc.
Davis stated that the company can reduce debt and invest in growth simultaneously due to strong cash generation.
Imperial Tobacco is in discussions with a Japanese company to enter the Japanese market.
The company has inherited approximately 1.1 billion pounds ($1.8 billion) of debt from the Hanson family break-up.
Davis indicated that the debt does not hinder plans for distribution deals or joint ventures in overseas cigarette markets.
Imperial Tobacco may consider small acquisitions in the fragmented cigar market.
Davis is open to raising debt levels for significant acquisition opportunities but prioritizes reducing debt.
Imperial Tobacco plans to report its first results since the demerger on December 5.

Imperial Tobacco Plc outlined its export growth strategy this week.
The company's share price has decreased by 17 percent since its Oct 1 demerger from Hanson Plc.
Gareth Davis is the chief executive of Imperial Tobacco Plc and graduated from Sheffield University in 1972.
Davis stated that investors should not underestimate his determination to expand exports quickly.
Imperial Tobacco was a late entrant to international markets due to the need to reduce costs.
Under Hanson's ownership, Imperial became one of the most efficient players in its sector, with productivity increasing by 195 percent over ten years.
Davis projects that Imperial will continue to grow by eight to nine percent over the next four years.
Imperial's profits are largely derived from a declining British market, accounting for 85 percent of its profits.
Analysts have expressed concerns about how Imperial can invest in export growth while managing its 1.1 billion pounds ($1.8 billion) in debt.
Natwest Markets and Credit Lyonnais issued sell notes on Imperial this month, while SBC Warburg deemed it undervalued.

The British government announced that the design of Eurotunnel's freight trains will be scrutinized following a fire in one of its main tunnels.
The fire injured eight people and caused significant damage.
British transport secretary Sir George Young stated that the Anglo-French Channel Tunnel Safety Authority would review the design aspects of the trains.
Changes to the design of Eurotunnel carriages could impose additional costs on the company, which recently restructured its nine billion pounds in debt.
The fire was the first serious incident since the tunnel opened two years ago and halted services on Tuesday.
Eurotunnel warned that traffic capacity would be reduced to one third of normal levels for an indefinite period, even if limited services resume on Wednesday.
Eurotunnel shares fell in London and Paris following the fire and concerns about safety and damage.
TNT Express Worldwide, a freight customer, indicated it would rely more on ferries due to the fire.
Fifteen heavy goods vehicles and the rear locomotive sustained severe damage in the fire.
The fire reportedly started in a goods carriage carrying flammable polystyrene, but the cause has not been determined.

Eurotunnel faced financial pressure due to a fire in a main tunnel.
The fire caused damage, halted services, and affected consumer confidence.
Eurotunnel recently restructured nine billion pounds ($15 billion) of debt.
One of Eurotunnel's two rail tunnels remains shut pending a safety review.
Analysts noted a modest fall in Eurotunnel shares following the fire.
Eurotunnel warned of reduced services for weeks due to repair work.
The cost of repairs may exceed initial estimates, potentially reaching millions of pounds.
Eurotunnel is losing revenues at a rate of one million pounds a day while the tunnel is shut.
A Eurotunnel spokesman stated that repair costs should be covered by insurance.
Eurotunnel had approximately 45 percent of the cross-Channel ferry market before the fire.

Christian Salvesen rejected a 1.1 billion pound hostile takeover from Hays.
Christian Salvesen stated that its special dividend and power unit demerger provide better shareholder value.
Chris Masters is the chief executive of Christian Salvesen.
Chris Masters expressed that the demerger plan is more in the interests of shareholders.
The special dividend and demerger plan for the Aggreko hire business is valued at 150 million pounds.
The rejected bid from Hays was 390 pence per share.
The plan to spin off Aggreko is part of a six-year restructuring strategy.
A review to enhance shareholder value was already in progress before the Hays bid.
The board's chosen path is financially advantageous in tax terms.
Aggreko operates in 20 countries and is a global market leader.

Stagecoach is a British bus and rail group.
Stagecoach's share price has grown fivefold in three years.
Stagecoach reported a 127 percent rise in first-half profits.
Stagecoach's half-year pre-tax profits reached 47 million pounds ($79 million).
The half-year dividend for Stagecoach rose 43 percent to 3 pence (5 cents) per share.
Stagecoach's group revenues increased to 405 million pounds ($679.0 million) from 198.8 million pounds ($333.3 million).
Chairman Brian Souter described the results as excellent.
Stagecoach shares rose to 629 ($10.54) by 1350 GMT (8:50 a.m. EST).
UBS analyst Richard Hannah stated that profits were two million ($3.4 million) above expectations.
Stagecoach's results were the first since acquiring Porterbrook and Swebus.

Richard Branson's Virgin Group secured a British rail franchise on Friday.
Virgin Group plans to invest an additional 250 million pounds ($420 million) in new trains and services.
Virgin Group won control of the CrossCountry service, which operates over 130 stations from Birmingham.
Virgin Group has 842 employees and reported passenger revenues of 108 million pounds ($181.3 million) for the year ending in March.
The national rail network in the UK is undergoing privatisation.
Will Whitehorn, director of Virgin Rail, stated that the company plans to purchase a new fleet with the 250 million pounds investment.
The order for new rolling stock is expected to be placed next year, with deliveries starting in 2002.
The government subsidy for the first year of the 15-year franchise will be 112.9 million pounds ($189.6 million).
The initial subsidy has been reduced from 127 million pounds ($213.2 million) in 1996/97 and will average 36.4 million pounds ($61.1 million) over the franchise term.
Virgin Rail will refurbish HST 125 diesel trains and aims to increase train miles by 14 percent between May 1998 and 2002.

LucasVarity Plc was formed in September from the merger of Lucas Industries of Britain and Varity Corp. of Buffalo, N.Y.
LucasVarity announced a major restructuring that includes the planned disposal of 13 non-core businesses.
The company plans to eliminate 3,000 jobs over the next two years.
LucasVarity identified additional moves that will result in an extra 120 million British pounds ($200 million) in profit benefits.
The company will take an extra one-time charge of 130 million pounds ($217 million), mainly in non-cash items.
LucasVarity has already planned for 120 million pounds ($200 million) in charges for this year.
Thirteen companies were identified for sale in a post-merger review, with eight named in the restructuring announcement.
The identified companies for sale are small businesses located in Britain, Argentina, and South Africa.
Chief Executive Victor Rice stated that major businesses like aerospace and electronics are not among the unnamed five companies for sale.
LucasVarity is involved in the design, manufacture, and supply of systems, products, and services in the automotive, diesel engine, aftermarket, and aerospace industries.

Cascade Communications Corp's earnings for the third quarter ended September were $0.21 per share.
Cascade's earnings exceeded analysts' consensus estimate by $0.02 per share.
Cascade's earnings growth year-on-year was approximately 200 percent.
Investors sold Cascade's stock after-hours, resulting in a decline of 6.5 points to 80.
Securities analysts noted disappointment in Cascade's sequential quarterly earnings growth.
Joe Noel, an analyst at Hambrecht, stated that Cascade needed $0.04 per share on the upside to maintain its stock price.
Cascade's sequential growth in the most recent third quarter was only 17 percent.
Cascade had reported above 20 percent sequential growth in quarterly earnings since June 1995.
Daniel Smith, Cascade's CEO, stated there were no issues in the company's business fundamentals.
Cascade derived between 10 and 15 percent of its overall revenues from ATM products introduced earlier in the year.

Computer Associates International Inc will focus more resources on its midrange software business.
Computer Associates International Inc will reduce its reliance on mainframe software sales.
CA President Sanjay Kurmar expects a charge in the $500 million range related to the planned acquisition of Cheyenne Software Inc.
The charge will be taken in the quarter ending in December.
Kumar stated that the company's international sales growth had slowed in the quarter ended in September.
The acquisition of Cheyenne Software Inc is likely to be accounted for as an asset purchase.
The acquisition will include a one-time writedown for research and development costs.
Kumar confirmed comments made in a meeting with Wall Street analysts.
Analysts reported that the news of the revenue transition and slowing international sales caused a sharp drop in the company's stock.
The stock decline occurred despite the announcement of fiscal second-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street expectations.

Computer Associates International Inc will unveil a new Internet business unit on Monday.
The new business unit will provide hosting and management of corporate Web sites.
The announcement will occur during the CA World conference in New Orleans.
Computer Associates has scheduled press events with Microsoft Corp, Intel Corp, and Tandem Computers Inc.
Bill Gates, chairman of Microsoft, will deliver a keynote speech on Tuesday evening.
Computer Associates declined to comment on the new Internet business unit.
The new Internet unit aims to help customers create dynamic Web sites linked to internal corporate databases.
Computer Associates plans to offer electronic commerce capabilities in exchange for a revenue-sharing arrangement.
Customers will receive turn-key systems for establishing a business presence on the Web.
Basic pricing plans for the services will start at $5,000 to $20,000.

MCI Communications Corp. reached a 10-year deal with NextWave Telecom Inc.
The deal positions MCI among the top U.S. wireless communications providers.
MCI will connect its network to a system planned by NextWave for personal communications services.
The agreement allows MCI to offer service to over 110 million individuals in 63 areas.
MCI will purchase at least 10 billion minutes of capacity from NextWave over the 10 years.
NextWave was the largest bidder in the U.S. Federal Communications Commission's auctions for 'C-band' wireless radio spectrum.
NextWave plans to sell stock to the public.
The deal enables MCI to expand into the market for wireless personal communications services.
MCI previously dropped out of U.S. PCS license auctions due to high bidding costs.
NextWave selected MCI to provide telecommunications and other services for its personal communications services system.

America Online Inc unveiled a strategy to transform into a mass media company.
AOL introduced a flat-rate Internet pricing option as part of a restructuring plan.
AOL hired Robert Pittman to head its flagship online service.
AOL plans to take $460 million in charges for accounting changes.
AOL shares rose to 25-5/8 in late trading on the announcement.
Gary Arlen stated that the market is responding to financial announcements.
Steve Case expects AOL to surpass 10 million subscriptions by late 1997.
Pittman aims to shift AOL's business model towards advertising and online merchandising.
AOL plans to discontinue its GNN Internet service as part of its new strategy.

Ingram Micro Inc. is set to hold its initial public offering on Wall Street on Thursday.
There have been last-minute delays for Ingram Micro's IPO, including management changes.
Manish Shah is the editor and publisher of the IPO Maven.
The estimated price for Ingram's 20 million share offering was increased to $17 to $19 a share.
Morgan Stanley is the underwriter for Ingram Micro's IPO.
Ingram Micro is based in Santa Ana, California.
Ingram Micro is the world's leading distributor of computer hardware, software, and networking equipment.
Ingram Micro's revenues are expected to reach roughly $10 billion this year.
Merisel Inc. has expected revenues of $6 billion, and Tech Data Corp. has expected revenues of $4 billion.
Seymour Merrin is a leading industry analyst and heads Merrin Information Services Inc. in Palo Alto, California.

H&R Block Inc. has decided not to complete the spin-off of its CompuServe online unit for now.
H&R Block owns 80 percent of CompuServe after spinning off part of the online service earlier this year.
CompuServe is facing financial troubles and uncertainties in the online industry.
CompuServe has approximately 5.2 million subscribers, with slightly more than half located outside the United States.
America Online Inc. is the largest online service with more than 6 million subscribers.
CompuServe and Prodigy have been negatively impacted as users have shifted to lower-cost Internet access providers.
Some analysts believe that online services may not survive in the long run.
H&R Block spun off 20 percent of CompuServe in April and planned to distribute the rest to shareholders.
H&R Block will not present the proposed spin-off of the rest of CompuServe at its annual meeting on September 11.
CompuServe's stock has decreased from a high of $35.50 to near $10 recently.

Shiva Corp stock rose five points on Wednesday.
Speculation exists that Shiva Corp may be an acquisition target of a major network equipment player.
Paul Johnson, an analyst at Robertson Stephens, maintains a long-term attractive rating on Shiva stock.
Shiva shares have increased nearly 14 percent in the last two days.
By early afternoon on Wednesday, Shiva stock was trading at 53-3/4, up 5 points for the day.
Shiva Corp declined to comment on what it termed a market rumor.
Cynthia Deysher, Shiva's chief financial officer, stated that the company has had similar rumors before.
Chris Stix, an analyst at Cowen & Co, noted that Shiva was mentioned as a potential merger candidate in a trade magazine.
The November 11 issue of Communications Week discussed a possible merger between Ascend Communications Inc and Shiva.
Shiva's share price rebound may be influenced by comments about a potential major contract win with an unnamed telecom carrier.

CompuServe Corp will disband its Wow! online service due to failure to attract U.S. consumers.
CompuServe plans to defend its business and technical customer base.
CompuServe will accelerate the expensing of customer marketing costs.
CompuServe is taking a $28.6 million charge for previously incurred subscriber acquisition costs.
CompuServe will pursue higher margin businesses, including international consumer markets like Europe.
Peter Krasilovsky, an analyst at Arlen Communications, stated that CompuServe's actions represent a strategic retreat.
Krasilovsky claimed that CompuServe will not contend for leadership among online service providers in North America again.
CompuServe stock fell by 1-5/8 to 10-1/8 in early trading.
H&R Block Inc suspended plans to spin off its remaining 80 percent stake in CompuServe.
H&R Block reported a substantial loss for its quarter ended October 31, citing CompuServe's turmoil.

Texas Instruments Inc will receive more than $1 billion in royalty payments from Samsung Electric Co Ltd.
The royalty payments will increase Texas Instruments's net income.
Texas Instruments will use the additional income to focus on more profitable lines of business.
Some Wall Street analysts were reassured by the deal, while others noted it was less generous than a previous agreement in 1995.
Texas Instruments's stock gained 4-3/8 to 60-7/8 by late Wednesday.
The stock was among the most actively traded on the NYSE.
Texas Instruments expects Samsung to pay it more than $1 billion as part of a 10-year technology cross-licensing pact.
Both companies agreed to drop pending patent infringement lawsuits against each other.
Merrill Lynch analyst Tom Kurlak stated that the agreement's royalty formula is at roughly 40 to 50 percent of the rate of the old agreement.
Kurlak indicated that Texas Instruments appears willing to accept a lower royalty rate to have the lawsuits dropped.

America Online Inc. has introduced a flat-rate pricing plan.
Analysts believe that America Online Inc. is on track to become a major media player.
America Online Inc. has more than 7 million subscribers.
Analysts warn that America Online Inc.'s network capacity may soon be overwhelmed.
The company's offer of unlimited usage for $19.95 per month could impact its capacity to handle demand.
If a small fraction of subscribers use the unlimited access, the service may become overloaded.
AOL's user base has grown from less than 1 million users three years ago to over 7 million.
AOL's stock price increased from a year-low of $22 to $44 before falling to $37.50.
Analysts note that increased online usage will raise costs for adding network capacity.
AOL expects the next two quarters to be transitional for its operations and finances.

Blue chip technology stocks experienced a buying spree on Wednesday.
The buying spree was driven by optimism about holiday PC sales and year-end book-squaring.
A Soundview analyst made positive comments about Compaq Computer Corp, contributing to the rally.
Fears regarding the holiday sales season for consumer personal-computer makers decreased.
Compaq Computer Corp's stock increased by 6-1/2 points to 78-3/4.
International Business Machines Corp's stock rose by 6-1/8 points to 157-3/4.
Intel Corp's stock increased by 5-3/8 points to 135-3/8.
Dell Computer Corp's stock rose by 3-5/8 points to 57.
Microsoft Corp's stock gained 2-3/4 points to 82-5/8.
Peter Jenkins stated that the buying activity was a group move among technology stocks.

The U.S. Postal Service announced a plan to enhance the security and reliability of electronic mail.
The plan allows businesses and consumers to verify that e-mail has not been tampered with.
The Postal Service will offer services for electronic mail similar to those for ordinary mail, such as sending certified letters.
Robert Reisner, vice president of strategic planning, stated that security threats have hindered the transition from messaging to electronic commerce.
Cylink Corp is developing a system for the Postal Service to verify the identity of e-mail senders.
The system will allow users to register a digital signature with the Postal Service.
The Postal Service will investigate any tampering with electronic mail, similar to how it investigates tampering with regular mail.
The Postal Service is collaborating with Sun Microsystems to enhance non-electronic mail delivery.
A new online system for bulk mailers will allow them to calculate postage rates using a Java-based software application.
The Postal Service plans to offer hybrid services that combine electronic and paper mail.

A group of leading trademark specialists plans to release recommendations.
The recommendations aim to minimize disputes over Internet address names.
The International Trademark Association is working on a white paper.
The white paper will be completed in the next few months.
David Maher is the co-chair of the association's Internet issues committee.
David Maher provided this information in a telephone interview.

The Internet grew significantly in 2023, while online services struggled to gain new customers.
A survey by Louis Harris and Associates conducted in late September estimated that 35 million adults in the United States had used the Internet, up from 27 million at the beginning of the year.
Humphrey Taylor, chairman of the polling organization, stated that the number of adult Americans using computers for cyber-activities is increasing.
America Online Inc. and Compuserve Corp. reported nearly 41 million subscribers, the same level found by Harris in January.
Online services faced increased competition from companies like AT&T Corp., which offer cheaper Internet-only access.
Businesses are interested in Internet usage figures as a potential source of new revenue.
The Harris poll indicated that, although more people are getting wired, they are spending less time online.
Home users reported being online for an average of 2.8 hours a week, down from three hours in an April survey.
Business and other users reported being online for an average of 1.8 hours, down from two hours in April.
The poll found that individuals with college and graduate degrees were more likely to use computers and access the Internet compared to those who graduated from high school.

The Business Software Alliance is withdrawing its support for the Clinton Administration's new policy on encryption export rules.
The Business Software Alliance includes Microsoft Corp and International Business Machine Corp's Lotus Development.
The alliance expressed concerns that the rules implementing the new encryption export policy are flawed.
The alliance stated that significant backtracking has occurred since the October 1 announcement.
The alliance doubts that the regulations will work, meet consumer demands, or be accepted by the private sector without immediate changes.
Greg Simon, the vice president's chief domestic policy adviser, and other officials have met with the software group to discuss their criticism.
Final rules on the encryption export policy are expected by January 1.
The administration is trying to create a compromise on the export of products containing encryption.
Current laws restrict export products to very weak coding features.
U.S. software companies claim they are losing overseas sales to foreign companies not subject to export laws.

A break-in at the U.S. Justice Department's World Wide Web site occurred on August 16.
Unidentified hackers replaced the department's web page with a message labelled the 'Department of Injustice' that included a swastika and a picture of Adolf Hitler.
Justice officials quickly removed the vandalized page.
Security experts stated that the security flaws that allowed the break-in likely exist in thousands of other corporate and government web sites.
Richard Power, a senior analyst at the Computer Security Institute, claimed that the vast majority of sites are vulnerable and that the Justice Department should not be singled out.
Justice Department officials stated that the compromised web site was not connected to any computers containing sensitive files.
The web site included copies of press releases, speeches, and other publicly available information.
Bert Brandenburg, a spokesman for the Justice Department, compared the security breach to graffiti on the outside of a building.
The Nation of Islam's Million Man March web site was vandalized last year.
According to a General Accounting Office report, hackers make 250,000 attempts annually to break into U.S. military computers.

An international task force released a draft plan for expanding Internet addresses.
The International Ad Hoc Committee on domain names was formed by the Internet Society in October.
The committee recommended adding seven new top-level domains to the Internet.
Top-level domains are three-letter designations that most Internet sites end with.
The committee suggested that an unlimited number of firms be authorized to register new addresses.
The committee plans to initially approve 20 to 30 new registration services.
Network Solutions Inc. currently distributes most site addresses and charges $100 for each registration.
Network Solutions will maintain a monopoly on existing domain names until the committee's ultimate goal is achieved.
The full text of the recommendations was posted on the Internet at http://www.iahc.org.
The proposal will be open for public comment until January 17, and a final report is expected by February 3.

The Federal Communications Commission proposed to reduce the $23 billion a year that long-distance telephone companies pay to local service providers in access fees.
The FCC did not propose whether access charges should be imposed on Internet service providers and instead requested comments on the issue.
The FCC stated it could reduce access fees through a schedule of long-distance access charge reductions or by allowing market forces to lower fees.
Access charges were established after the break-up of AT&T Corp. in 1984, leading to the creation of regional local service companies known as 'Baby Bells'.
New telecommunications rules signed into law in February aim to increase competition for local and long-distance service and reduce prices.
Long-distance companies argue that access fees are excessive and support significant government-mandated cuts.
AT&T recommended that the FCC quickly eliminate $10 billion in excess access fees to benefit consumers.
Local phone companies acknowledge that access fees exceed their actual costs for carrying long-distance calls but prefer gradual reductions based on competition.
Roy Neel, president of the U.S. Telephone Association, stated that the FCC should prevent long-distance companies from benefiting at consumers' expense.
Local phone companies connect Internet users to Internet service providers over local lines without receiving access charges for those calls.

Philip Karn is a computer scientist who was barred from exporting a floppy disk containing computer encryption programming.
Karn asked a federal court to strike down the export limits, claiming they violate his right to free speech.
The State Department denied Karn's request to export the programming on disk in 1994 but allowed him to export the same material in a book.
U.S. law categorizes many types of encryption and computer coding programs as munitions.
The Clinton administration issued new rules that relaxed some export limits, but many encryption programs remain classified as munitions.
Karn's attorney, Kenneth Bass, argued that the export limits infringe on Karn's constitutional rights to free speech and due process.
Bass claimed that the First Amendment should apply equally to computer code in a book and on a floppy disk.
Karn's disk contained 'source' code, which provides directions to write software, rather than 'object' code, which is a working program.
Federal district court Judge Marilyn Patel ruled that source code should be considered a protected form of speech.
The ruling by Judge Patel is not binding on the D.C. Appeals court.

Prospects for comprehensive reform of U.S. banking and financial services laws are considered bright.
The Clinton Administration is considering a far-reaching proposal that has upset some banks.
There is a general agreement that the Glass-Steagall Act should be scrapped.
There is little consensus about removing barriers between financial firms and other commercial companies.
The Clinton Administration is actively considering reform proposals expected in the next two months.
Larry LaRocco, a former Congressman and bank lobbyist, stated that there is a strong desire for Glass-Steagall reform.
LaRocco believes that legislators have sufficient time to reach an agreement within the 105th Congress.
Federal courts and regulators have lifted many restrictions on banks' non-banking activities.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin is considering recommendations to remove barriers between financial and non-financial companies.
The commerce issue is the last remaining obstacle in the reform process according to a source familiar with the administration's deliberations.

An influential global research group is preparing guidelines on encryption policy for its member countries.
The guidelines will avoid some contentious issues according to a draft report obtained by Reuters.
The Clinton administration sought support for its encryption export policy in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development guidelines but did not receive an endorsement.
The draft guidelines do not take a position on a U.S. policy requirement for data-scrambling encryption programs to provide law enforcement access to keys.
The draft states that governments should weigh the costs and benefits of key recovery without implying that they should or should not legislate for lawful access.
John Dryden, head of the OECD's Information, Computer and Communications Policy division, stated that member countries have differing views on controversial issues.
Some countries view encryption as a means to protect privacy and encourage global commerce, while others see it as a potential obstacle to law enforcement.
The guidelines suggest that encryption users should have access to cryptography that meets their needs and that government controls should be minimal.
The draft guidelines outline competing interests and do not aim to create a model national law.
The guidelines recommend that encryption standards and usage be determined by the market in an open and competitive environment.

Internet access providers and others expressed concerns about potential negative impacts of Congress on cyberspace.
Company representatives met with members of the Congressional Internet Caucus to discuss legislation related to the Internet.
Tom Evslin, vice president of AT&T Corp.'s WorldNet Internet service, stated that it is likely there will be bills introduced to legislate Internet content.
Evslin expressed that preventing Congress from making mistakes regarding Internet legislation would be challenging.
Bill Schrader, president of Internet provider PSINet Inc., warned that careless legislation could harm the Internet industry.
Members of Congress at the meeting committed to protecting the Internet.
Rep. Rick White, R-Pa., acknowledged the challenges ahead in addressing various Internet-related issues.
Sen. Conrad Burns noted that government legislation often lags behind private sector developments.
Last year, Congress passed the Communications Decency Act, which faced opposition from online companies and civil libertarians.
Congress also rejected measures that would have held Internet providers liable for copyright infringement.

A dispute has arisen between the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the state of Rhode Island regarding insurance laws.
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency is considering overriding a new Rhode Island insurance law.
The Rhode Island insurance law imposes different requirements on banks selling insurance compared to those on insurance agents.
National banks have the legal right to sell insurance in small towns.
State insurance regulators have historically imposed strict rules on banks selling insurance.
The Supreme Court ruled last year that states cannot significantly interfere with national banks conducting permissible activities.
Banks claim that states are attempting to evade the Supreme Court's ruling.
James McIntyre, counsel to the Association of Banks-in-Insurance, stated that the Rhode Island statute is the first successful restrictive legislation effort.
Major states such as Texas, Pennsylvania, and Illinois are expected to consider similar legislation.
The Independent Insurance Agents of America stated that preempting the Rhode Island law would be inappropriate.

Legislators introduced two bills to overturn the Clinton administration's export limits on computer encryption technology.
Encryption products scramble information and render it unreadable without a password or software key.
Encryption is used for various purposes, including keeping business emails confidential and protecting consumers' credit card numbers online.
Senators claimed that export restrictions on encryption products hindered the development of the Internet and U.S. companies' competitiveness.
The bills aim to roll back restrictions on the export of strong cryptography to allow U.S. firms to compete globally.
Sen. Pat Leahy stated that online commerce would not reach its full potential under current policies.
The bills would allow U.S. companies to export products with strong encryption if similar products are available from foreign suppliers.
Under current policy, companies can only export strong encryption if it includes a feature for the U.S. government to recover the software key.
The Clinton administration argues that it needs to crack codes to catch international criminals and terrorists.
If the bills became law, mandatory key recovery would be banned, but the government could still restrict encryption exports for military use or to certain countries.

The Czech Republic and Spain played to a scoreless draw in a World Cup group six qualifier.
The match was described as lacklustre and did not meet expectations.
The Czech Republic faced their first significant test since reaching the Euro 96 final.
Raul Gonzalez made his debut for Spain in the match.
Both teams had previously won their World Cup openers against weaker opponents.
Spain won 6-2 against the Faroe Islands, and the Czech Republic won 6-0 against Malta.
Yugoslavia and Slovakia had already secured wins against the same teams.
Both teams started the match tentatively, looking for mistakes from the opponent.
Karel Poborsky missed a scoring chance for the Czech Republic.
Pavel Srnicek, the Czech goalkeeper, made a mistake that nearly led to a goal.

Goran Ivanisevic won against Adrian Voinea with a score of 7-6 6-4 in the first round of the Czech Indoor Open.
Tim Henman defeated Nicklas Kulti with a score of 7-6 6-4 on the opening day of the tournament.
Both Ivanisevic and Henman utilized the fast carpet court to achieve multiple service winners.
Ivanisevic is ranked fifth in the world and Voinea is ranked 42nd.
Ivanisevic hit 14 aces during his match.
Ivanisevic stated that the carpet at the current venue is faster than the one used in Vienna.
Ivanisevic mentioned that winning the tournament would require defeating at least one top 10 player.
Ivanisevic is scheduled to play the winner of the match between Petr Korda and Nicolas Lapentti.
Ivanisevic may also need to compete against Boris Becker and Bohdan Ulihrach to reach the final.
Henman expressed that he felt he should have won the first set before the tiebreak.

Boris Becker withdrew from the $475,000 Czech Indoor Open due to a recurring wrist injury.
Becker tore a ligament in his right wrist during the third round at this year's Wimbledon.
Becker experienced pain after training and withdrew from his scheduled second round match against Martin Damm.
ATP Tour Supervisor Gayle Bradshaw stated that Becker's wrist was too sore for him to play.
Becker won his previous match against Frederik Fetterlein with a score of 6-3 6-4.
During the match against Fetterlein, Becker held his wrist several times.
Becker attempted to return to the circuit last month but had to retire from the first round in Bucharest.
Becker also lost in the second round in Basle and withdrew from Lyon two weeks ago.
Becker's absence has hindered his goal of qualifying for a record 12th appearance at the ATP Tour championship.
Becker currently trails Wayne Ferreira for the eighth and final spot in Hannover.

Tim Henman is the only seed to advance to the semifinals of the $475,000 Czech Indoor Open.
Tim Henman defeated Wayne Ferreira with a score of 6-4 6-3.
David Prinosil defeated Todd Martin with a score of 7-6 7-6.
Martin Damm defeated Michael Stich with a score of 5-7 6-4 6-4.
Petr Korda defeated Jiri Novak with a score of 6-1 6-0.
Tim Henman will compete against David Prinosil in the semifinals.
Petr Korda will compete against Martin Damm in the semifinals.
Wayne Ferreira is ranked seventh in the world.
Tim Henman is ranked 26th in the world.
Todd Martin is currently 199 points behind Wayne Ferreira in the race for the final spot at the ATP Tour championship.

The Prague Stock Exchange closed higher for the third consecutive session on Tuesday.
The PX50 index increased by 2.5 points, or 0.47 percent, to 537.1.
Komercni Banka, IPB, Ceska Sporitelna, and Zivnostenska Banka all gained ground.
The Reuters RPIX index climbed five points to 1,095.
A total of 188 shares rose, 121 shares lost, and 74 shares held steady.
The total volume was 701,356 shares with a turnover of 721.14 million crowns.
IPB rose 15 crowns to 331, marking its second consecutive five percent gain.
The government announced that IPB would be the first of the big four banks to undergo privatization.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik indicated that a strong foreign strategic partner would likely benefit from the sell-off.
Nomura and ING Bank have been rumored as frontrunners in the bid for IPB.

The Czech trade deficit fell to 10.5 billion crowns in September from 14.5 billion in August.
Analysts stated that the fall in the trade deficit buoyed market sentiment.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) reported that the January-September trade shortfall reached an all-time high of 110.7 billion crowns.
The January-September trade shortfall surpassed the full 1995 deficit of 95.7 billion crowns.
The September trade shortfall was the smallest one-month deficit of the year.
Analysts had forecasted an average trade gap of 13 to 15 billion crowns for September.
Martin Kupka, an economist at Patria Finance, expressed optimism about the September figure but did not revise the full year forecast.
Patria Finance forecasted a year-end deficit of 150-160 billion crowns.
The CSU reported that September imports rose 15.2 percent year-on-year, while exports rose 5.9 percent.
Strong growth in machinery and transport equipment imports accounted for 38.3 percent of total imports.

Czech telephone operator SPT Telecom a.s. reported a nine-month gross profit of 6.0 billion crowns.
SPT Telecom's gross profit for all of 1995 was 7.0 billion crowns.
SPT Telecom used International Accounting Standards in calculating its profit.
The company's revenues totaled 23.3 billion crowns, nearly equal to the 26.4 billion crowns for 1995.
SPT Telecom's outlays for investment in the nine-month period exceeded 20 billion crowns.
A Dutch-Swiss consortium of PTT Netherlands and Swiss Telecom bought a 27 percent stake in SPT from the government.
The consortium paid $1.32 billion for its stake in SPT Telecom.
SPT Telecom installed 272,000 new telephone lines year-to-date, bringing its total to 2.67 million lines.
SPT Telecom aims to achieve a target of over 400,000 new set lines in 1996.
SPT Telecom plans to increase its network by another 500,000 lines in 1997 and 650,000 lines in 1998.

Sepap Group a.s. reported a nine-month net profit of 188.4 million crowns, down from 520.4 million crowns in the same period in 1995.
The company's revenues decreased to 3.94 billion crowns from 5.34 billion crowns over the same nine-month period.
The shutdown of Sepap's main paper mill contributed to the decline in net profit.
The Steti mill accounts for approximately 75% of Sepap's revenues and profits.
The Steti mill's pre-tax profits fell to seven million crowns, compared to a gross profit of 95 million crowns in the same nine-month period in 1995.
Sepap's third quarter results stabilized after a downturn in the first half of the year.
The company anticipates a slight improvement in year-end earnings compared to third quarter levels.
ROTO, Sepap's second largest subsidiary, reported a nine-month pre-tax profit of 149 million crowns on sales of 1.25 billion crowns.
Michael Dingman controls 48% of Sepap through Daventree Ltd, while Assidoman holds a 39% stake in the company.
The market for pulp and paper is experiencing mixed signals for the fourth quarter.

The Czech capital market has been criticized for a lack of transparency.
An independent regulator is needed for the Czech capital market, according to a senior Finance Ministry official.
Jan Veverka stated that the creation of an independent securities committee will not immediately improve the Czech capital market.
Veverka mentioned that the independent body would create better conditions for gradual market refinement.
Foreign and domestic investors have complained about poor legislation and lack of enforcement in the Czech capital market.
The Prague Stock Exchange has declined by approximately 16 percent over the past two months due to a negative outlook from investors.
Legislation allows for near complete secrecy of off-market deals, where an estimated 70 percent of trading occurs.
Veverka noted that the original laws governing securities trading discarded the concept of regulation due to fears of abuse of power.
The mass voucher privatization resulted in shares from nearly 2,000 firms being placed on the market in a short period.
Veverka called for a higher level debate on creating a U.S.-style SEC oversight body.

The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) led in the Senate election run-offs in the Czech Republic.
Turnout for the Senate elections was 30.5 percent.
The ODS won 19 seats in the new upper house.
The opposition Social Democrats won eight seats.
The Christian Democrats won seven seats.
The Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) won two seats.
President Vaclav Havel appealed for greater voter turnout before the elections.
The Senate elections were considered important for the future of Klaus's coalition.
Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik predicted that government parties would control the Senate.
Klaus has expressed skepticism about the necessity of the Senate.

Czech share prices increased after the coalition government's victory in the Senate elections.
Analysts believe the rise in share prices is primarily due to a technical correction.
The Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index rose 0.86 percent during the daily price fixing.
The increase was driven by gains in seven of the eight most-capitalised shares.
Brokers expressed limited optimism that the rally would continue beyond a few days.
The coalition government led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus won 52 of 81 seats in the Senate.
The centre-left opposition Social Democrats secured 25 seats in the Senate.
Voter turnout for the Senate elections was just over 30 percent.
The Prague bourse has declined approximately 17 percent since September.
Analysts do not expect the Senate elections to lead to changes in securities laws.

The Czech trade deficit increased by nearly 16 billion crowns ($600 million) in October.
Analysts were not alarmed by the rise in the trade deficit as it aligned with their full year forecasts.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) reported that the trade gap for the first 10 months of the year reached a record 125.5 billion crowns.
The trade deficit for January-September was revised to 109.6 billion crowns.
The CSU, the Ministry of Industry and Trade, and some analysts predict the year-end deficit will be between 150-160 billion crowns.
Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka, stated that the year-end deficit will be 150-160 billion crowns.
Janacek noted that the economic revival of Germany will impact export growth in the first half of next year.
The CSU reported that imports rose by 14.4 percent year-on-year in the first ten months of the year.
Exports increased by 5.2 percent year-on-year after a 5.9 percent increase in January-September.
Imports of machinery and transport equipment grew by 19.1 percent year-on-year, making up 38.3 percent of total imports.

Liberty International Holdings is entering the British pensions market.
Liberty is establishing a pensions company called Liberty International Pensions.
Liberty International Pensions will target money purchase pension schemes and retail pensions.
BT Pension Scheme is paying five million pounds for 10 percent equity in Liberty International Pensions.
The remaining equity in Liberty International Pensions will be held by Liberty.
Liberty and Hermes are creating a subsidiary called Hermes Liberty International Pensions.
Hermes will act as the fund manager for Hermes Liberty International Pensions.
BT Pension Scheme will transfer 1.5 billion pounds in assets to the new funds.
Liberty's chairman Donald Gordon stated that Liberty is well positioned for changes in the UK pensions industry.
Liberty International Pensions requires approval from Britain's Department of Trade and Industry before launch.

Britain's largest cable television company was formed from the merger of Cable & Wireless, NYNEX Corp., and Bell Canada International.
The merger took five weeks to complete.
The new company surpasses Telewest as Britain's biggest cable operator.
Richard Brown is the Chief Executive of Cable & Wireless and was appointed five months prior to the merger.
C&W replaced British Telecommunications Plc in a major German alliance with RWE.
The merged company will provide integrated telecommunications, information, and entertainment services.
C&W's Mercury telephone company will have access to 18 million business and domestic customers.
30 percent of homes that can take cable have opted for one or more cable services.
Around 6 billion pounds has been invested in building the broadband fibre optic network in the U.K.
Videotron is being acquired by Bell Cablemedia in a transaction involving a $338 million equity investment from Cable & Wireless.

Halifax Building Society plans to shed its mutual status and become a publicly quoted bank in June next year.
David Gilchrist is the director of corporate affairs at Halifax.
Halifax's nine million members will vote on the conversion early next year.
The conversion will involve transferring business to an existing subsidiary, which will result in losing a five-year protection against takeover.
The voting threshold required for approval of the conversion plans will increase.
Gilchrist is confident that at least 50 percent of voting members will approve the conversion.
Previous building society conversions have achieved approval rates of over 75 percent.
Halifax will provide members with details of the conversion plans and share distribution scheme in January 1997.
The cost of the conversion exercise will include significant printing and postage costs.
A special general meeting will be held in Sheffield in February for members to vote on the proposals.

Invesco announced a merger with AIM Management Group.
The combined entity will be called AMVESCO Plc.
AMVESCO Plc will manage approximately $150 billion.
The merger values AIM at around $1.6 billion.
Bob McCullough is Invesco's chief financial officer.
Analysts had mixed opinions on the timing of the merger.
Martin Cross from UBS stated that Invesco is buying at a high market valuation.
Phillip Gibbs from BZW expressed a positive outlook on the merger.
Invesco shares closed at 237.5p.
Charles Brady is the chairman and chief executive of Invesco.

KPMG is one of the world's big six international accounting and consultancy firms.
KPMG believes investment in infrastructure and technology will hasten revenue growth.
Jon Madonna is the chairman of KPMG International.
KPMG reported an eight percent rise in worldwide revenues for the fiscal year to September 30, 1996, totaling $8.1 billion.
KPMG's revenue for the previous year was $7.5 billion.
Madonna stated that revenue growth in excess of 10 percent was a reasonable expectation.
KPMG invested heavily in infrastructure and technology during the year.
Significant revenue growth is likely to come from the consulting side of the business.
KPMG's growth rate for the year was lower than rival firm Andersen Worldwide, which reported a 16 percent increase in 1996 revenues to $9.4 billion.
Madonna indicated that KPMG's 1996 revenue growth, when adjusted for dollars, was the same as the previous year.

Lloyd's of London declared that over 90 percent of its members had accepted a settlement offer for its recovery plan.
Lloyd's reported a significant increase in acceptances from U.S. investors after a U.S. appeals court overturned a ruling that threatened its survival.
As of Wednesday afternoon, 66.7 percent of U.S. members had accepted the recovery plan.
Lloyd's Chairman David Rowland stated that the level of acceptances indicated members' support for the reconstruction of Lloyd's.
A Lloyd's spokesman noted that acceptances from U.S. investors, known as Names, increased significantly overnight.
Before the recent increase, only 53 percent of the 2,700 U.S. Names had accepted the plan by Tuesday night.
A federal appeals court in Baltimore overturned a ruling by U.S. District Court Judge Robert Payne that had allowed U.S. Names more time to consider the plan.
The appeals court sent the case back to the lower court with orders to dismiss it.
As of Tuesday evening, acceptances for the recovery plan totaled 82 percent, up from 75 percent on Saturday.
The deadline for accepting the 3.2 billion pounds recovery plan was extended to allow more time for responses.

Britain's investment watchdog fined companies in the Robert Fleming group a total of 700,000 pounds.
The fines equate to approximately $1.09 million.
Hong Kong authorities secured nearly $20 million in voluntary compensation from a company jointly owned by Jardine Matheson and Robert Fleming groups.
The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) fined Robert Fleming Asset Management (RFAM) 400,000 pounds.
Three other firms in the Robert Fleming group received 100,000 pound penalties each.
The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of Hong Kong agreed to the compensation package.
Robert Fleming Asset Management accepted the failings exposed by the investigation and expressed regret.
Paul Bateman, RFAM's chairman, stated that the company was embarrassed by the breaches.
A five-month joint investigation by IMRO and the SFC focused on dealing procedures at Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM).
Colin Armstrong, a former senior fund manager at JFIM, engaged in late allocation of deals, resulting in losses for three accounts managed by JFIM.

Most Britons associate moneylending with loan sharks.
Britain's established credit companies lend to people who cannot borrow from high street banks or credit card companies.
Eddie Cran is the chief executive of the financial services group Cattle's, which operates door-to-door moneylenders Shopacheck.
Cattle's and similar firms are publicly quoted and profitable, paying annual dividends to shareholders.
Borrowers from these firms may have minor civil court judgments, be unemployed, or prefer not to use bank accounts or credit cards.
The rates charged by credit companies may seem high compared to traditional credit options.
Credit companies include costs such as collection and insurance in their rates, which are agreed upon in advance.
The annualized percentage rates (APRs) for borrowing can exceed 150 percent.
Borrowing 100 pounds over 25 weeks from Shopacheck with a five-pound weekly repayment costs 25 pounds.
Shopacheck has 2,800 agents and its average loan is for six months, with an average amount of 150 pounds and average indebtedness of 350 pounds.

Singapore's Hotel Properties and property group Canary Wharf applied for detailed planning consent for a development in London's former docks.
Thio Gim Hock is the executive director of HPL.
HPL and Canary Wharf formed an 80-20 joint venture for a residential, hotel, and leisure project.
The project is the first phase of development on an 11-acre site adjoining the River Thames.
The development is part of the Canary Wharf docklands development to the east of the City financial district.
The development will be the first at Canary Wharf since banks sold out to the Reichmann-led consortium.
80 percent of the offices at Canary Wharf have been occupied.
Thio Gim Hock expects to start building 330 residential units, a five-star hotel, and a sports club in early 1997.
The completion of the project is expected by the end of 1998 or early 1999.
The initial capitalisation for the project will be 50 million pounds from the partners.

The role of compliance in financial institutions has gained attention due to recent rule violations.
Compliance officials are responsible for ensuring adherence to procedures that prevent fraud and malpractice in banking and finance.
The British investment watchdog IMRO fined companies in the Robert Fleming group 700,000 pounds ($1.09 million).
Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) secured nearly $20 million in voluntary compensation from a Robert Fleming and Jardine Matheson joint venture.
The penalties were a result of compliance violations that led to two individuals being banned from the markets.
A compliance officer at a top international investment bank stated that the irregular dealings leading to the investigation were longstanding issues.
Colin Armstrong, a former senior fund manager at Jardine Fleming Investment Management, profited from late allocation of deals, affecting client accounts.
Compliance industry insiders indicated that early warning signs could have prevented significant damage.
Compliance officers began appearing in London firms about 10 years ago, with many coming from accounting and legal backgrounds.
Top-ranking compliance professionals can earn up to 100,000 pounds a year, including bonuses.

In 1996, 278 British companies valued at 14.4 billion pounds were sold in cross-border deals.
In the first nine months of 1995, 258 British firms worth 19.1 billion pounds were sold in cross-border deals.
Rupert Faure Walker is the head of corporate finance at HSBC Samuel Montagu.
Faure Walker stated that the first quarter of 1997 is expected to be very active for mergers and acquisitions.
Britain is regarded as the European leader for takeover activity.
The upcoming general election is expected to influence market activity in 1997.
The Labour party has consistently led in opinion polls ahead of the Conservatives.
An election is due to be called by May 1997.
If Labour wins the election, companies may delay significant moves until after the first Labour budget.
A 6-9 month period of caution may follow a Labour election victory.

Hunting high-earning company executives has become a focus for British media.
Institutional shareholders are scrutinizing the pay of top executives in the UK.
General Electric Co faced objections from shareholders regarding a £10 million package for managing director George Simpson.
General Electric Co set tougher performance targets in response to shareholder objections.
