Both research firms expect an increase in fourth quarter PC shipments compared to the third quarter.
IDC forecasts an 18.5 percent growth in worldwide personal computer shipments for 1996, while Dataquest projects a 19.7 percent growth.

Ingram Micro Inc. is set to hold its initial public offering on Wall Street on Thursday.
There have been last-minute delays for Ingram Micro's IPO, including management changes.
Manish Shah, editor and publisher of the IPO Maven, stated that there has not been a comparable IPO in the technology sector this year.
The estimated price for Ingram's 20 million share offering was increased to $17 to $19 a share from $14 to $16.
Morgan Stanley is the underwriter for Ingram Micro's IPO.
Ingram Micro is the world's leading distributor of computer hardware, software, and networking equipment.
Ingram Micro is based in Santa Ana, California, and is expected to generate roughly $10 billion in revenues this year.
The three world-class distributors of computer products are Ingram Micro, Merisel Inc. with $6 billion in revenues, and Tech Data Corp. with $4 billion in revenues.
Seymour Merrin, a leading industry analyst, stated that market share is the only important factor in the distribution business.
Ingram Micro's suppliers include major brands such as IBM, Intel, Microsoft, Cisco, Apple, Novell, and U.S. Robotics.

Iomega Corp plans to apply its computer storage technology to handheld consumer electronics.
The reusable data storage system is called 'n-hand'.
The n-hand technology could be used in digital cameras, computer game devices, cellular phones, and handheld personal computers.
In cameras, the technology could function as a removable 'digital film' replacing existing chemical photographic film.
Kim Edwards is the president and chief executive of Iomega Corp.
George Meyer is Iomega's director of marketing for new business.
The n-hand disks are expected to be priced at less than $10 for a 20-megabyte disk.
Iomega expects the n-hand disks to be available by the second half of 1997.
The n-hand disks are about half the size of a business card.
Several industry analysts believe Iomega's technology could help propel digital cameras into the consumer mainstream.

Anysoft Inc. is a U.S.-based start-up formed by Israeli computer scientists.
Anysoft Inc. unveiled a technology that aims to overcome barriers between rival software programs.
The technology allows users to manipulate information from any application while retaining formatting and properties.
The system functions as an underlying layer of operating system software, independent of any one operating system.
Anysoft's system can handle text, numerical data, graphical images, video, and data from remote Internet sites.
Anysoft Chief Executive Illan Poreh stated that this technology represents the beginning of true software interoperability.
Anysoft is backed by Bank Leumi and 21 private investors, including executives from U.S. Robotics Corp.
The company's software programmers were selected from top professors and graduate students at leading Israeli universities.
Industry analysts consider the technology a significant breakthrough for software interoperability.
Previous attempts to create a universally accepted format for computer data have failed due to competitive rivalries.

Microcom Inc and Rockwell Semiconductor Systems plan to enhance their technology partnership.
The partnership aims to accelerate the development of 56-kilobit modems for central switch equipment.
The 56-kilobit modems will enable internet connections at speeds nearly double that of current 28.8 kilobit modems.
The partnership builds on a decade-old product development collaboration between Microcom and Rockwell.
Rockwell Semiconductor is a unit of Rockwell International Corp.
New Microcom central site switch equipment will allow phone carriers, ISPs, and corporate offices to handle calls from 56-kilobit modems.
Prudential analyst Jim Thayer stated that the partnership increases the market scope of Rockwell's 56k offering.
Analyst Rakesh Sood suggested that the Microcom/Rockwell agreement is a defensive response to U.S. Robotics Inc's initiative.
Rockwell will contribute its K56Plus modem chipset, while Microcom will provide its Modemware technology.
Rockwell is opening an East Coast development center with 15 to 20 engineers working with Microcom staff.

CompuServe Corp. will disband its Wow! online service and focus on business and technical customers.
CompuServe will accelerate the expensing of customer marketing costs.
CompuServe will take a $28.6 million charge for previously incurred subscriber acquisition costs.
CompuServe plans to pursue businesses with higher profit margins, particularly in international consumer markets in Europe.
Peter Krasilovsky, an analyst at Arlen Communications, stated that CompuServe's actions represent a strategic retreat.
Krasilovsky also claimed that CompuServe will not compete for the top position among online service providers in North America again.
CompuServe officials stated that no layoffs would result from the latest changes.
The 35 employees from Wow! have been absorbed into CompuServe Interactive.
CompuServe's total head count is approximately 3,200 worldwide.
CompuServe laid off 150 employees, or 4 percent of its workforce, in a previous cutback announced last summer.

America Online Inc has introduced a flat rate pricing plan.
AOL's pricing plan aims to meet increasing subscriber demand.
AOL has over seven million subscribers.
Analysts warn that AOL's network capacity may be overwhelmed by demand.
The unlimited usage offer for $19.95 per month could strain AOL's network.
AOL's user base has grown from under one million to seven million in three years.
AOL's stock price recently doubled from a year-low of 22 to 44.
AOL officials expect the next two quarters to be transitional as they shift business models.
AOL is moving towards generating revenue from advertising and commercial transactions.
Abishek Gami believes AOL can manage the pressures of growing demand.

The stock of General Electric Co. rose in active trading on Tuesday.
The rise in stock was attributed to speculation about a potential dividend increase and share buyback programme.
Chairman John Welch made upbeat comments during a private meeting with analysts.
Analyst Russell Leavitt reported that Welch expected earnings to increase by about 13 percent this year.
First Call projected GE's profits for the 1996 calendar year to be $4.40 per share.
In 1995, GE earned profits of $3.90 per share, totaling $6.6 billion on revenues of $43 billion.
The news from the meeting contributed to General Electric's stock being listed among the NYSE most actives.
The stock price increased by $2.25 to $97.50 in late afternoon trading.
A GE spokesman declined to comment on Welch's remarks but confirmed the board would meet on Friday.
Analyst Martin Sankey from CS First Boston raised his 1997 earnings estimate for GE to $5 per share.

Shiva Corp. stock lost almost half its value on Wednesday.
The company's stock price dropped by $15.625, or 45 percent, to $19.25 on Nasdaq.
Shiva Corp. expected fourth-quarter earnings to be between 5 cents and 7 cents a share.
Consensus estimates for fourth-quarter earnings were 21 cents a share, according to First Call.
Twenty-four million shares of Shiva Corp. were traded on that day.
Securities analysts attributed the stock's decline to the earnings shortfall and changes in business strategy.
Cynthia Deysher, Chief Financial Officer of Shiva Corp., stated that the shortfall was due to weakness in domestic sales and a delayed order from IBM.
Shiva Corp. plans to reorganize its sales force to address the earnings shortfall.
Shiva Corp. renegotiated its strategic alliance with Northern Telecom Ltd., which may lead to declining revenues but rising profit margins.
Shiva Corp. will receive a percentage of sales from the new arrangement with Northern Telecom instead of a fixed fee.

Two members of Congress criticized the Federal Reserve for its record of hiring and promoting women and minorities.
Representative Henry Gonzalez and Representative Jesse Jackson Jr. wrote a letter to Fed chairman Alan Greenspan.
The letter stated that several discrimination lawsuits against the Federal Reserve indicate a need for reform.
Henry Gonzalez is a Democrat from Texas serving his 19th term in Congress.
Jesse Jackson Jr. is a second-term Democrat from Illinois and the son of a civil rights leader.
A Fed spokesman declined to comment on the criticisms.
Four black secretaries filed a lawsuit against the Federal Reserve in January.
Fifteen other current and former employees have requested to join the litigation related to the lawsuit.
The Federal Reserve's record of diversity in hiring and promotion was described as woefully inadequate by Gonzalez and Jackson.
In 1993, there was one woman and one non-white among the 35 top paid staff at the Federal Reserve, while currently, there are 11 women and five minorities among 72 top paid staff.

Senator Bob Kerrey is preparing legislation regarding computer encryption export policy.
People familiar with Senator Bob Kerrey's plans have reported on this preparation.
The current debate involves the Clinton administration and U.S. software companies.
The Clinton administration favors strict export controls on encryption.
U.S. software companies and civil libertarians want to relax export limits on encryption.
Encryption programs scramble information.
Scrambled information becomes unreadable without a password or software 'key.'

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan urged lawmakers to delay consideration of proposals allowing banks to merge with commercial companies.
Greenspan suggested that Congress should focus on modest financial reforms to remove legal barriers preventing banks from affiliating with insurance companies and securities firms.
Greenspan stated that Congress should widen the permissible range of affiliations for banking organizations to enhance consumer choices and financial market efficiency.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin presented the Clinton administration's plan to allow banks to enter the securities and insurance businesses.
Rubin did not address whether banks should merge with commercial companies and offered Congress two proposals regarding such combinations.
Greenspan acknowledged that barriers between banks and commercial companies will eventually diminish due to technological advancements.
Greenspan advised caution in removing these barriers due to uncertainties regarding their impact on the U.S. financial system.
Greenspan recommended postponing wider authorization of banking and commerce while focusing on financial modernization.
The administration's plan aims to allow banks, securities firms, and insurance companies to compete under a uniform set of regulations.
Rubin estimated that increased competition from the plan could save consumers up to $15 billion a year.

The Czech economy is showing signs of slower growth and a widening trade gap.
Analysts expressed concerns about the pace of industrial restructuring in the Czech economy.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has been praised for achieving low inflation rates, good GDP growth, and an unemployment rate of about three percent.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported a record trade deficit of 160.33 billion crowns ($5.75 billion) for 1996.
The trade deficit increased from a 95.7 billion crown shortfall the previous year.
Some economists are concerned about the export competitiveness of Czech industry.
Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka, stated that competition from other transforming economies is increasing.
Since 1992, the Czech economy has transitioned from recession to 4.8 percent consumption-driven real growth in 1995.
Unemployment in the Czech Republic remains around three percent, with nearly 70 percent of the economy in private hands.
The current account showed a deficit of $3.1 billion crowns for the first three quarters, while the capital account was in surplus by approximately $2.0 billion.

The Prague Stock Exchange faced difficulties in 1996.
Analysts predict that the Prague Stock Exchange will recover in the following year.
Government officials previously lacked commitment to strengthen minority shareholder rights and increase market transparency.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and bourse officials have committed to improving the market.
Jan Sykora of Wood and Company stated that foreign investors are under-invested in the Prague Stock Exchange.
The PX50 index reached a year-high of 582.0 in September 1996.
The PX50 index dropped by nearly a quarter to just above 500 points by the end of 1996.
Government officials supported the creation of an independent supervisory body for the market.
Prime Minister Klaus previously showed little enthusiasm for creating a body similar to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Tomas Jezek stated that creating an SEC-type body is a priority for 1997.

The Prague Stock Exchange fell on Monday from a year high due to profit taking.
Analysts believe sentiment remains bullish for the coming weeks.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka fell sharply, dragging the PX50 index down 0.28 percent to 598.0 points.
Marco Anderegg of Patria Finance stated that there seems to be good support at the current level.
Foreign investor interest remains solid according to Marco Anderegg.
SPT Telecom shares closed down 75 crowns at 3,700.
CEZ shares were down 28 crowns to 1,202.
Komercni Banka shares lost 25 crowns to 2,620.
A local trader suggested that the market's weakness may be short-lived and prices could begin rising again soon.
The PSE has gained 9.7 percent so far in 1997.

British hotels and betting group Ladbroke Group Plc announced the closure of its property arm.
Ladbroke Group Plc will sell its remaining properties to focus on its core businesses of hotels and betting and gaming.
Brian Wallace is the group finance director of Ladbroke.
The cost of the closure is estimated at 52.3 million pounds ($84.4 million).
The closure cost will mainly cover losses from the sale of property and a provision to write down the remaining portfolio.
Ladbroke's 1996 accounts will include a non-operating exceptional charge of 17.6 million pounds.
The exceptional charge mainly represents losses on disposals of investment properties announced during 1996.
Analysts noted that the closure and property sales removed uncertainty for Ladbroke in 1997.
Ladbroke is expected to report a profit rise of around 30 percent for 1996.
The portfolio sold to Minerva Plc had a book value of about 34.6 million pounds and consisted of around 10 commercial and residential properties.

Michael Marks was the chairman of British stockbroking firm Smith New Court before it was taken over by Merrill Lynch.
Michael Marks was appointed chief operating officer for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at Merrill Lynch.
Michael Marks was previously co-head of global equities and will remain as deputy chairman of Merrill Lynch International.
Michael Marks's appointment as chief operating officer comes into force on June 16.
Michael Marks stated that the realignment emphasizes the importance of London as a financial center.
Merrill Lynch International will have a coordinating role to ensure clients are well served.
Under the new structure, there will be five chief operating officers for Merrill's international regions.
Kevin Watts was made chief operating officer for the Asia-Pacific region.
Merrill Lynch's new structure includes a U.S. private client group, an international private client group, an asset management group, and a corporate and institutional client group.
Michael Marks began his career in the City of London with Smith Brothers in 1960.

A future Labour government may overhaul Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
The SIB must find a new chairman.
The Labour Party plans to streamline London's regulatory bodies if it wins the upcoming elections.
The SIB was established in 1985.
The SIB is responsible for ensuring the regulatory system works efficiently.
Chairman Sir Andrew Large will resign at the end of May.
Industry sources believe the new chairman may not come from Britain's frontline regulators.
The SIB supervises frontline regulators that authorize firms to conduct investment business in Britain.
Sir Andrew Large stated that most changes he was overseeing have been completed.
The appointment of a new SIB chairman will be significant due to the potential change in government.

A Chinese court rejected a plea of insanity by bank robber Guo Song and sentenced him to death.
Guo Song was convicted along with two accomplices for a series of bank heists in Beijing.
The court proceedings were observed by foreign reporters to highlight a crackdown on crime.
Guo Song appeared unrepentant during the court session.
The Beijing Number One Intermediate People's Court convicted Guo Song of robbing three bank cash delivery vans.
The presiding judge stated that the court did not accept Guo Song's plea of insanity.
Psychiatric tests indicated that Guo Song had total control over his mental faculties during the crime.
Guo Song, 32 years old, did not speak during the 20-minute hearing.
Guo Song has two weeks to file an appeal to the Higher People's Court.
Guo Song was previously sentenced to four years for rape and was found guilty of shooting four bank guards.

China introduced rules governing direct shipping links with Taiwan on Tuesday.
The new regulations allow only wholly Chinese-owned or Taiwan-owned shipping companies or joint ventures involving Chinese or Taiwanese shipowners to operate between the two sides.
Xinhua news agency reported that Xiamen and Fuzhou would be the first ports opened to direct shipping links with Taiwan.
Taiwan's Nationalist government has banned direct air and shipping links with China since 1949.
Civilian aircraft and vessels have circumvented the ban by stopping in third countries or territories.
Taiwanese businessmen have invested more than $20 billion into China and are eager for direct transport links.
Taiwanese authorities have been reluctant to lift the ban on direct transport links.
The Chinese Ministry of Communications must approve shipping companies wishing to operate routes between the two sides.
The ministry has 45 days to decide on shipping company applications according to the new regulations.
The central bank of Taiwan denied a report about studying how to control capital outflows to China.

China's stock markets are currently overheating.
The People's Daily newspaper warned of a potential crash similar to the Wall Street collapse of 1929.
China's foreign currency B share market in Shanghai rose by about 80 percent between November 11 and December 10.
The Shenzhen stock market increased by about 100 percent before experiencing sharp declines.
The Shanghai B-share market fell by 12.26 percent on a recent Friday.
The Shenzhen stock market dropped by 14.75 percent on the same day.
The Shanghai A-share index decreased by 5.51 percent.
The Shenzhen A-share index declined by 4.84 percent.
The commentary stated that the government would not intervene to support the markets during downturns.
The commentary suggested that bank savings are the safest investment method.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello announced financial reforms on Wednesday.
The reforms are the largest since 1983.
The reforms loosen restrictions on bank and life office mergers and foreign takeovers of banks.
Costello did not allow mergers between Australia's big four banks: Westpac, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ), National Australia Bank (NAB), and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Costello announced the abolition of the 'Six Pillars' policy.
The 'Six Pillars' policy prevented mergers between major banks and two largest pension and life insurance groups.
Costello stated that the Treasurer will retain powers to reject mergers under relevant banking and insurance laws.
Costello indicated that major domestic banks would not be allowed to merge at this time.
Costello announced the end of the outright ban on foreign takeovers of Australian banks.
Costello emphasized that large-scale transfer of Australian ownership of the financial system to foreign hands would be contrary to the national interest.

Australia's anti-monopolies watchdog is examining claims of collusion against the four major banks.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has asked the banks to explain why they cut their mortgage rates by the same amount within hours of each other.
ACCC Chairman Allan Fels stated it was unusual for the banks to all move quickly to cut their rates by the same amount.
Fels mentioned that the ACCC does not claim to have evidence of collusion but is seeking an explanation from the banks.
National Australia Bank, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and Westpac Banking Corp all cut their standard variable mortgage rates by 0.35 percent to 7.2 percent.
The banks made these cuts hours after the Reserve Bank reduced official rates by 0.5 percent to 5.5 percent.
Government and opposition politicians, along with consumer groups, have suggested that the banks colluded to limit the passing on of the official rate cut to customers.
Fels indicated that the commission would request details of any communications between the banks on the day of the rate cuts.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia denied collusion with other major banks and stated it had not discussed interest rates with them.
CBA Managing Director David Murray emphasized that the bank believes in competition and would cooperate fully with the ACCC.

Treasurer Peter Costello announced financial reforms in Australia on Wednesday.
The reforms are the largest since 1983.
The reforms loosen restrictions on bank and life office mergers and foreign takeovers of banks.
Costello did not allow mergers between Australia's big four banks: Westpac, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ), National Australia Bank (NAB), and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Costello warned that foreigners would not be allowed to buy a significant portion of Australia's banking sector.
Costello announced the abolition of the 'Six Pillars' policy.
The 'Six Pillars' policy prevented mergers between major banks and two largest pension and life insurance groups.
The 'Six Pillars' policy was introduced by former Labor treasurer Paul Keating.
Costello's government set up the Wallis Inquiry to reform Labor's policies.
The government decided that mergers among the four major banks will not be permitted at this time.

U.S. Robotics Corp's stock increased on Wednesday due to speculation about a faster analog modem.
U.S. Robotics is based in Skokie, Illinois.
U.S. Robotics announced at an Oppenheimer & Co investors conference that it is exploring new technologies, including higher speed modems.
U.S. Robotics previously stated that it did not believe 33.6 kilobits per second was the fastest speed for modems.
An Oppenheimer analyst noted that the presentation about the faster modem was more detailed than previous discussions.
Oppenheimer analyst Steven Levy mentioned that this was the first time U.S. Robotics discussed the topic with slides.
Rockwell International Corp's semiconductor systems unit plans to demonstrate 56 kilobit transmission capabilities at a trade show in November.
Analysts believe that a modem capable of 56 kilobits would enhance Internet communication over standard telephone lines.
U.S. Robotics holds approximately an 80 percent share of the modem market for online services and a 38 percent share for desktop modems.
U.S. Robotics declined to comment on whether it was close to releasing a faster modem.

The U.S. bank megamergers of 1995 have been completed.
First Bank System Inc announced the acquisition of U.S. Bancorp for nearly $9 billion.
Steven Schroll is a banking analyst at Piper Jaffray.
Schroll stated that 1997 is starting similarly to 1995.
SNL Securities LP reported $12.85 billion in bank and thrift acquisitions announced in 1997.
In 1995, there were $74.4 billion in bank deals.
In 1996, bank deals fell to $46.27 billion.
Regulatory barriers to mergers between banks, insurance companies, and securities firms are likely to be lowered.
Frank Barkocy is an analyst at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
Barkocy noted that the recent deal could lead to increased merger and acquisition activity.

Wallace Computer Services Inc has strong business fundamentals.
Analysts believe a change in the shareholder profile of Wallace Computer Services Inc will protect it from a bid by investor Guy Wyser-Pratte.
Judith Scott is an analyst at Robert W. Baird.
Judith Scott stated that Wallace has created shareholder value.
Moore Corp Ltd abandoned its 13-month takeover campaign in early August.
Martin McDevitt Jr. is an analyst at Cleary Gull Reiland and McDevitt.
Martin McDevitt Jr. noted a substantial change in the profile of the Wallace shareholder base since August 6.
Most of the selling of Wallace stock since early August is attributed to arbitrageurs.
McDevitt believes the current shareholder base is likely composed of long-term investors.
Wyser-Pratte controls a 2.3 percent stake in Wallace and filed proxy materials with the SEC.

Canadian police announced on Wednesday that they laid more charges in a sex scandal involving young boys at Maple Leaf Gardens.
Police filed 50 additional charges of sexual abuse against Gordon Stuckless, 47, a former backstage helper at Maple Leaf Gardens.
Gordon Stuckless now faces a total of 52 charges, including indecent assault, gross indecency, and buggery.
Stuckless and another former employee, John Paul Roby, allegedly lured teenage boys to the arena with free tickets and autographs.
John Paul Roby is currently facing 75 charges of sexual abuse.
Toronto police detective Dave Tredrea stated that the investigation is ongoing.
Police reported that the abuse occurred in the back rooms of the arena, sometimes during hockey games or events.
The scandal may involve up to 90 victims from the late 1960s to early 1990s.
The allegations surfaced after Martin Kruze, 34, came forward with claims of sexual abuse starting when he was 13.
Retired deputy police chief Walter Tyrrell has been appointed to review security at Maple Leaf Gardens.

Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. resumed trading on Wednesday.
Trading volumes overwhelmed the computer system on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Bre-X's stock fell C65 cents to C$3.20 on the TSE on Wednesday.
Trading was stopped in late morning due to heavy order volumes and technical difficulties.
Bre-X had a turnover of 11.7 million shares during the abbreviated trading session.
The stock was halted all day on Monday and resumed trading for 22 minutes on Tuesday.
Bre-X's market value decreased by almost C$3 billion last Thursday.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. revealed that drilling samples from the Busang property showed insignificant amounts of gold.
Bre-X stock continued trading on Nasdaq and other exchanges despite issues on the TSE.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh claimed that tampering with core samples was impossible.

Canada's top securities regulator is probing Bre-X Minerals Ltd for potential breaches of insider trading and disclosure laws.
The Ontario Securities Commission has been investigating Bre-X Minerals since the end of 1996.
The OSC confirmed that the investigation relates to breaches of continuous disclosure requirements or insider trading provisions.
The OSC has not determined if there is enough information to begin formal proceedings against Bre-X.
The investigation is focusing on potential breaches of Ontario's Securities Act.
A group of Canadian Bre-X shareholders launched a class action lawsuit on Thursday.
Bre-X Minerals faces five court actions in the United States.
The Toronto Stock Exchange halted trading of Bre-X shares on Thursday due to heavy order volumes.
A report on Bre-X's assay program confirmed the company's original findings but raised new questions about the gold project.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. revealed that early drilling samples from the Busang gold property showed only tiny amounts of gold.

General Motors Corp. workers ratified a new labour contract.
The United Auto Workers union reported that 85 percent of the workers who voted approved the contract.
The approval margin is the largest in 20 years.
The contract affects more than 386,000 hourly workers at GM, Ford Motor Co., and Chrysler Corp.
Negotiations at GM led to a national strike by the Canadian Auto Workers in October.
Local UAW strikes occurred at two GM plants and extended into November.
GM estimated that the walkouts would reduce its fourth quarter profits by approximately $700 million.
Costs associated with the UAW pact are expected to be around $170 million.
The GM contract follows the pattern set by Ford and Chrysler, including a guarantee to maintain 95 percent employment of its UAW hourly workforce.
The GM pact includes restrictions to prevent the shifting of parts work to outside suppliers.

Ford Motor Co. reported a 2.2 percent decline in U.S. light vehicle sales in November.
The decline in Ford's sales was attributed to a significant drop in car sales, despite gains in truck sales.
General Motors Corp. reported a 12 percent drop in November sales.
Chrysler Corp. reported a 1.4 percent increase in November sales.
Ford sold 290,774 cars and light trucks in November, down from 297,362 a year earlier.
Domestic car sales for Ford fell 11.3 percent to 52,101 units.
Light truck sales for Ford rose 5.7 percent to 175,606 units.
Ford's import car sales fell 48.2 percent to 1,597 units.
Robert Rewey, Ford's group vice president of sales and marketing, stated that the retail market is shifting from cars to light trucks.
Ford's combined sales of the Explorer, Mountaineer, and Expedition sport utility vehicles rose 38 percent to 55,343 units.

General Motors Corp. experienced a 50.8 percent drop in fourth quarter earnings from continuing operations.
Wall Street had anticipated the earnings drop from General Motors Corp.
General Motors Corp. generated strong cash, raising hopes for a strong performance in 1997.
At year-end, General Motors Corp.'s cash and marketable securities exceeded $17 billion.
General Motors Corp.'s cash and marketable securities increased by $2.5 billion from September 30, 1996.
General Motors Corp.'s cash and marketable securities increased by $6.8 billion from a year earlier.
$1 billion of General Motors Corp.'s fourth quarter cash increase was due to a tax refund.
Analysts noted a $1.5 billion increase in cash from operations affected by strikes.
General Motors Corp.'s fourth quarter North American production volume fell by 11.4 percent.
General Motors Corp. reported a $124 million loss in North America for the fourth quarter.

Ford Motor Co announced it would cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant near Liverpool, England.
The job cuts represent almost one third of the Halewood workforce.
The Halewood plant will not build the planned new model of the Escort car, due in 1999.
Production of the new Escort model is likely to transfer to factories in Spain and Germany.
Ford stated that Halewood could become the European source for a planned new vehicle, which is still a concept.
Halewood will continue to produce the current Escort model through 2000.
David Gorman, European vehicle operations manager for Ford, commented on the future of the Halewood plant.
Local MP David Alton reported that Ford indicated the job losses would occur through voluntary redundancy.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000 from a peak of 14,000 in the 1960s.
Workers expressed anger over the job cuts, attributing them to British labour laws and the lack of the European Union's Social Chapter.

Tomkins Plc is a UK conglomerate with businesses in baking and engineering.
Tomkins Plc is expected to see a rise in half-year pretax profits.
Analysts predict six-month profits of around 160 million stg, up from 126.1 million stg the previous year.
The average forecast for the half-year payout is 3.0 pence per share, up from 2.70 pence last time.
Tomkins shares have recently gained following a 'buy' recommendation from Kleinwort Benson analysts.
Tomkins was listed as one of the nine stocks to buy in 1997 by Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Tomkins shares are currently at 278 pence, down two pence.
The group board obtained permission for a buyback of up to 10 percent of its shares in 1995.
Tomkins currently has around 400 million stg in cash.
Analyst Ian Rennardson from Credit Lyonnais stated that the group has not indicated a buyback at the interim stage.

Britain's building sector has shown signs of recovery in the domestic housing market.
Sales in the housing market are increasing.
Housebuilders are expected to benefit from the recovery.
RMC Plc, Redland Plc, and BPB experienced a decline in their share prices.
RMC's shares fell by 36p to 903.5.
Redland's shares closed 5.5p lower at 330.
BPB's shares decreased by 13p to 362.5p.
Blue Circle's shares dropped by 7.5p to 368.
Concerns about the German economy and the rising value of the pound are affecting building material companies.
Germany accounts for up to 40 percent of profits for some building materials firms.

New York state utility regulators approved the $23 billion merger between Nynex Corp. and Bell Atlantic Corp.
The approval is subject to conditions that must be agreed upon by the companies by the end of March.
Consumer groups opposed the merger and criticized the decision as a sellout.
New York was the last state in Nynex's six-state service region to approve the merger.
The merger would create the largest local phone company in the United States, serving customers in 12 Northeastern states and Washington.
John O'Mara, Chairman of the New York State Public Service Commission, stated that improved service quality and tangible benefits for ratepayers are requirements for approval.
O'Mara indicated that there would be no immediate rate reduction but conditions attached to the merger could lead to rate reductions in the future.
Federal regulators are reviewing the merger's competitive implications, which is delaying the process.
Bell Atlantic spokesman Eric Rabe stated that the companies expect the deal to close after April 22.
The combined company must keep major operations in New York state and maintain its headquarters there, as agreed by both companies.

America Online Inc. plans to place advertising on company-sponsored discussion areas.
The company aims to expand its revenue base beyond mainly subscriber fees.
America Online is based in Dulles, Virginia.
The company expects to generate 360 million ad impressions every month from chat rooms.
An analyst estimated that this program could generate $15 million to $25 million in new revenues in 1997.
Impressions are the standard way of measuring the impact of individual ad promotions in the advertising industry.
America Online stock rose $3.75 to $43.75 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bob Pittman is the president of America Online Networks.
Over 70 percent of America Online members engage in chat, logging 1 million hours of chat every day.
Brian Oakes, a Lehman Brothers analyst, estimated that chat rooms account for about 23 percent of online usage time among America Online subscribers.

America Online Inc. plans to launch a national Internet service in Japan in mid-April.
America Online Inc. aims to make Japan its biggest international market within a couple of years.
AOL Chairman Steve Case stated that Japan is a significant market opportunity for AOL.
AOL Japan Inc. is a joint venture involving America Online, Mitsui & Co. Ltd., and Nihon Keizai Shimbun Inc.
America Online owns a 50 percent stake in AOL Japan, Mitsui owns 40 percent, and Nikkei owns 10 percent.
AOL Japan will offer multimedia features not available on other Japanese online services.
Leading online service providers in Japan include Nifty-serve, PCVAN, and ASCIINet.
AOL Japan's service will be provided in the Japanese language.
AOL Japan will charge a monthly fee of 980 Japanese yen for three hours of use.
New members of AOL Japan will receive a 10-hour free trial in the first month.

A top federal regulator urged banks to be more careful in issuing credit cards.
The American Bankers Association reported that late payments by consumers reached a record level at the end of last year.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, late payments jumped to 3.72 percent of credit card accounts.
The 3.72 percent late payment rate is the highest since the American Bankers Association began tracking delinquencies in 1980.
The late payment rate increased from 3.34 percent a year earlier.
Personal bankruptcies are at record levels.
Bank losses from credit card loans are growing.
Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig oversees almost 3,000 nationally chartered banks.
Ludwig stated that there was a 44 percent growth in credit card losses and a 50 percent increase in credit card delinquencies during the past year.
Bank charge-offs on credit cards increased to 6.5 percent in January from 4.7 percent a year earlier.

Ten leading U.S. high-technology companies lobbied in Washington for stronger laws against piracy.
Executives from Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp met with senators, reporters, Vice President Al Gore, and Commerce Secretary William Daley.
The executives presented research showing the software industry significantly contributes to economic growth.
Bill Gates stated that the PC software industry is fast-growing and innovative.
Research for the Business Software Alliance indicated the software industry was worth $102.8 billion in 1996.
The software industry directly employed 619,000 people and paid $36.4 billion in wages in 1996.
An additional 1.4 million American workers were indirectly employed due to the software industry.
The software industry grew at an annual rate of 12.5 percent since 1980, outpacing the U.S. economy.
Piracy cost the software industry $11.2 billion in 1996, with a significant portion occurring in China.
The executives advocated for relaxing export limits on encryption technology to promote software sales.

A new class of financial derivative based on credit risk is growing in popularity.
U.S. banking regulators are assessing complex financial derivatives.
Most derivatives are linked to interest rates or currencies.
Credit derivatives are based on the value of loans, bonds, or other lending vehicles.
William Kroener is the general counsel of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.
Bank regulators issued preliminary guidance to bank examiners concerning credit derivatives in August.
The guidance emphasized that banks should have policies for managing risks from credit derivatives.
Regulators requested banks to clearly list credit derivative activity in their call reports.
Regulators are considering the amount of capital a bank must set aside for its credit derivative portfolio.
Christine Cumming is a senior vice president in the bank supervision group of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

East European markets increased this week, with Poland and Hungary leading in foreign buying.
Warsaw and Budapest reached year-highs during the week.
Romania and Slovenia also experienced significant increases.
Bratislava and Prague saw slight increases but lacked upward momentum.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange achieved three consecutive 33-month highs this week.
Heavy turnover was noted on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
Post-fixing buying on Thursday contributed to another high on Friday.
Analysts predicted a profit-taking correction for the following week.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange has risen 23 percent since December 10.
Analysts expect 16,000 points to provide strong support for the WIG index next week.

The Prague Stock Exchange gained ground on Thursday.
Analysts are not convinced that the bourse's fortunes have turned around.
The rise in the bourse is attributed to thin domestic buying.
The bourse has gained in 15 of the past 16 sessions.
Analysts see little change in market sentiment amid mostly domestic trading.
The PX50 index closed up 0.56 percent at 521.1 on Thursday.
The bourse is about nine percent higher than its low in mid-November.
The Czech market has been plagued by poor legislation affecting minority shareholders.
The Securities Registry is bound by law to provide services related to securities transactions.
Local brokers prefer the Securities Registry for its privacy and faster settlement process.

Czech trading firms experienced a trade deficit that nearly doubled year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997.
Analysts stated that the trade deficit figures were in line with forecasts.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released a survey indicating the trade deficit for the quarter should rise to about 45 billion crowns.
The trade deficit for the first quarter of 1996 was 27.1 billion crowns.
Martin Kupka, an economist at Patria Finance, predicted that the deficit situation would gradually worsen throughout the year.
The CSU forecasted the overall 1997 trade deficit to rise to between 211-219 billion crowns.
The CSU reported a record trade deficit of 160.3 billion crowns in the previous year.
The survey conducted by the CSU included estimates from firms that accounted for 20 percent of all import business and 36 percent of exports last year.
A total of 170 firms were polled in the CSU survey, with a 67 percent response rate.
Total imports in the first quarter of 1996 were 174.3 billion crowns.

Hammerson Plc's chief executive is Ron Spinney.
Ron Spinney expects the British market to perform well over the next two years.
Hammerson Plc announced a 21.3 percent rise in pre-tax profit for 1996 to 70.0 million stg.
The pre-tax profit for 1995 was 57.7 million stg.
Net asset value (NAV) per share rose 3.2 percent to 388 pence from 376 pence.
Hammerson turned over 15 percent of its portfolio in the past year.
Hammerson invested 50 million stg on improving existing properties.
Hammerson embarked on an 800 million stg development programme.
Hammerson plans to spend around 115 million stg on its existing portfolio and developments.
Hammerson's gearing is currently 58 percent.

Members of the Woolwich voted to change its mutual status to a publicly listed bank.
The vote was held during a special general meeting.
More than 95 percent of savers and borrowers who voted approved the proposals.
Individual members will receive an average share windfall of 1,200 pounds.
The handout will include at least 450 shares to around 2.57 million qualifying members and pensioners.
Approximately 1,200 members attended the meeting, with many expressing dissatisfaction with the conversion.
The vote was largely decided by a postal vote.
Woolwich Plc plans to offer a full range of personal financial services after its flotation.
The flotation is expected to occur in July and is valued at 3.0 billion pounds.
The Woolwich aims to expand into pensions and other financial areas, potentially through friendly mergers.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is involved in a probe into alleged irregularities in three Morgan Grenfell investment funds.
The investigation has extended beyond Britain to include overseas elements.
Holding companies listed in Luxembourg are being investigated as part of the inquiry.
The SFO is in contact with Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
IMRO will share any relevant material with the SFO.
The SFO investigates and prosecutes major financial crimes in the City of London.
A senior SFO lawyer has been briefed by IMRO regarding the investigation.
Overseas authorities in the U.S., Luxembourg, and Switzerland are involved in the investigation.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell reported that nearly eight percent of the suspended funds were redeemed after they resumed trading.
IMRO's probe into Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) has led to the suspension of two fund managers.

Residents of a town in Xinjiang, China, returned to work on Wednesday after the Lunar New Year holiday.
Officials vowed to address separatism following a riot that resulted in 10 deaths.
Zhang Youlian is the deputy director of the foreign affairs office of the Yili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture.
Zhang Youlian stated that there is a resolve to deal with ethnic separatist elements.
Police arrested between 200 and 300 people in the crackdown after the riot.
About 1,000 Uighurs participated in a riot in Yining, Yili prefecture.
The riot was one of the largest and most violent demonstrations for independence in Xinjiang in several years.
The riot left 10 people dead and 144 wounded, with all victims being Han Chinese.
132 of the wounded were civilians and 12 were members of the paramilitary armed police.
Authorities had sealed off the town but planned to reopen the airport on Friday.

China is considering restrictions on foreign investment in textiles and garments.
Li Qiming is the director of the State Statistical Bureau's department of industry and transportation statistics.
Li Qiming stated that the production capacity of some traditional industries in China is excessive.
Li Qiming mentioned that losses of state enterprises in textiles and garments exceed the national average.
China plans to curb textile output and unnecessary expansion in the industry to reduce losses in the state sector.
China has set a target to phase out obsolete textile equipment, including 10 million cotton spindles.
In 1995, 429 state textile enterprises reported losses of more than five million yuan each.
The combined losses of these state textile enterprises reached 5.21 billion yuan in 1995.
A survey conducted by the bureau showed that foreign investment is concentrated mainly in electronics, telecommunications, textiles, garments, and food processing.
By the end of 1995, there were 59,311 wholly foreign-owned and Sino-foreign joint ventures in China.

Chinese police arrested Abudu Heilili, the suspected ringleader of a riot in Xinjiang.
The riot occurred last week and resulted in at least 10 deaths and 144 injuries.
Abudu Heilili is 29 years old and belongs to the Uighur ethnic minority.
Heilili was in police custody and under interrogation following the riot.
Heilili was unemployed and had previously led a less violent anti-Chinese demonstration in August 1995.
Heilili was released after the 1995 demonstration following 'ideological education'.
Police detained 200 to 300 people after last week's riot.
The death toll from the riot could rise, with up to seven people reported missing.
Of the injured, 132 were civilians and 12 were members of the People's Armed Police.
Authorities issued circulars warning of severe punishment for the rioters and aimed to combat separatism.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia's (CBA) home loan portfolio has shown solid growth.
CBA's profit outlook has improved slightly due to this growth.
CBA is expected to report a profit rise of about one percent for the six months to December 31.
CBA has warned since early 1996 that margin pressure would lead to flat profits for the year to June 30.
Some analysts believe CBA has been more optimistic in recent months.
Analysts forecast a net profit before abnormals for CBA of between A$535 million and A$560 million for the six months.
CBA's home loan portfolio grew 10.3 percent to A$28.8 billion in the year to November.
Home lending growth by all banks rose 7.5 percent during the same period.
CBA's share of home lending by banks increased to 22.3 percent from 21.7 percent over the year.
Analysts expect CBA's bad debts and provisioning to remain stable and not negatively impact profits.

The federal government is expected to release the Wallis Inquiry's report into Australia's financial system later this week.
The Wallis Inquiry was set up in June last year and is chaired by businessman Stan Wallis.
The Inquiry released a 415-page discussion paper in late November that canvassed various options for reform.
The Inquiry's report was presented to the government last month.
The report will make recommendations about mergers, foreign investment, ownership of banks, prudential regulation, and deposit insurance.
The report will address whether the government should abandon the current 'Six Pillars' policy that stops mergers between the four major banks and two major life insurance and superannuation groups.
The six pillars include Westpac Banking Corp, National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society.
The report will consider whether the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Treasurer should continue to have the power to reject or approve a bank merger.
The report will evaluate whether the current ban on foreign takeovers of the big four banks should be scrapped.
The report will assess whether to combine the functions of the four regulatory bodies into a single body for prudential regulation and consumer protection.

The Seven Network Ltd is expected to report a 25-30 percent higher pre-abnormal annual net profit on Monday.
Analysts believe the profit rise may disguise a second half profit slowdown.
A Sydney analyst stated that second half sales growth is likely to be modest due to competition from the Ten Network and Nine Network.
The Seven Network had the Australian TV rights to the Atlanta Olympic Games.
The median forecast for Seven's pre-abnormals net profit for the year to June 30 is A$114 million.
Forecasts for Seven's net profit range from A$105 million to A$120.7 million.
The A$114 million forecast compares with A$88.5 million posted in 1994/95.
The 1994/95 figure was negatively impacted by a bungle over discounted advertising rates costing Seven A$20-30 million.
Seven managing director Gary Rice expected a better second half in 1995/96 than the second half of 1994/95.
Seven expects advertising sales in 1995/96 to be six to seven percent higher for the year.

Mercury Finance Co. announced it is suspending payment of a previously announced dividend.
The company is attempting to secure short-term financing as it accumulates debt.
Mercury Finance Co. has been unable to refinance $61 million in commercial paper that matured.
An additional $127 million in debt is due between Thursday and February 14.
The company has been in violation of certain loan covenants since last week.
Mercury Finance Co. was unable to pay $17 million in commercial debt.
The company announced accounting irregularities that resulted in an overstatement of earnings by about $90 million.
The accounting misstatements were linked to unauthorized entries by former controller James Doyle.
Doyle's lawyer has accused Mercury Finance Co. of a 'charade' and stated that Doyle is cooperating with federal authorities.
FBI agents served a search warrant seeking financial records from Mercury Finance Co.

U.S. retailers are expected to post sales gains in the single digits for March.
Sales at low-end discount stores are contributing to the expected sales gains.
Department store performance was nearly flat compared with a year ago.
Michael Niemira is an analyst at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
Niemira expects comparable-store sales to be up about 5 percent or slightly less.
An early Easter could depress sales at stores that were closed on the holiday.
Winter storms in much of the northern part of the nation may have held sales back.
William Armstrong is an analyst at Fahnestock & Co. Inc.
Armstrong expects overall retail sales for March to increase by 2 percent to 4 percent.
J.C. Penney Co. Inc. reported a 3.7 percent decline in comparable-store sales in March.

Retailers in the nation are expected to post modest sales gains for February.
Analysts predict a rise of about 4 percent in same-store sales for February.
Warm weather had a mixed impact on retail sales results.
Sales of apparel increased due to warm weather in the Northeast.
Sales in some hardline areas were depressed by warm weather.
Carson Pirie Scott & Co. reported an 8.2 percent rise in same-store sales for February.
Michael Niemira, an analyst at Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, suggested that Carson's strong sales might indicate positive trends for smaller retailers.
Sears, Roebuck and Co. is expected to have sales gains of about 2 percent to 4 percent.
Merrill Lynch analysts noted that Sears' sales were affected by its automotive business and weak performance in hard lines.
J.C. Penney Co. is expected to exceed the average with same-store sales gains of about 9 percent.

Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. has extended its review of an Indonesian gold mining project until June 30.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. announced the extension on Wednesday.
Freeport is a partner in the Busang project in Indonesia.
Freeport requested the extension to consider the findings of the Strathcona audit.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. is expected to deliver a report on Busang to Bre-X on Thursday or Friday.
Bre-X plans to issue a press release on the report before North American financial markets open on Monday.
Freeport-McMoRan's preliminary tests found 'insignificant' amounts of gold at Busang on March 26.
Bre-X estimates that Busang contains about 71 million ounces of gold.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion from the company's market value last month.
Bre-X shares fell 32 cents Canadian to C$3.48 in heavy trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Canadians are experiencing a winter of dismay related to ice hockey.
Ice hockey in Canada is facing issues such as sex scandals, fraud trials, and a decline in team performance.
This year marks the 25th anniversary of Canada's victory in the 1972 Summit Series against the Soviet Union.
Paul Henderson scored the winning goal in the final game of the 1972 Summit Series.
There are concerns that Canada is losing its grip on ice hockey.
The current season began with Canada losing to the United States in the final of the inaugural World Cup of Hockey.
Computer-enhanced pucks and NHL expansion into U.S. markets are causing concern among hockey purists.
A sex scandal involving young boys has emerged at Maple Leaf Gardens, home of the Toronto Maple Leafs.
Two employees of Maple Leaf Gardens have been charged in connection with a pedophile ring involving up to 60 victims.
Graham James, a junior hockey coach, pleaded guilty to sexually assaulting two players in the 1980s.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is based in Calgary, Alberta.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. reported a gold discovery at the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Doubts about the Busang deposit and the death of chief geologist Michael de Guzman led to a decline in Bre-X's stock.
Shares of Bre-X were halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange after a report indicated the Busang deposit was smaller than previously estimated.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. is a partner in the Busang project.
Freeport stated that its due diligence on the Busang site was not complete.
Bre-X shares fell to a 52-week low of C$14.25 during trading.
Bre-X closed down C$2.25 at C$15.20 on 9 million shares traded.
Michael de Guzman, the chief geologist of Bre-X, died after falling from a helicopter in Indonesia.
Analysts expect rumors about the Busang deposit to continue until Freeport completes its review.

Chrysler Corp. has developed a new method to extract hydrogen from gasoline.
This method could reduce the timeline for introducing super-efficient electric cars powered by fuel cells by 10 years.
Fuel cells generate electricity through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen, using a platinum catalyst.
Chrysler's fuel cell system can extract hydrogen from normal gasoline.
The system is expected to provide a 50 percent increase in fuel efficiency over conventional internal combustion engines.
Francois Castaing, Chrysler's vice president of vehicle engineering, stated that hydrogen needs to be processed from gasoline on-board vehicles.
Castaing noted that hydrogen is not a practical fuel choice today due to a lack of filling stations.
The proposed system would allow drivers to refuel at normal gasoline stations, although the car would have a smaller tank.
The on-board refinery system is expected to cost about $30,000, which is 10 times more than a conventional internal combustion engine.
Chrysler aims to have a working test vehicle within three years and estimates that fuel cells could become commercially viable by 2010 to 2015.

U.S. sales of General Motors Corp. cars and trucks in November dropped nearly 12 percent from a year ago.
Total U.S. vehicle sales for General Motors in November fell to 336,815 from 382,372 a year earlier.
GM car sales decreased by 22.5 percent to 179,150 units.
Total truck sales rose 4.2 percent to 157,665 units despite strike-related production losses.
Walkouts by the United Auto Workers and Canadian Auto Workers unions reduced the availability of several GM vehicle models.
Sales of key high-volume models that GM is replacing were down significantly due to model changeovers.
Lincoln Merrihew, an auto analyst with DRI/McGraw-Hill, stated that GM's car market share is expected to struggle for about six months.
Production of the Chevrolet Corsica and Beretta compact cars was recently ended, resulting in a sales drop of 89 percent to 1,494 units.
Chevrolet, GM's largest division, had November sales of 169,110, a drop of more than 13 percent from 194,973.
For the first 11 months of 1996, GM dealers sold 4,447,147 total vehicles, down 1.7 percent from the same period of 1995.

The United Auto Workers union has chosen Ford Motor Co. to lead labor contract negotiations with the Big Three U.S. automakers for the second consecutive time.
UAW vice president Ernest Lofton notified Ford executives of the decision on Tuesday.
The union is not viewing Ford as a traditional 'strike target' in the negotiations.
Ford is the lead company in resolving the UAW's 1996 negotiations.
The selection of Ford will allow it to negotiate an agreement that will serve as a pattern for General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp.
Contracts covering nearly 400,000 U.S. hourly workers at Ford, General Motors, and Chrysler expire on September 14.
Ford faces the threat of a national strike if it fails to reach an agreement before the contract expiration.
Ford spokesman Jon Harmon stated that the company is negotiating with the UAW at both the subcommittee level and the main table.
Ford employs about 104,000 UAW members and negotiated the current pact in 1993.
The UAW's top priorities in the 1996 negotiations include improved job security and restrictions on shifting work to lower-cost suppliers.

UK defence to industrial giant GEC Plc announced potential job cuts of up to 1,000 at its two newly-acquired businesses.
The job losses will primarily affect AG Power Transmission and Distribution and Hazeltine Corp of the U.S.
The expected cost of the job cuts is 45 million stg of a total 160 million charge.
An additional 50 million of the total charge relates to asset write-downs at two other units.
Finance director David Newlands did not disclose the names of the two companies with reduced asset values.
Newlands stated that the asset write-downs were necessary for the disposal of those companies.
Newlands mentioned that the first sale of companies marked for disposal is expected to occur before Christmas.
The remaining portion of the 160 million charge relates to restructuring within the remaining firms.
Newlands indicated that George Simpson, the successor to former managing director Lord Weinstock, began his role in September.
GEC reported a decline in half-year profits to 261 million stg from 402 million stg after accounting for the 160 million charge.

Wickes Plc is a British do-it-yourself retailer.
Wickes Plc's former bosses are being investigated for fraud.
Wickes Plc warned it faced receivership unless investors supported its financial restructuring.
The financial restructuring includes a 53 million pound rights issue.
Accounting irregularities dating back five years were discovered at Wickes Plc.
Wickes Plc announced a major refinancing plan that includes a cash call and possible sale of its continental business.
Wickes chairman Michael von Brentano stated that a vote against the plans could lead to receivership.
The refinancing plan includes a capital reduction of 100 million pounds and new banking facilities of 52 million pounds.
Wickes Plc expects to make a loss before tax in 1996 of not more than 56 million pounds.
Wickes Plc will not pay an interim dividend in 1996 or 1997, but may pay a final dividend in 1997.

Talks between the British and U.S. governments on an open skies pact were postponed for two weeks due to the illness of a senior British negotiator.
The talks were scheduled to begin in Washington with representatives from both governments and main transatlantic carriers.
A spokesman for the British government confirmed that the lead official is in hospital and the meeting has been cancelled.
The European Commission began a separate series of private hearings in Brussels regarding the proposed British Airways and American Airlines alliance.
The British Airways and American Airlines alliance is conditional on the open skies pact being finalized.
British and U.S. carriers expressed regret over the delay of the Anglo-U.S. talks.
Sources indicated that the postponed talks were not expected to result in a final deal.
Scott Yohe, senior vice-president of government affairs at Delta Air Lines Inc, stated that full agreement was not possible in the current round of talks.
The British government wants to link the open skies talks with the BA/AA alliance, while the U.S. prefers to keep them as separate issues.
Britain is awaiting a final verdict from the Office of Fair Trading regarding the BA/AA alliance, particularly concerning the divestment of 168 landing slots at Heathrow airport.

MCI Communications Corp. reported flat quarterly earnings despite a rise in revenues.
MCI earned $295 million, or 42 cents a share, in the first quarter.
MCI's earnings were unchanged from a year ago and in line with analysts' consensus estimates.
Revenues grew 8.7 percent to $4.9 billion from $4.1 billion.
Gerald Taylor, chief executive of MCI, stated that the company demonstrates strong overall revenue growth and profits.
MCI and British Telecom announced a merger valued at $23 billion.
The merger is expected to create the world's second-largest telecommunications group.
The deal is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close in the fall.
Long-distance revenues rose 8.2 percent to $4.4 billion from $4.1 billion.
MCI expects revenue and traffic growth rates to slow in coming quarters.

International Business Machines Corp. announced a 2-for-1 stock split.
The stock split was approved by IBM's board and is subject to shareholder approval for an increase in authorized shares.
The stock split will double the number of shares traded and halve the stock's price.
Industry analysts believe the stock split provides only a temporary boost unless IBM can demonstrate growth in its core computer business.
Nomura Securities analyst Daniel Ries stated that IBM's management must show sustained growth for the stock to recover.
IBM's stock price rose by $5 to $150.75 following the announcement of the split.
IBM's stock is included in the Dow Jones industrial average and is widely held by individual and institutional investors.
The stock split may reduce the psychological focus on IBM's previous record high of $175 set in 1987.
Soundview Financial analyst Gary Helmig described the stock split as not significant, stating it primarily increases daily share volume.
Analysts noted that the split may make IBM shares more affordable for smaller investors.

WavePhore Inc unveiled a service that broadcasts data to home personal computers via television signals.
The service is called WaveTop and allows users to bypass bottlenecks in the Internet.
WaveTop will broadcast entertainment and information programming nationwide through TV signals.
The service aims to avoid clogged phone lines and overstrained computer networks that slow Internet connections.
Sandy Goldman is the vice president of WavePhore's consumer unit.
Initially, WaveTop will carry stereo broadcasts of a music radio station, real-time news, educational programs for children, and new software to home PCs.
WaveTop will begin U.S. operations in September.
WaveTop will be the first wireless data broadcast medium delivering audio, video, software, and real-time data to home PCs.
The system will be free to consumers who own a broadcast-ready personal computer equipped with a TV tuner.
WavePhore has a pact with the Public Broadcasting Service's 250 local stations to broadcast via an unused portion of their signals.

A coalition of corporations lobbied on Capitol Hill for relaxed export restrictions on computer encoding technology.
The Senate Commerce Committee will mark-up the Promotion of Commerce Online in the Digital Era Act of 1996, known as Pro-CODE.
The Pro-CODE bill aims to abolish most export restrictions on encryption technology.
Under current law, only weak encryption programs created in the United States can be sold abroad.
Domestic use of encryption is not regulated in the United States.
High-tech industry companies claim they are losing business to foreign competitors not bound by U.S. export restrictions.
Multinational companies in other industries state that export restrictions hinder their ability to conduct business overseas.
Gregory Garcia, director of international trade affairs for the American Electronics Association, stated that the current situation is unacceptable.
The Pro-CODE bill has bipartisan support in the Commerce Committee and is sponsored by Senators Conrad Burns and Pat Leahy.
The Clinton administration opposes the Pro-CODE bill, citing concerns about law enforcement and intelligence operations.

Congress is reviving the debate over encryption export policy this week.
Encryption has become a critical component of electronic commerce and global communications on the Internet.
The Clinton administration has a new policy allowing freer export of encryption products.
The new policy allows the export of stronger encryption than previously allowed.
The new policy requires companies to incorporate features allowing the government to access software keys within two years.
The government claims it needs the ability to crack strong encryption to catch criminals and terrorists.
Most high-tech companies are frustrated with the new policy and want to export very strong encryption without government access features.
Privacy advocates oppose the current Clinton policy, arguing it gives too much power to the government.
The Senate Commerce Committee will hear testimony on two bills to remove almost all export restrictions.
Industry representatives and privacy advocates will testify at the hearings.

The Clinton administration has developed a plan to reform U.S. banking laws.
The administration will announce its positions in the coming weeks.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will present the plan at a House Banking Committee hearing on June 3.
Under Secretary John Hawke is a key architect of the administration's plan.
Hawke is scheduled to speak on Wednesday regarding the administration's stance on banking and commerce.
There is general agreement in Congress and the finance industry about removing barriers between banking, securities, and insurance.
There is disagreement about allowing banks to merge with securities and other firms.
The administration's position has changed over the past several months.
A task force initially recommended eliminating all barriers between financial sectors.
The administration is now said to favor allowing limited combinations of financial and non-financial activities.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus supports the creation of an independent market regulator.
Analysts believe that more than just the creation of a regulator is needed to revive confidence in the Prague bourse.
Klaus stated that the Czech bourse is moving towards becoming a normal market after its creation under the mass voucher privatisation programme of 1992-95.
Klaus acknowledged that the transition to a normal market would happen gradually.
Analysts and traders indicated that concrete results are necessary to attract investors back to the market.
Jan Sykora, a broker at Wood and Company, commented that the government's recognition of the problem is a positive trend.
Sykora noted that confidence in the Czech market has been significantly reduced, particularly among foreign investors.
The Prague Stock Exchange has experienced a decline, losing about 20 percent since the beginning of September due to a selloff by foreign investors.
Radim Bajgar of ING Barings described Klaus' comments as positive but emphasized that results are essential for the market.
There is criticism regarding the lack of transparency in Czech markets, especially concerning the Securities Centre's failure to provide detailed price information.

Britain's Bass plc has increased its stake in Pivovar Radegast a.s. to 30.07 percent.
Jan Sikora is the Director of Radegast.
Bass raised its stake in Radegast by about 10 percent.
The source of the stake purchase was not disclosed by Sikora.
CTK news agency reported that Bass purchased 9.97 percent of Radegast from Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Praha.
Raiffeisen and Bass officials could not confirm the CTK report.
Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. is Radegast's largest shareholder with a 34 percent stake.
A fund managed by Ceska Pojistovna holds a 30 percent stake in Radegast.
In July, Bass acquired an initial 20 percent stake in Radegast.
Radegast posted a gross profit of 281.5 million crowns over the first nine months of 1996.

The Prague Stock Exchange reached a year-high on Thursday.
The rise was attributed to strong gains in blue chip stocks.
Analysts noted that bullish sentiment was limited by low liquidity and low foreign investor interest.
SPT Telecom and CEZ are the two most-capitalised issues on the exchange.
SPT Telecom and CEZ together account for over one-third of the PX50 index.
Both SPT Telecom and CEZ reached 52-week highs on Thursday.
The PX50 index increased by 1.1 percent to 586.5.
SPT Telecom shares rose by 85 crowns to 3,660.
CEZ shares increased by 34 crowns to 1,193.
The PSE index has gained 8.7 percent in 1997.

Premier Farnell criticized BZW over a profits warning.
Howard Poulson is the chief executive of Premier Farnell.
Poulson suggested that BZW mishandled a profits warning.
The criticism is damaging to BZW in the short term.
A banking analyst stated that problems with client relationships are common.
BZW is part of Barclays Plc, a British banking giant.
BZW is facing scrutiny from the Takeover Panel regarding its role in a takeover defense for Northern Electric.
The Takeover Panel is investigating a late disclosure of a fee clause by BZW.
The fee issue led to an extension of CE Electric's offer for Northern Electric.
Barclays's chairman Andrew Buxton expressed confidence in BZW's ability to recover from setbacks.

Hambro Countrywide Plc is a British estate agency and financial products group.
The company reported a pre-tax profit of 30.8 million pounds for 1996, recovering from a pre-tax loss of 3.9 million pounds in 1995.
Managing director Harry Hill stated that the company anticipates further growth.
Hill noted that the British housing market is improving, with regional differences in performance.
London and the south east are experiencing faster growth compared to other areas.
Hill does not believe that housing prices will rise unsustainably.
He mentioned that there is significant momentum in the housing market expected to sustain through this year and next.
Hambro Countrywide is 52 percent owned by British merchant bank Hambros Plc.
The company acquired Faron Sutaria & Co for 7.45 million pounds, which has five branches in London.
Hill indicated that the acquisition would allow for additional revenue through mortgages and financial services.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is involved in a probe into alleged irregularities at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
MGAM is the funds arm of Deutsche Bank's UK-based investment bank.
The SFO is in contact with the British investment watchdog IMRO.
IMRO will share any relevant material with the SFO.
The SFO investigates and prosecutes major financial crimes in the City of London.
IMRO's probe into MGAM has led to the suspension of two fund managers.
Trading was briefly halted in three MGAM funds, which have around 90,000 small investors.
Trading in the three funds resumed after a £180 million ($280 million) bail-out by Deutsche Bank.
The investigation is focusing on links between suspended fund manager Peter Young and Fiba Nordic Securities.
Fiba Nordic Securities has been a broker and valuer for funds managed by MGAM.

A survey published in Beijing indicated that most Chinese have not forgiven Japanese atrocities from World War Two.
The survey was conducted by the official China Youth Daily in December and involved 15,000 people nationwide.
99.4 percent of respondents believed young Chinese should remember Japan's occupation of China from 1931 to 1945.
More than 97 percent of the respondents were under 40 years old.
According to Beijing, 35 million Chinese were killed or wounded by Japanese troops during the occupation.
81.3 percent of respondents associated Japan with the Rape of Nanjing.
Japanese troops entered Nanjing in 1937 and committed acts of rape and massacre, resulting in up to 250,000 Chinese deaths.
More than 97 percent of respondents opposed attempts by Japanese officials to downplay wartime atrocities.
94.9 percent of respondents opposed Japan's membership in the United Nations Security Council.
85.1 percent believed Japan aimed to become a military superpower, and 70.7 percent viewed Japan as a new threat to peace in Asia.

China Jialing Industrial Co Ltd is a motorcycle manufacturer founded by the military.
The Chinese government holds a 75 percent stake in China Jialing Industrial Co Ltd.
Jialing was the largest motorcycle manufacturer in China as of the mid-1990s.
Jialing began producing civilian products in 1979.
Market competition increased significantly for Jialing in 1994 and 1995.
Jialing's sales dropped from 4.6 billion yuan in 1995 to 3.5 billion yuan in 1996.
After-tax profits for Jialing fell from 460 million yuan in 1995 to 270 million yuan in 1996.
China has approximately 300 motorcycle plants with a total annual production capacity of 20 million units.
Only 10 motorcycle manufacturers in China produce more than 100,000 units annually.
China produced 7.83 million motorcycles in 1995 but sold only 6.1 million.

China denied that its worsening pollution is a threat to the world environment.
China accused developed countries of fabricating the idea of a 'China environmental threat' to monopolize global resources.
The official China Daily described the 'China environmental threat' theory as a rumor and sensationalism.
China claimed it has done more to clean up its environment than developed countries during their initial stages of industrialization.
China announced plans to spend up to 320 billion yuan ($38.6 billion) over the next five years to curb pollution.
As of last November, China had shut down almost 57,000 small polluting factories to limit environmental damage.
Most of the closed factories produced paper, fertilizers, electroplates, or extracted sulfur.
More than 20,000 environment officials were deployed across China to inspect factories and close down polluting units.
China stated that developed countries should bear the major responsibility for the current state of world environmental pollution.
China's annual per capita income was reported to be $400, and it is committed to protecting the environment.

Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA) is an Australian-based soft drink bottler.
CCA announced it had settled the final details of a share swap deal with San Miguel Corp of the Philippines.
The deal aims to create the world's second largest Coca-Cola bottler.
CCA originally announced the deal in April.
Some San Miguel shareholders protested the deal, claiming it would limit their boardroom influence and undervalue cashflows.
CCA confirmed the initial terms of the deal, which involve CCA buying San Miguel's stake in a soft drink bottling joint venture in exchange for a 25 percent stake in CCA.
The Coca-Cola Co, CCA's parent group, will see its shareholding in CCA diluted from 36 percent to 33 percent.
The deal is valued at A$3.7 billion (US$2.8 billion) and will result in annual sales of almost A$4 billion.
The number of San Miguel representatives on the CCA board will increase from three to four.
CCA's shares initially rose by 62 cents to A$16.02 following the confirmation of the deal.

The consortium building the 2000 Olympic Stadium in Sydney has sought permission from the International Olympic Committee to sell Games tickets overseas.
The Stadium Australia group aims to raise A$364.4 million (US$282.4 million) by selling packages of Olympic tickets, equity, and stadium memberships.
The group has struggled to find local buyers for its financing scheme.
The underwriters have extended their deadline for the Olympic float due to a lack of local buyers for the 34,400 packages.
Each package sells for A$10,000.
Stadium Australia wants to sell the ticket component of the package separately to overseas buyers.
The underwriters must fund the project regardless of whether all the packages are sold.
The stadium is due to open in 1999 at a cost of A$660 million.
Each 'Gold' package includes one seat at each of the stadium sessions during the Olympics, a seat at most sporting events at the stadium until 2029, and 1,000 shares in the Stadium company.
City brokers reported that only about one third of the packages had been sold.

The Australian government ordered Canwest Global Communications Corp to reduce its stake in the Ten television network.
The order reflects the Australian government's opposition to more foreign ownership of local media.
Treasurer Peter Costello ruled that Canwest must cut its stake from 76 percent back to 57.5 percent.
Canwest raised its stake earlier in the year through associated local companies.
A government authority stated that the increased ownership broke foreign control rules.
Prime Minister John Howard expressed that he does not want foreign investment in Australian media to increase.
The Australian government is reviewing cross-media ownership rules set by the former Labor government.
The government is expected to drop cross-media ownership rules, allowing Kerry Packer to launch a takeover bid for John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
Howard stated that a proposal by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd to increase its Australian television holdings collapsed.
Kerry Stokes accused Howard of favoring Packer in his review of media laws.

Reliance Acceptance Corp borrowed from its bank credit lines.
The short-term commercial debt market has been closed to sub-prime lenders for most of the week.
Howard Silverman is the chairman of Reliance Acceptance Corp.
Reliance is the auto lending unit of Cole Taylor Financial Group Inc.
Sub-prime lenders have had trouble securing commercial debt due to issues with Mercury Finance Co and another firm.
Mercury Finance Co overstated its earnings by about $90 million over the last four years.
Mercury Finance Co is currently in default and negotiating with its lenders for short-term financing.
