Jayhawk Acceptance Corp may have to file for reorganization under the U.S. Bankruptcy code.
Sub-prime lenders use commercial debt with maturities of 270 days or less to fund purchases of loans from auto dealers.
Reliance's bank debt costs about 200 basis points more than commercial debt.

Mosinee Paper Corp expects capital expenses to double in 1997.
Mosinee Paper Corp plans to spend about $40 million in 1997.
Daniel Olvey is the chief executive of Mosinee Paper Corp.
In recent years, Mosinee Paper Corp has spent about half of $40 million on capital expenses.
Mosinee Paper Corp is adding a large number of paper-converting lines at its Bay West commercial towel and tissue unit.
Mosinee Paper Corp paid down $31 million in debt in 1996.
About 55 percent of Mosinee Paper Corp's $314.5 million in revenues came from specialty paper in 1996.
Daniel Olvey expects towel and tissue to account for more than 50 percent of revenues in the next couple of years.
Mosinee Paper Corp is adding about 30 percent capacity to its Bay West towel paper converting plant.
Mosinee Paper Corp produces about 99,000 tons of towel and tissue each year from 140,000 tons of waste paper.

FBI agents searched the headquarters of Mercury Finance Co. on Monday.
Mercury Finance Co. announced a change in leadership after revealing bookkeeping problems.
The company overstated its earnings by millions of dollars due to these bookkeeping issues.
William Brandt Jr. was named president and chief executive officer of Mercury Finance Co.
Brandt replaced John Brincat, who resigned but remains an employee and board member.
FBI agents arrived at Mercury's headquarters in Lake Forest, Illinois, with a search warrant.
The FBI was seeking financial records during the search.
Mercury stated it was cooperating fully with the FBI's investigation.
The company discovered bookkeeping problems that led to a $90 million overstatement of earnings over four years.
The misstatements were attributed to unauthorized entries by former controller James Doyle, who was dismissed.

Toronto is Canada's biggest city.
A citizens' revolt has emerged against Ontario's ruling Conservatives due to proposed changes in Toronto.
Ontario's Conservative Premier is Mike Harris.
Mike Harris proposes merging Toronto and six neighbouring municipalities into a single 'megacity' of 2.4 million people.
The new 'megacity' would represent about eight percent of Canada's population of 30 million.
Harris plans to change how public services are delivered and funded.
Opponents of the merger fear it will increase taxes and lead to urban decay.
Toronto Mayor Barbara Hall stated that government is elected by the people for the people.
A recent referendum showed that residents voted three to one against the merger, but the vote was not binding.
High-profile Canadian figures, including Norman Jewison, Norman Seagram, and Margaret Atwood, oppose the merger plan.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. stated that the Busang gold mystery may be solved by late next week.
Bre-X reported that Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. is expected to issue an interim report on its findings by the end of next week.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. reported preliminary tests found 'insignificant' amounts of gold on March 26.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion or 80 percent of the company's stock market value.
Investors are awaiting Strathcona's findings regarding the Busang project.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh stated that a press release will be issued upon receiving and reviewing the interim report.
Confusion over Bre-X's announcement led to heavy selling on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Bre-X shares fell to a session low of C$2.50 but recovered to finish down C35 cents at C$3.25 on 8.9 million shares.
Freeport's annual meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, April 29 in New Orleans.
Bre-X holds a 45 percent stake in Busang, Freeport holds 15 percent, the Indonesian government holds 10 percent, and local companies hold the remaining 30 percent.

Barrick Gold Corp is the world's second largest gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp stated that Indonesia and Canada's mining sectors are innocent casualties of the Busang gold controversy.
Peter Munk is the chairman of Barrick Gold Corp.
Peter Munk was a former bidder for Busang.
The Bre-X Minerals Ltd saga has tarnished the reputations of Indonesia and Canada among foreign investors.
Peter Munk described the Busang affair as creating backlash.
Munk stated that the success of other Canadian mining companies should not be affected by the controversy surrounding one junior gold prospector.
Munk claimed that the Canadian mining industry is second to none.
Munk's comment about a 'rogue' operation did not imply that he believed there was no gold at Busang.
Bre-X has estimated that the Busang site contains about 71 million ounces of gold.

General Motors Corp. announced changes to its marketing organization.
GM will replace the heads of its Buick and Cadillac divisions.
Buick and Cadillac divisions have experienced slow sales in recent years.
John Grettenberger, Cadillac General Manager, and Ed Mertz, Buick General Manager, will depart on February 1.
The departures of Grettenberger and Mertz will increase the number of GM division chiefs who have left in the past year to four.
John Rock, Oldsmobile General Manager, announced his retirement effective at year-end.
James Perkins retired as Chevrolet General Manager earlier this year.
John Middlebrook succeeded Perkins as Chevrolet General Manager.
GM is reducing the power and independence of its divisions to focus on its brands.
GM plans to move division staffs to its new corporate headquarters at Detroit's riverfront Renaissance Centre.

Chrysler Corp. reported better-than-expected fourth quarter earnings due to strong sales of light trucks.
Chrysler's net income for the fourth quarter was $807 million, or $1.12 per share, after $279 million in charges.
Excluding special charges, Chrysler's operating earnings were a record $1.09 billion, or $1.51 per share.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, Chrysler posted profits of $1.04 billion, or $1.33 per share.
Chrysler's full-year 1996 net income was $3.53 billion, or $4.74 per share, including $347 million in special charges.
Chrysler's full-year 1996 net income fell short of its 1994 all-time record of $3.71 billion.
On a pretax basis, Chrysler earned $6.09 billion for all of 1996, a record that topped 1995's $3.45 billion.
Chrysler announced that its 79,000 U.S. employees will receive average profit-sharing checks of $7,900 in February.
Comerica Bank economist David Littman estimated that the profit-sharing payments could boost Michigan's economy by $356 million.
Chrysler's stock rose $1.50 a share to close at $36 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Chrysler Corp. will report record earnings for 1996.
Chrysler's record worldwide sales for 1996 are 2.97 million vehicles.
Robert Eaton is the chairman of Chrysler Corp.
Chrysler's previous annual profit record was $3.713 billion in 1994.
Chrysler earned $2.025 billion in 1995.
Chrysler's sales in 1995 were limited to 2.61 million units due to the launch of its current line of minivans.
Chrysler expects to exceed its 1996 sales results in 1997.
Chrysler plans to produce about 190,000 more trucks in 1997 than in 1996.
Chrysler plans to unveil the Dodge Durango at the Detroit auto show.
Chrysler stock dropped 12.5 cents to $35.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

LucasVarity is an Anglo-U.S. auto-components-to-aerospace company.
LucasVarity announced it is reviewing offers for 13 companies designated for disposal.
Victor Rice is the chief executive of LucasVarity.
Victor Rice stated that the group expects to enter active negotiations for the sale of non-core units soon.
Only eight of the 13 businesses marked for sale were identified in the restructuring statement.
Major businesses like aerospace and electronics are not among the unnamed five companies for sale.
Victor Rice did not provide a timeline for when the first disposals would occur.
The restructuring plans will lead to the divestment of 13 businesses and 3,000 job cuts worldwide over two years.
Victor Rice indicated that post-merger savings are expected to be virtually double the original expectations.
Annual operating savings are projected to reach 120 million stg by January 31, 1999.

The British government warned it would refer the proposed transatlantic alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission unless conditions are accepted.
Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang stated that final clearance for the alliance depends on an open skies deal between the British and U.S. governments.
Lang supported conditions proposed by the Office of Fair Trading regarding the alliance.
Lang claimed that without suitable undertakings, the alliance would likely lead to a significant loss of actual and potential passengers on competing routes.
The latest open skies talks ended in London without a deal being signed.
Industry sources indicated there was no new date for further talks due to uncertainty over the BA/American deal.
The conditions for clearance of the alliance include BA and American dropping 168 slots at London Heathrow airport.
The government wants BA to remove a clause in its agreement with USAir that prevents competition on transatlantic routes.
Both BA and American should be prepared to reduce services on the London to Dallas Ft Worth route if a new entrant wishes to enter.
Will Whitehorn, spokesman for Virgin Atlantic Airways, expressed doubt that BA and American would meet the conditions and suggested the alliance would still be anti-competitive.

Stagecoach Plc's shares increased by 138 percent in a year.
Stagecoach Plc promised more growth this year due to overseas acquisitions.
Brian Souter is the executive chairman of Stagecoach Plc.
Stagecoach Plc has a total gearing of 567 percent.
Brian Souter stated that Stagecoach Plc has the financial capacity to make major acquisitions.
Stagecoach Plc is targeting rail and bus firms in the Nordic region and examining the Pacific Rim.
Stagecoach Plc has a 17 percent market share in the British bus market and aims to reach 25 percent.
Stagecoach Plc is delaying acquisitions in the British bus market until after the upcoming election.
Stagecoach Plc expects to have 230 million pounds in free cash in two to three years.
70 percent of Stagecoach Plc's total debt of 830 million dollars is fixed for seven years at 7.19 percent.

AT&T Corp. reported a 17 percent decline in first-quarter profits.
AT&T's profit decline was attributed to competition in long-distance services and investments in new businesses.
AT&T warned that second-quarter results might also be weak.
BellSouth Corp. reported an 11 percent increase in operating earnings.
BellSouth's earnings growth was due to an increase in customer lines and strong growth in wireless operations.
AT&T earned $1.13 billion, or 69 cents a share, on revenues of $13.05 billion in the first quarter.
In the first quarter of 1996, AT&T had a net income of $1.36 billion, or 85 cents a share, on revenues of $12.85 billion.
AT&T's earnings per share for the first quarter met Wall Street's expectations.
AT&T's first-quarter revenue growth was driven by local telephone service and wireless services.
AT&T's long-distance calling volume increased by 6.7 percent compared to the same period in 1996.

Shareholders of MCI Communications Corp are expected to vote in favor of the proposed merger with British Telecommunications Plc.
The shareholder vote is a milestone for the $23 billion cross-border merger.
The merger will create a combined company known as Concert Plc with $40.6 billion in revenues.
The merger awaits regulatory approvals in Washington, London, and Brussels.
Company officials are confident the merger is on track to close in the fall of 1997.
The annual shareholder meeting will be held in Wilkes Barre, Pennsylvania.
The agenda for the annual meeting includes the shareholder vote, election of directors, and election of auditors.
Wilkes Barre was chosen for the meeting because it is the hometown of William McGowan, the founder of MCI.
Bert Roberts, MCI's chairman and chief executive, is expected to discuss the benefits of the merger in his speech.
Industry analysts expect Roberts to reveal early products and services resulting from the merger.

NCR Corp reported a small profit in the fourth quarter of 1996.
NCR Corp experienced year-over-year gains in profit margins.
NCR executives stated that matching computer industry growth rates is a distant goal.
NCR Chief Financial Officer John Giering indicated that profits are affected by a 75 percent tax rate.
Giering stated that NCR is unlikely to reduce its tax levels to industry norms of 35 to 40 percent before 1999.
Giering's goal is for NCR's U.S. operations to break even in profitability in 1997.
NCR is already profitable in its overseas operations, which contributed to half of its $7 billion in 1996 revenues.
NCR aims for a 9 to 12 percent growth rate from core operations over the next several years.
Giering expects NCR to achieve gross profit margins in the mid-30 percent range within three years.
NCR ended 1996 with $1.2 billion in cash and $76 billion in debt.

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato introduced legislation to prohibit banks from charging additional fees to non-customers using their automated teller machines.
About 54 percent of all automated teller machines impose a surcharge on non-customers, according to a survey by the General Accounting Office.
Alfonse D'Amato stated that ATMs were supposed to reduce costs and pass savings to consumers.
D'Amato claimed that banks are now saying ATMs are no longer cost-effective.
D'Amato accused banks of charging multiple fees to consumers for withdrawing money.
Consumer groups urged lawmakers to enact a ban on ATM surcharges.
Edmund Mierzwinski, programme director at the U.S. Public Interest Research Group, stated that surcharges threaten smaller banks.
Mierzwinski warned that if small bank customers switch to big banks to avoid surcharges, big banks may raise their fees due to reduced competition.
Banks denied that surcharges amount to double-dipping and argued that consumers benefit from the proliferation of ATMs funded by surcharge revenues.
Ed Yingling, executive director of the American Bankers Association, stated that consumers should decide if they are willing to pay for ATM convenience.

Federal bank regulators are urging U.S. financial institutions to prepare for potential computer problems in the year 2000.
Many computers and software programs only record the last two digits of a year, which could lead to confusion between the year 2000 and the year 1900.
Confused computers could cause issues such as bounced checks, missed loan payments, and miscalculated interest rates for banks.
Regulators informed Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato about the dangers associated with the year 2000 issue.
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency have formed an interagency working group to address the year 2000 issue.
Comptroller Eugene Ludwig stated that the costs of making systems year 2000 compliant will be substantial and may impact some banks' earnings.
Experts believe that even well-prepared organizations will face some problems related to the year 2000 issue.
Nicholas Retsinas, director of the Office of Thrift Supervision, warned that the year 2000 rollover could pose substantial risks to the financial services industry.
Analysts estimate that corporations and governments may need to spend $300 to $600 billion worldwide to fix the year 2000 problem.
Bank examiners will inquire about year 2000 preparations this year to ensure solutions are implemented before the end of 1999.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin outlined a plan to overhaul Depression-era laws governing the U.S. financial sector.
The Clinton administration favored allowing banks to enter the securities and insurance fields.
Rubin stated that the lines separating insurance, securities, and banking industries have blurred due to new financial services and products.
The administration proposal was originally expected in March and is alongside several bills already introduced in Congress.
Rubin expressed a desire to work with Congress on this initiative.
Increased competition in financial services is expected to benefit consumers, generating savings of up to $15 billion a year.
The new proposal did not take a firm position on allowing banks to combine with non-financial, commercial firms.
Some lawmakers, smaller banks, and consumer groups oppose allowing banks to combine with commercial firms.
Insurance companies and securities firms argue they are intertwined with non-financial interests and need to compete with banks.
Rubin outlined two possible approaches regarding mixing banks with commercial firms.

The Czech Republic recorded its first budget deficit in 1996.
The budget deficit was 1.56 billion Czech crowns, equivalent to $57.28 million.
This was the first budget shortfall since the Czech Republic became a sovereign nation in 1993.
The Finance Ministry reported that revenues for 1996 totaled 482.8 billion crowns.
Expenditures for 1996 were 484.3 billion crowns.
The original 1996 budget was balanced at 497.6 billion crowns.
The forecast expenditure was later reduced to 491 billion crowns due to budget cuts.
Parliament approved a balanced budget plan for 1997 with both expenditures and revenues forecast at 549.1 billion crowns.
The 1997 budget was based on an expected economic growth of 5.4 percent.
Independent analysts forecasted economic growth for 1997 at under five percent.

The United States offered the Czech Republic free use of seven Navy Hornet aircraft for five years.
The U.S. Navy representatives offered to lease seven McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet fighter planes to the Czech Republic under a no-cost, five-year agreement.
The offer includes six single-seat F/A-18A and one two-seat F/A-18B aircraft.
The offer also includes the supply of replacement parts, pilot and ground personnel training programs, and support equipment at cost.
Lockheed Martin, SAAB and British Aerospace, and Dassault Aviation are also competing for post-Cold War business in central Europe.
It is unclear whether the aircraft in the U.S. offer will be used or new.
Czech pilots could begin training in the planes in six months.
Delivery of the aircraft is expected 18 months after the contract is signed.
McDonnell Douglas plans to locate production of components for the Hornet at Czech light jet maker Aero Vodochody.
The Czech government is debating aircraft purchases due to proposed cuts in defense spending.

The Czech Republic's trade deficit nearly doubled in January year-on-year.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported a January trade deficit of 13.6 billion crowns.
The January trade deficit in 1996 was 7.86 billion crowns.
Imports grew by 8.2 percent year-on-year.
Exports contracted by 2.5 percent.
Raw material exports decreased by 11.8 percent.
Petr Tomek of Zivnostenska Banka stated that the figures were better than expected.
The Czech Statistical Bureau forecasted the 1997 trade deficit to rise to about 215 billion crowns.
Overall nominal imports for January were 60.04 billion crowns.
Exports for January totaled 46.45 billion crowns.

Merrill Lynch purchased an equities research and sales boutique in Italy.
The acquired firm is Carnegie Italia SpA, based in Milan.
Merrill Lynch previously acquired FG Inversiones in Spain for 3.7 billion pesetas ($29.5 million).
Merrill Lynch also bought British equities specialist Smith New Court last year.
Tony Morrongiello will lead Merrill Lynch's local institutional equity sales in Milan.
Merrill Lynch's Italian equity sales, research, and trading teams will collaborate with Morrongiello's team.
Paul Roy stated that the acquisition would enhance client service and leverage in the market.
Christopher Reeves identified Italy as a growth area for Merrill Lynch in various financial sectors.
Carnegie agreed to sell its Italian operations to Merrill Lynch to obtain capital for expansion in the Nordic region.
Merrill Lynch has previously relied on personnel from London and New York for investment banking deals in Europe.

National Westminster Bank Plc announced it would complete an internal investigation into a 50 million pound trading loss as quickly as possible.
A NatWest spokeswoman stated that the internal inquiry is ongoing.
NatWest revealed mispricing errors in the interest rate options book at its investment banking arm, NatWest Markets.
NatWest is employing an outside firm to assist with the investigation.
The investigation will include a thorough review of NatWest's control systems and is expected to take several weeks.
The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) has been informed of the errors.
NatWest did not confirm whether it had meetings with the SFA over the weekend.
The Bank of England stated it would be looking into the situation.
Kyriacos Papouis was named as the interest rate options trader involved in the mispricing issue.
NatWest has not confirmed Papouis's involvement and he could not be reached for comment.

Judith Mayhew is the new head of the Corporation of London.
Mayhew stated that London will defend its share of foreign exchange trading after the introduction of a single European currency.
Mayhew emphasized the importance of maintaining market share.
The Corporation of London is the local authority for London's financial hub.
Mayhew identified three main challenges for the Corporation.
The first challenge is the survival of the Corporation to represent the views of the City.
The second challenge is to ensure that London is the primary market for the euro.
The third challenge is to ensure that LIFFE dominates the derivatives market for the European single currency.
Mayhew believes it is important for Britain to remain involved in negotiations regarding the single currency.
Mayhew stated that the Corporation aims to increase the number of global banking headquarters in the Square Mile.

A Chinese court sentenced dissident Li Hai to nine years in prison for prying into state secrets.
The trial was held behind closed doors.
A family member of Li Hai expressed surprise at the sentence.
Li Hai was initially charged with leaking state secrets.
Li's family and lawyer argued that he was not a civil servant and had no access to state secrets.
The court lacked evidence to convict Li of leaking state secrets.
Li's relative believed the appeal process had already started.
The appeals trial is also expected to be held behind closed doors.
Li Hai has not been allowed to meet his family since his detention in May 1995.
Li Hai was first arrested in May 1990 for his role in the 1989 student demonstrations for democracy.

A Chinese court has agreed to hear a lawsuit by Liu Nianchun accusing the government of illegal incarceration.
Liu Nianchun's wife stated that finding a defense lawyer has been difficult.
Beijing's Chaoyang District Court has accepted Liu Nianchun's lawsuit.
Liu Nianchun's family lacks financial resources to hire a lawyer.
Several lawyers have faced government pressure not to take Liu Nianchun's case.
Beijing's Dongcheng District Court has agreed to hear Wang Hui's lawsuit against the police.
Wang Hui accused police of illegally detaining her from May 16 to June 13.
Wang Hui also accused five guards at a detention center of beating her after the guards had been drinking.
Wang Hui demanded 10,000 yuan in compensation, a public apology, and punishment of the guards.
Liu Nianchun and Zhou Guoqiang are both serving three-year sentences of re-education through labor.

China's propaganda machine praised the selection of Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive as the beginning of true democracy.
The China Daily described the election of Tung Chee-hwa as a significant moment in Hong Kong's democratic development.
Tung Chee-hwa was elected by a 400-member Selection Committee chosen by Beijing.
Tung Chee-hwa will officially assume the role of chief executive when Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on June 30, 1997.
Major Chinese newspapers reported on Tung's election with prominent coverage and images.
The official Xinhua news agency characterized Hong Kong-style democracy as distinct from both the mainland and the West.
Xinhua stated that Hong Kong is establishing a democratic system that is lawful, open, fair, civilized, and orderly.
China plans to dismantle Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council after the handover and replace it with an appointed legislature.
Xinhua criticized British rule in Hong Kong, claiming there was no democracy during that period.
Xinhua asserted that China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong provides an opportunity for democratic development.

Macquarie Bank Ltd is Australia's largest locally-owned investment bank.
Macquarie Bank posted an annual profit of A$116.94 million for the year to March 31.
Macquarie's net profit increased by 25.4 percent compared to the previous year.
The return on average shareholder funds for Macquarie was 25.2 percent.
Macquarie raised its annual dividend to 43 cents from 36 cents the previous year.
Earnings per share for Macquarie rose to 74.9 cents from 61 cents.
Analysts had forecast a net profit of around A$105 million for Macquarie.
Macquarie's Corporate Advisory division had 130 advisory mandates during the year.
Simon Hannes, a senior corporate advisory executive at Macquarie, was charged with insider trading.
Macquarie's managing director Allan Moss stated that the Hannes matter did not affect corporate advisory work.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia warned that proposed changes to Australia's prudential regulation system could lead to significant collapses.
David Murray is the Managing Director of Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Murray stated that proposals to regulate banks and non-banks within the same prudential system are too risky.
Murray compared the proposed system to the U.S. savings and loan sector before its collapses in the 1980s.
Murray criticized the plan to increase competition in the banking payments system and remove the Reserve Bank of Australia's prudential supervision role.
Murray's criticism is the first major opposition to the Wallis report since its release.
The Liberal/National government is considering the recommendations from the Wallis Inquiry.
Murray's comments were labeled as emotive scare-mongering by an audience member at a CEDA luncheon.
Murray emphasized the importance of debating Wallis' plan and being critical of it.
The Reserve Bank currently requires banks to meet strict prudential requirements and restricts non-banks from issuing cheques.

Bank of Melbourne Ltd announced a A$1.435 billion takeover bid by Westpac Banking Corp.
The takeover bid valued Bank of Melbourne at 2.1 times net assets.
Bank of Melbourne and Westpac will merge their retail operations in Victoria.
The merged entity will trade under the Bank of Melbourne brand name with local management.
The merger is subject to the approval of Treasurer Peter Costello and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Westpac will offer A$9.75 for each Bank of Melbourne ordinary share, including a 90 cent per share special dividend.
Shareholders can choose to receive the A$8.85 balance in cash or in the form of one Westpac share plus up to A$1.85 in cash.
Westpac will offer A$15.36 in cash for each converting preference share or a combination of Westpac shares and cash up to A$1.36.
The offer represents an earnings multiple of 15.2 times 1997 prospective earnings as forecast by Barceps.
The ACCC will examine the merger proposal over the next several weeks.

Mercury Finance Co. secured $50 million in short-term financing from Bank of America.
The financing provides Mercury with the ability to work on longer-term financing.
Some competitors in the automotive financing market are interested in purchasing Mercury's assets.
Mercury has directed interested parties to Salomon Brothers, its adviser.
The financing from Bank of America is secured by Mercury's assets.
The funds will be used for day-to-day operating expenses and upcoming interest payments.
Mercury continues to serve customers at all its locations.
Mercury was unable to refinance $61 million in short-term debt that matured through February 5.
Another $127 million in debt is due between February 5 and February 14.
Mercury had to restate its earnings downward by about $90 million due to accounting discrepancies.

Mercury Finance Co. announced it would be unable to pay $17 million in commercial debt due on Friday.
The company's stock lost nearly 90 percent of its value, dropping from $13 to $1.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock traded over 27 million shares and fell as low as $1.625.
Mercury Finance Co. had more than 172 million shares outstanding as of early November, resulting in a loss of over $2.2 billion in market capitalization.
The company reported problems in its bookkeeping that led to an overstatement of earnings by $90 million over four years.
Due to downgrades from several debt rating services, Mercury Finance Co. could not issue new short-term debt to repay maturing debt.
Standard & Poor's Corp. and Fitch Investors Service downgraded the company's commercial paper to a default rating.
Mercury Finance Co. was in discussions with its lenders regarding its working capital needs but could not predict the outcome.
The company retained Salomon Brothers Inc. to advise on its current and future capital needs.
A class-action lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court in Chicago, accusing Mercury Finance Co. of violating securities laws.

TCF Financial Corp. is a bank holding company.
TCF Financial Corp. signed a letter of intent to acquire Winthrop Resources Corp. for about $326 million.
Under the agreement, TCF will offer one share of its stock for every 1.2877 shares of Winthrop in a tax-free pooling of interests.
TCF has suspended its share repurchase program due to the pending acquisition.
Winthrop Resources Corp. has leased assets of $327 million and specializes in leasing high technology and business equipment.
Winthrop Resources Corp. is based in Minneapolis.
Winthrop will become a subsidiary of TCF Bank Minnesota after the acquisition.
The deal values Winthrop at $36.50 a share based on a TCF stock price of $47.
TCF shares fell to $46.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal is expected to close by the third quarter, pending negotiation of a definitive agreement and approvals.

Molson Cos Ltd will hold its annual shareholder meeting on Wednesday.
Molson Cos Ltd is under pressure for a stock buyback.
Molson Cos Ltd is searching worldwide for a brewing acquisition.
The meeting marks the debut of a new chief executive.
The new chief executive aims to lead the company's return to its brewing roots.
Molson is close to completing the C$1 billion sale of its Diversey Corp chemicals unit.
Molson is looking for overseas opportunities to expand its core brewing business.
Some investors are pushing for a share buyback due to concerns about acquisition costs.
Molson owns 40 percent of Canada's largest brewer, Molson Breweries.
Molson Breweries is also owned 40 percent by Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20 percent by Miller Brewing unit.

Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves stated that the government was ahead of its revised deficit target for 1996/97.
Eves indicated that the province may balance its budget before the year 2000.
Eves mentioned that he does not feel obligated to accelerate the timetable for the next stage of the government's planned 30 percent income tax cut.
The Conservative government will present its second full budget on May 6 since taking power in 1995.
Eves revised the 1996/97 deficit down to C$7.67 billion from an original forecast of C$8.2 billion.
Eves suggested that the economy performed well and that the deficit might be slightly better than the revised figure.
Eves declined to comment on predictions that the 1996/97 deficit would fall below C$7 billion.
Some analysts speculated that the government could eliminate the deficit by fiscal 1999/2000, one year ahead of plan.
Eves stated that balancing the budget ahead of schedule would require significant economic growth.
Eves confirmed that he would use conservative economic forecasts in the upcoming budget.

Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. increased on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
The stock price of Bre-X rose C$1.22 to close at C$3.62.
Bre-X traded 17 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The stock reached a session high of C$5.75 during late afternoon trading.
Bre-X has faced controversy due to preliminary tests by Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. indicating the gold deposit may contain insignificant amounts of gold.
The announcement of preliminary test results caused panic selling of Bre-X shares, reducing the company's market value by over 80 percent.
Reports indicated that Freeport received independent tests of the Busang deposit, which were disputed by Freeport and Bre-X officials.
Freeport's spokeswoman stated that testing is ongoing and no assay results have been communicated to Freeport.
Bre-X commissioned Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. to conduct an audit of its Busang project, with results expected in early May.
Bre-X released drill results from 22 holes at the Busang property, with 16 holes showing varying amounts of gold and six holes showing no significant amounts.

Chrysler Corp. developed a new method to extract hydrogen from gasoline.
The new method could accelerate the introduction of super-efficient electric cars by 10 years.
Chrysler's system uses normal gasoline to obtain hydrogen.
The future car powered by this system is expected to have a 50 percent increase in fuel efficiency over current cars.
Cars using this hydrogen extraction system would be more expensive than internal combustion engine cars.
Chrysler officials stated the system could be commercially viable between 2010 and 2015.
Drivers of gasoline fuel cell cars would refuel at normal gasoline stations.
Chrysler aims to have a working test vehicle within three years.
Francois Castaing, Chrysler's vice president of vehicle engineering, stated that hydrogen needs to be processed from gasoline on-board vehicles.
The on-board 'refinery' system faces significant development hurdles and currently costs about $30,000.

Canada's Magna International Inc. will acquire Douglas & Lomason Co. for about $135 million in cash.
Magna made a $31-a-share tender offer for all of Douglas & Lomason's 4.45 million common shares outstanding.
Douglas & Lomason shares rose 37.5 cents to $26.125 on Nasdaq prior to the merger announcement.
The acquisition will enhance Magna's North American car and truck seating business.
Douglas & Lomason had 1995 revenues of $561 million.
Douglas & Lomason was finding it difficult to compete for new seating contracts from automakers.
Douglas & Lomason earned $11.2 million on sales of $299 million in the first six months of 1996.
Some analysts suggested the deal was encouraged by Ford Motor Co. to strengthen Magna's competitiveness.
Douglas & Lomason currently supplies seats for the Ford Contour and Mystique cars.
Magna's traditional strength has been in instrument panels, door panels, and other interior components.

Chrysler Corp. broke ground on a $10 million historical museum.
The museum will be located on the grounds of Chrysler's corporate headquarters and technical center.
The museum will cover 35,000 square feet and house vintage vehicles, company archives, and a theater.
This museum will be the first company-owned museum among Detroit's Big Three automakers.
Mercedes-Benz AG and Bayerische Motoren Werke AG have museums in Stuttgart and Munich, respectively.
Chrysler's Historical Museum will eventually open to the public and aims to instill pride in employees.
The project indicates Chrysler's confidence in its future and a shift in its fortunes since financial difficulties in 1980 and 1991.
Chrysler nearly sold its collection of vintage vehicles in the late 1970s to raise cash.
Chrysler's largest shareholder, Kirk Kerkorian, has encouraged stock buybacks totaling $4 billion over two years.
Eaton indicated that Lee Iacocca's role in Chrysler's history may be featured in the museum.

Ford Motor Co announced 1,300 job cuts at its plant in northwest England.
Unions raised the possibility of strikes in the British automobile industry following Ford's announcement.
Ford's Halewood factory near Liverpool received a global quality award for 1996.
Ford stated that the new version of its mid-range Escort would not be built at the Halewood factory.
The new Escort model is likely to be built in Spain and Germany.
Ford's proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000.
Halewood's workforce peaked at 14,000 in the 1960s and was around 4,500 before the cuts.
British Prime Minister John Major described Ford's decision as 'very surprising' and contrary to investment trends in the UK.
Unions plan to hold mass meetings at Ford plants to discuss potential protest actions against the job cuts.
Workers will be asked to support measures, including a ballot for strike action, to secure the future of Halewood.

1,300 jobs were cut at Ford Motor Co's Halewood plant in Northern England.
The job cuts at Ford dented Northern England's record of attracting foreign firms.
Cheap local labor, flexible employment rules, and government laws have attracted foreign investors to Northern England.
Companies that have invested in Northern England include Nissan Motor Co, Siemens, Samsung Co, and Vauxhall.
Prime Minister John Major stated that the job cuts went against the trend of investment.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke commented that 'You can't win them all.'
Professor Charles Bean of the London School of Economics stated that low firing costs make foreign companies more likely to create jobs in the UK during good times and cut jobs during tough times.
Christine Kennedy, a spokeswoman for Northern Development Co, claimed that foreign investment has contributed to the regeneration of the north.
Inward, the north west's corporate development body, reported that 2,600 jobs were created in the region in the financial year 1995/96.
Liverpool Chamber of Commerce policy executive Peter Rigby noted that the discovery of oil and gas in Liverpool Bay could create up to 2,000 jobs.

Racal Electronics announced an alliance with ITT Defence for a defense contract.
The defense contract is valued at two billion pounds ($3.4 billion).
David Elsbury is the chief executive of Racal Electronics.
The alliance could yield joint savings of 100 million pounds in development costs.
The Bowman communications contract decision is due by March 1997.
The contract is important for Racal's future earnings and for Siemens of Germany.
The winner of the Bowman contract could receive an estimated two billion pounds in follow-through export orders.
Winning the contract would create 6,500 new jobs.
If Racal loses the contract, it may need to downsize the company.
Racal's costs to date for the contract are between 30 and 50 million pounds.

3Com Corp. proposed a $6.6 billion acquisition of U.S. Robotics Corp.
The acquisition proposal caused a drop in the stocks of 3Com and U.S. Robotics.
3Com's stock fell $4 to $35 and was the most heavily traded issue on Nasdaq.
More than 40 million shares of 3Com changed hands on Nasdaq.
U.S. Robotics' stock dropped $1.875 to $59.125 and was the second-most active share on Nasdaq.
Analysts claimed the proposed stock swap undervalued U.S. Robotics.
Eric Buck, an analyst at Donaldson Lufkin, criticized the terms of the deal.
The offer involved stock and options valued at $7.3 billion.
Peter Swartz, a Salomon analyst, described the deal as a 'take-under' rather than a takeover.
U.S. Robotics Chairman Casey Cowell stated the sale price was not too low.

A coalition of 28 computer and communications equipment makers announced a plan to develop a common standard for faster modems.
The coalition aims to create modems that operate at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second.
U.S. Robotics Corp. is not a member of the coalition.
U.S. Robotics is the leading maker of consumer modems and is credited with pioneering the development of 56-kilobit modems.
U.S. Robotics began shipping its 56-kilobit modems earlier in the week of the announcement.
3Com Corp. announced it would acquire U.S. Robotics in a deal valued at $6.6 billion.
Faster modems will reduce the time required to access web pages or download software.
The 56-kilobit-per-second speed would double the speed of current 28.8-kilobit-per-second modems.
The standards group is called the Open 56 Forum and includes support from companies like Rockwell International Corp., Lucent Technologies Inc., and Motorola Inc.
U.S. Robotics was invited to join the Open 56K Forum shortly before the coalition's announcement.

Lucent Technologies Inc expects its consumer products unit to show substantial profit gains in 1997.
Lucent Technologies Inc expects a return to revenue growth in the consumer products unit by the December quarter.
Chief Financial Officer Don Peterson stated that profitability improvements will mainly come from cost-cutting.
Lucent Technologies Inc reported a 41 percent decline in consumer product revenues in the second quarter ended in March.
Consumer products comprised a small fraction of total revenues of $5.15 billion in the March quarter.
The consumer products unit was the only Lucent unit not to see double-digit growth in the March quarter.
The division's revenues fell to $174 million in the March quarter due to the closing of phone center stores and reduced revenue from phone rentals.
Lucent's carrier network systems division revenues increased by 23.3 percent to $2.93 billion.
Lucent's business communications unit revenues rose by 14.1 percent to $1.3 billion.
Lucent's semiconductor revenues gained 18.3 percent to $615 million.

The Clinton administration supported congressional efforts to reform U.S. banking laws.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin presented a plan to eliminate the Glass-Steagall Act barriers.
The administration's plan was due to Congress by March 31.
There was a nearly two-month delay in submitting the plan.
Congress has attempted to reform banking laws for over a decade.
Interest groups have historically blocked banking legislation.
Recent court and regulatory decisions have granted banks new authority.
Insurance companies and securities firms are now seeking a level playing field.
David Farmer, a lobbyist for the Alliance of American Insurers, expressed renewed hope for reform.
Rubin will provide more details of the plan in testimony before Congress on June 3.

The U.S. Commerce Department approved an application from Sybase Inc to export computer encoding products.
Sybase Inc officials reported the approval on Wednesday.
About a dozen companies have received permission to export products with encryption this year.
Sybase's products appeared to bypass strict U.S. export rules in effect since the beginning of the year.
Tom Parenty is the director of data and communication security at Sybase.
Parenty expressed surprise at the approval and wrote a letter outlining differences in their approach versus the regulations.
To export powerful encryption, a company must include features that allow the government to access software keys.
Companies can export medium-strength encryption by promising to include key recovery features within two years.
Sybase's products will allow for key recovery only for stored data, not for live communications.
Sybase supports legislative proposals to eliminate most export restrictions.

Scientists are working on the next generation of the Internet.
The first challenge is to convince the U.S. Congress to fund the project.
The next generation network has encountered roadblocks on Capitol Hill.
Scientists, including John Gibbons, will address concerns at a Senate hearing.
Some lawmakers are concerned that the project lacks focus and is similar to Internet2.
The next generation Internet project aims to send data at 1,000 times the speed of today's Internet.
Clinton pledged $100 million annually for five years to build the super high-speed network.
The funding was to come from reallocating existing research funds, but this plan is facing issues.
The House of Representatives passed a budget that bars spending on the next generation Internet.
28 senators expressed concerns about the advisory board's composition in a letter to Gibbons.

The Czech Republic recorded its first budget deficit in 1996.
The government attempted to achieve a fourth consecutive surplus.
In December 1996, the government froze some outlays and required early repayment on credit to address a projected deficit.
The Finance Ministry announced a definitive budget deficit of 1.562 billion crowns for 1996.
Revenues for 1996 totaled 482.8 billion crowns, while expenditures were 484.3 billion crowns.
The Czech Republic had three consecutive year-end budget surpluses since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
Finance ministry officials indicated that the deficit could increase due to late bill submissions.
The 1996 budget was initially approved as balanced at 497.6 billion crowns but was later revised to 491 billion crowns due to spending cuts.
Parliamentary budget committee chairman Jozef Wagner expressed concern about the impact of government payment adjustments on the 1997 budget.
The 1997 budget was approved with both expenditures and revenues forecast at 549.1 billion crowns, based on an expected economic growth of 5.4 percent.

The Budapest Stock Exchange reached a record high on Friday.
A foreign-buying induced bull run occurred in eastern Europe this week.
Markets in the region rose, with Budapest and Warsaw recording year-highs.
Romania and Slovenia also experienced significant increases.
Bratislava and Prague saw slight increases with minimal upward momentum.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange achieved four consecutive 33-month highs this week.
Heavy turnover was noted on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
Analysts predicted a profit-taking correction was likely to occur later.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange has risen 25 percent since December 10.
Maciej Matusiak, an analyst at PKO BP brokerage, suggested investors would start taking profits next week.

The Czech crown fell sharply on Thursday following comments from the central bank.
The central bank expressed dissatisfaction with the recent rise of the Czech crown.
Dealers believe the Czech crown remains attractive and should stabilize by the end of the week.
The Czech crown is one of post-Communist Europe's most stable currencies.
The crown has reached record highs in recent weeks due to demand from over 30 billion crowns in Eurobond issues since the start of the year.
The crown was trading at 3.48 percent above parity against the dollar basket.
The crown fell over 60 basis points from its opening and about 200 points lower from Tuesday's record fixing at +5.51.
Analysts believe the country's high interest rate differential and overall economic stability should limit further drops in the crown's value.
The central bank's repo rate is at 12.4 percent, and the discount rate has been at 10.5 percent since last June.
CNB spokesman Martin Svehla stated that the central bank has the option to intervene in the market when necessary.

Nick Durlacher is the chairman of the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA).
The head of Britain's financial markets watchdog stated that volatile markets and new financial tools contributed to recent investment banking failures.
Durlacher emphasized the need for firms to focus on control and compliance in addition to profitability and market share.
The SFA announced it would not publish controversial changes to its rules until they align with standards proposed by the Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
Durlacher noted that the growth of derivatives over the last 10 years has created new management challenges.
Durlacher mentioned that senior managers are making outdated mistakes.
The investment banking industry is experiencing a volatile job market.
Durlacher highlighted that bonuses and the 'star system' are factors firms need to consider.
The SFA's proposals aim to make senior executive officers more accountable for catastrophic failures in their firms.
Durlacher expressed hope that the proposals would be finalized by the end of April.

A proposed reform of Britain's state pensions system aims to prevent burdens on future taxpayers.
The ruling Conservative government unveiled these proposals on Wednesday.
Workers would be responsible for providing for their old age under the proposed reform.
Roger Taylor, deputy chairman of Royal & Sun Alliance, described the plans as a significant shift in financial services.
Taylor believes the proposals would encourage other governments to implement similar changes.
If enacted, the proposals are expected to generate additional business in three to four years.
Tony Baker, deputy director general of the Association of British Insurers, stated the proposals are beneficial for the industry.
The opposition Labour Party is ahead in opinion polls and wants to retain the basic state pension.
Labour also aims to develop new second pensions for those not in occupational pension schemes.
The banking and life insurance industry is preparing for changes regardless of the election outcome.

Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is involved in the probe into alleged irregularities in three Morgan Grenfell investment funds.
The investigation by the SFO extends beyond Britain.
The SFO is in contact with Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO).
The SFO is not conducting its own investigation.
A senior SFO lawyer has been briefed by IMRO.
Overseas authorities in the U.S., Luxembourg, and Switzerland are involved in the investigation.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell reported that nearly eight percent of the three Morgan Grenfell investment funds had been redeemed.
The funds were suspended due to suspected irregularities but resumed trading after Deutsche Bank removed certain unlisted securities.
IMRO's investigation has led to the suspension of two fund managers at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
The probe is focusing on links between suspended MGAM fund manager Peter Young and UK-based broker Fiba Nordic Securities.

Deng Xiaoping, China's paramount leader, died of respiratory failure on Wednesday.
Deng was 93 years old by Chinese reckoning.
Jiang Zemin is the anointed successor of Deng Xiaoping and holds the positions of Communist Party chief, state President, and head of the armed forces.
Diplomats and analysts expect calm in China following Deng's death.
There is speculation about whether Jiang Zemin will reverse Deng's economic reforms.
A power struggle among potential successors to Deng is anticipated.
China faces multiple issues including unemployment, a widening wealth gap, corruption, and a one-party system.
Analysts predict that the country may experience a period of mourning and political maneuvering.
Tai Ming Cheung, a Hong Kong-based Sinologist, stated that there will be an emphasis on stability and internal security.
Jiang Zemin appears to have consolidated his power base, but political rivals are expected to compete for influence.

China and South Korea negotiated on Friday regarding the defection of Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop is a top North Korean official who has taken refuge in Seoul's mission in Beijing.
Pyongyang officials aimed to persuade Hwang Jang-yop to return to North Korea.
Talks in Singapore between South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen did not resolve the deadlock over Hwang Jang-yop.
Hwang Jang-yop is 73 years old and is the most senior Pyongyang official to flee North Korea.
A South Korean embassy official stated that negotiations over Hwang Jang-yop had begun in Beijing.
Hwang Jang-yop spent a second night in the South Korean embassy compound with an aide.
China is involved in the dispute between North Korea and South Korea regarding Hwang Jang-yop.
China's Qian stated that more time is needed to investigate the incident.
Hwang Jang-yop is in good health and spending his time reading while in the embassy.

Guo Song was sentenced to death by a Beijing judge for bank robbery.
Guo Song killed four bank guards and stole several payrolls.
Guo Song's execution could occur by January 1 due to amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law.
The judge delivered the verdict during a trial that was videotaped by a court clerk.
Court hearings in China are described as resembling theatre.
A judge-turned-lawyer stated that verdicts may be decided beforehand in Chinese trials.
Defendants in China are presumed guilty before being proved innocent.
Suspects can be detained for extended periods, and lawyers receive the bill of indictment shortly before trial.
Criminal law professor Qu Xinjiu commented that the amendments approved by the National People's Congress represent a significant improvement.
Lawyer Li Shuguang expressed concerns about the preparedness of judges and prosecutors for upcoming judicial reforms.

BHP Petroleum and Phillips Petroleum agreed that BHP should be the sole operator of the Bayu-Undan gas field.
The Bayu-Undan gas field is located in the Timor Sea.
The estimated cost of developing the Bayu-Undan gas field is A$4 billion.
The field has proven and probable reserves of 3.1 trillion cubic feet (tcf).
The Bayu-Undan gas field is divided into two sides: the 'Bayu' side and the 'Undan' side.
The 'Bayu' side is owned by a Phillips-led joint venture that includes Oryx Energy Co and Hardy Oil & Gas Plc.
Phillips holds a 60 percent stake in the 'Bayu' side of the field.
The 'Undan' side is owned by a BHP-led joint venture that includes Petroz, Santos Ltd, and Inpex Sahul.
BHP holds a 42.417 percent stake in the 'Undan' side of the field.
The ZOCAs were established by a treaty between Australia and Indonesia.

Analysts expected that Fisher and Paykel Ltd would post a slightly lower profit in 1996/97.
Gary Paykel is the chief executive of Fisher and Paykel Ltd.
Gary Paykel stated that local analysts' reports were accurate regarding profit expectations.
The analysts referenced include J.B. Were and Hendry Hay McIntosh.
Analysts forecasted Fisher and Paykel's full year net profit would fall to about NZ$38 million from NZ$39.25 million in 1995/96.
Fisher and Paykel reported a first half net profit of NZ$19.2 million in early November.
Fisher and Paykel could not make a profit forecast for the full year.
New Zealand market conditions were described as tough by Gary Paykel.
Fisher and Paykel lost an exclusive distribution agreement with Noel Leeming, impacting sales.
Fisher and Paykel signed an exclusive distribution agreement with Harvey Norman Holdings Ltd for New Zealand stores.

HSBC Holdings Plc, Citicorp, and Standard Chartered Plc are considered the most interested in acquiring Australia's major banks following the lifting of a foreign takeover ban.
Treasurer Peter Costello announced the end of a ban on foreign takeovers of Australia's four largest banks.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp are viewed as the most vulnerable to foreign takeovers.
Mike Pulman, an analyst at ABN AMRO, stated that HSBC is regarded as the top predator among potential acquirers.
Other potential acquirers mentioned include Lloyds TSB, ABN AMRO, Citicorp, and Deutsche Bank.
Analysts believe HSBC is unlikely to pursue ANZ due to its strong Asian presence through its Grindlays unit.
National Australia Bank Ltd is considered the least likely target for takeover due to its significant overseas assets and size.
Anusha Srinivasan, a banking analyst at Shaw Stockbroking, noted that NAB's foreign assets may not attract bidders already in those markets.
Westpac is seen as the most likely candidate for a takeover among the weaker banks due to its management's receptiveness to bids.
Standard Chartered Plc is identified as the most likely acquirer of Westpac, having already formed an alliance with the bank.

Banyan Strategic Realty Trust will report funds from operations (FFO) of $0.03 a share for the 1996 fourth quarter.
The FFO for the 1996 fourth quarter is down from $0.07 a share a year ago.
Leonard Levine is the chief executive of Banyan Strategic Realty Trust.
Banyan expects FFO for the year ended December 31 to be $0.34 a share, up from $0.32 a share a year ago.
Banyan expects FFO to increase in 1997 to between $0.50 and $0.55 a share.
The company's target for 1998 FFO is $0.65 to $0.70 a share, not including additional acquisitions.
By June 30 of this year, Banyan expects to own 19 properties in the Midwest and Southeast.
Banyan's strategy is to spread risk by focusing on smaller real estate markets and properties.
Banyan aims to improve its revenue stream and sell properties at a profit.
Leonard Levine expects Banyan to explore an equity offering within the next 12 months to raise market capital.

Mercury Finance Co. is in negotiations to extend $50 million in short-term financing from Bank of America.
The financing was granted to Mercury in February to help with daily operating expenses and interest payments.
Mercury has faced issues including overstated earnings, an FBI investigation, and multiple shareholder lawsuits.
The loan is due on Monday unless Mercury secures waivers from lenders.
A spokesman for Mercury stated that discussions for the extension were ongoing and an announcement was expected before the market opens on Tuesday.
Analyst Thomas Kmiotek indicated that Mercury expected to receive the extension.
Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co. downgraded Mercury's senior debt rating from triple-C to double-D after Mercury failed to pay $15 million in debt.
The $15 million debt was the first medium-term note due since Mercury's financial troubles began.
On January 29, Mercury announced it would lower its earnings over the last four years by about $90 million due to accounting discrepancies.
Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt, has been served with a search warrant by the FBI, hired a new CEO, and is involved in multiple lawsuits.

Cobra Electronics Corp expects to report increases in revenue and profits in 1997.
Cobra Electronics Corp reported a profitable year in 1996, its first year in the black since 1989.
Cobra Electronics Corp reported revenue of $90.3 million and net income of $601,000 in 1996.
Cobra Electronics Corp had revenue of $90.4 million and a loss of $1.1 million in 1995.
Cobra Electronics Corp completed a cost-cutting program in 1996.
Cobra Electronics Corp is introducing a system called Safety Alert.
The Safety Alert system allows drivers to receive signals alerting them to emergency vehicles and other hazards.
The Safety Alert detector will be sold for about $69.95.
The transmitter for the Safety Alert system will sell for about $300.
Cobra Electronics Corp currently has about 15 percent of the detection market and expects to grow its market share to 20 to 25 percent by the end of the year.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is a Canadian mining company.
Bre-X's Busang gold find is now considered worthless.
Bre-X's Busang discovery was claimed to be the richest find of the century.
A report by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. stated that the falsification of the Busang discovery was unprecedented in mining history.
Patrick Sheridan, a veteran mine promoter, compared the Bre-X scandal to the Windfall affair.
The Windfall Oils and Mines Ltd. affair was Canada's biggest national mining scandal before Bre-X.
The Windfall affair occurred in the 1960s during a copper and zinc rush in northern Ontario.
George and Viola MacMillan were the promoters involved in the Windfall affair.
The Kelly Commission investigated the Windfall affair and found no evidence of wrongdoing by the MacMillans.
Martin Frobisher believed he found gold on Baffin Island in 1575, but it was determined to be worthless iron pyrites.

The Busang gold controversy has negatively impacted Canada's junior mining sector.
Investment advisors predict that many investors will be scared off in 1997 due to the controversy.
John Kaiser, editor of a financial newsletter, stated that the Busang bust has ended the current junior resource market cycle.
Fund managers are expected to reduce their holdings of junior mining stocks following the Bre-X saga.
Kaiser predicted a funding drought for junior mining companies that will likely last through the rest of the year.
Retail investors are expected to remain inactive because they believe the market cycle is over.
Kaiser anticipates a return of the bull market in 1998.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd is conducting an independent audit of Bre-X's Busang project.
Preliminary tests by Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc indicated that the Busang deposit may contain insignificant amounts of gold.
The selloff of Bre-X shares last month resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion from the company's stock market value.

Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves is expected to deliver the 1997/98 budget next month.
The 1997/98 budget will be released on May 6.
Eves revised the 1996/97 budget deficit to C$7.67 billion.
The revised deficit is down C$508 million from the original budget forecast.
Economists predict the final 1996/97 deficit figure could be around C$7 billion.
Eves is expected to improve his C$6.6 billion deficit forecast for 1997/98.
Nesbitt Burns senior economist Doug Porter stated the deficit may come in below C$6 billion.
The government's contingency reserve is used to reduce the deficit if not needed for unexpected spending.
Royal Bank of Canada economist Craig Wright expects a deficit of around C$7 billion in 1996/97, falling to about C$6 billion in 1997/98.
Eves reported that government revenues grew almost C$1.2 billion higher than projected due to a rebounding economy.

Robert Lutz is the Vice Chairman of Chrysler Corp.
Lutz has reduced his corporate responsibilities.
Lutz considers himself an integral part of Chrysler's product creation activities.
Lutz gave up his president and chief operating officer titles on January 1.
Lutz's change in title is in anticipation of his 65th birthday in February.
Lutz is credited with improving Chrysler's product development operations.
Lutz instituted a system of super-efficient 'platform teams' for vehicle development.
Lutz acts as a coach and mentor for engineers and product executives.
Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton took over Lutz's chief operating officer duties.
Lutz plans to gradually ease himself out of Chrysler before turning 70.

General Motors Corp. informed analysts that its fourth-quarter North American incentive and marketing costs were higher than previously estimated.
As a result of GM's announcement, analysts reduced their earnings estimates for the company by hundreds of millions of dollars.
GM's product mix in Europe is expected to be weaker than anticipated, with the low-margin Corsa subcompact comprising a larger portion of sales.
GM's new product launch costs remain high.
Analysts lowered their estimates for GM's earnings by 45 cents to 50 cents per share, leading to a decline in GM stock by $1.375 to close at $54.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Burnham Securities analyst David Healy estimates that GM will earn $435 million, or 52 cents per share, in the fourth quarter, excluding extraordinary items.
GM plans to take a charge of $170 million, or 22 cents per share, for lump-sum payments to United Auto Workers members as part of a new contract.
GM disclosed that strikes in the United States and Canada during the quarter reduced its fourth-quarter profit by about $700 million.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, GM earned $1.87 billion, or $1.98 per share.
Analyst Michael Ward stated that GM may view the fourth quarter as a 'cleanup quarter' and could accelerate some costs to improve next year's results.

Chrysler Corp. named Robert Lutz vice chairman on Thursday.
Robert Eaton was given the title of president and will take on more day-to-day operating duties.
The chief operating officer position that Lutz held was left vacant.
Lutz is expected to stay on for two more years.
Chrysler's board increased its share buyback program to $2 billion for 1997.
Chrysler raised its annual dividend to $1.60 a share from $1.40.
The new quarterly dividend of 40 cents a share is payable on January 15 to stockholders of record as of December 15.
Chrysler has raised its dividend seven times in the past three years.
Chrysler has increased its dividend payout by 433 percent since September 1993.
Chrysler switched international and product development duties between Thomas Gale and Francois Castaing.

Britain cleared U.S. utility CE Electric's 782 million pound hostile takeover bid for Northern Electric.
The clearance occurred just days ahead of a final deadline for shareholders to accept the offer.
Trade and industry minister Ian Lang stated that CE Electric provided assurances to address regulatory concerns.
The bid is for 650 pence per share and closes next Friday.
Northern Electric claims the bid 'short changes' investors.
Prudential Corporation owns more than 11 percent of Northern Electric's shares and has purchased additional shares at 600 pence each.
Prudential traditionally supports the target company's board in hostile takeover situations.
CE Electric claims to have major investors on its side and is confident of winning the takeover.
David Sokol, CE Electric's chairman and chief executive, stated that the decision for shareholders is clear.
Northern Electric's share price increased by 41 pence to 643.50 following the news of the deal being cleared.

Tomkins Plc reported a 34 percent increase in pretax profits for the six months to November 2, amounting to 168.8 million pounds.
The dividend increased from 2.7 pence to 3.06 pence compared to the previous year.
Gregory Hutchings is the executive chairman of Tomkins Plc.
Hutchings stated that the results represent another period of outperformance for Tomkins.
Tomkins shares fell by 3.5 pence to 274 in the market after buy-back hopes were dismissed.
Hutchings ruled out the possibility of returning Tomkins's 366.8 million pound cash reserve to shareholders this year.
Hutchings indicated that Tomkins is looking at acquisition opportunities instead of a share buy-back.
Tomkins is likely to pursue several smaller acquisitions, potentially worth up to 200 million pounds.
The company has experienced earnings per share growth for 12 consecutive years.
Gates Corp contributed 259.5 million in sales and 20 million in profit in its first 14 weeks after acquisition.

The British government warned that it would refer the proposed trans-Atlantic alliance between British Airways Plc and American Airlines to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission unless conditions were met.
Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang stated that final clearance for the alliance would depend on an open skies deal between Britain and the United States.
Lang supported conditions proposed by Britain's Office of Fair Trading regarding the alliance.
Lang claimed that without suitable undertakings, the alliance would likely lead to a significant loss of actual and potential passengers on competing routes.
The latest open skies talks in London ended without a deal signed.
Industry sources reported no new date for further talks, attributing the deadlock to uncertainty over the British Airways-American deal.
The conditions for clearance of the alliance included British Airways and American Airlines dropping 168 slots at London Heathrow airport.
AMR Corp., American Airlines' parent company, stated that the terms were not a deal breaker but were more severe than those imposed by other regulatory authorities.
British Airways responded that unconditional divestiture of slots was unprecedented and should be based on fair market value.
The government requested British Airways to remove a clause in its agreement with USAir that restricts competition on trans-Atlantic routes.

3Com Corp and U.S. Robotics Corp are merging.
The merger is valued at $6.6 billion in stock.
This merger is the largest deal in the computer network industry.
The merger aims to create a competitor to Cisco Systems Inc in the Internet access business.
Analysts are divided on the merger's potential to compete with Cisco.
Bear Stearns analyst Eric Blachno commented on Cisco's market leadership.
Frank Dzubeck, an industry analyst, questioned the merger's viability.
Dzubeck compared the merger to the 1994 Bay-Wellfleet-Synoptics deal.
3Com is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
U.S. Robotics is located in Skokie, Illinois.

America Online Inc. plans to place advertising in company-sponsored discussion areas.
The company aims to expand its revenue base beyond subscriber fees.
America Online is based in Dulles, Virginia.
The advertising program is expected to generate 360 million ad impressions monthly.
An analyst estimated the program could generate $15 million to $25 million in new revenues in 1997.
Impressions measure how many times an ad is viewed.
America Online stock rose $3.75 to $43.75 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bob Pittman is the president of America Online Networks.
Over 70 percent of America Online members participate in chat.
America Online logs 1 million hours of chat every day.

Cascade Communications Corp shares experienced a significant decline on Friday.
The decline was triggered by comments made during a conference call.
The comments raised concerns about future earnings for Cascade Communications Corp.
Several analysts downgraded their ratings on Cascade Communications Corp.
Analysts expressed concern that growth rates for Cascade's core frame-relay switching business may decrease.
The expected growth rates for the core business may drop to industry levels of 30-50 percent.
Previously, the growth rates for Cascade's core business were over 100 percent.
The stock price of Cascade Communications Corp fell by 19-3/4 to 44-3/8.
All gains in the stock price since April were lost.
Cascade Communications Corp was previously considered a high-flying data networking stock.

The Internet Society approved a plan to add seven new top-level domains.
The new top-level domains will include names such as 'firm,' 'arts,' and 'web.'
The implementation of the new domains is set to start in the third quarter of 1997.
America Online Inc. has more than eight million members.
William Burrington is the director of law and public policy at America Online Inc.
Burrington stated that the plan needs more work despite praising its concept.
AT&T Corp's Worldnet service is the largest pure Internet service provider.
Mike Miller is a spokesman for AT&T Corp's Worldnet service.
Online service providers are seeking to delay the implementation of the plan.
Network Solutions Inc. is the sole registration agent for the most popular current domains.

Commuters on the Leesburg Pike in Northern Virginia are near a significant global traffic jam of digital data.
The Internet's data routes are experiencing increased traffic due to thousands of new users signing on daily.
Mark Luker, programme director of the National Science Foundation's network infrastructure project, stated that demand for the Internet is outstripping supply.
Efforts are being made to increase Internet capacity through technical solutions.
There are explorations into rationing Internet access by price based on speed and data quantity.
Mae East is a computer interchange in Northern Virginia where 46 Internet service providers exchange data.
MFS Communications Inc operates Mae East and claims it is the busiest public exchange point on the Internet.
Peak data loads at Mae East can reach 53 million bytes per second.
The National Science Foundation managed the Internet's network backbone until April 1995.
Internet traffic increased from 1.3 trillion bytes per month in March 1991 to 17.8 trillion bytes in late 1994.

The Clinton administration has developed a plan to reform U.S. banking laws.
The administration will announce its positions in the coming weeks.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will present the plan at a House Banking Committee hearing on June 3.
Under Secretary John Hawke is a key architect of the administration's plan.
Hawke is scheduled to speak on Wednesday regarding the administration's stance on banking and commerce.
There is general agreement in Congress and the finance industry to eliminate barriers between banking, securities, and insurance.
There is disagreement about allowing banks to merge with securities and other firms.
The administration's position has changed to favor limited combinations of financial and non-financial activities.
Financial firms may be restricted to a percentage of non-financial activity based on total revenue or capital.
Debate continues regarding the regulation of diverse financial businesses within a single firm.

The Prague Stock Exchange gained ground on Thursday.
Analysts are not convinced that the fortunes of the Prague Stock Exchange have turned around.
The rise in the Prague Stock Exchange is attributed to thin domestic buying.
The bourse has gained in 15 of the past 16 sessions.
Analysts observed little change in market sentiment amid mostly domestic trading.
The PX50 index was up 0.25 percent at 519.5 at its daily price fixing on Thursday.
The bourse is 8.3 percent higher than its low in mid-November.
The Prague Stock Exchange lost close to 20 percent during most of the autumn.
The Czech market has been plagued by poor legislation that fails to protect minority shareholders.
The Securities Registry is bound by law to provide services related to securities transactions.

The Czech crown has recently gained strength due to increased demand from Eurobond issues.
Market speculation exists regarding possible central bank intervention in the Czech crown.
The Czech National Bank (CNB) is monitoring the development of the crown.
The CNB is prepared to allow the market to determine the crown's rate within a fluctuation band.
Since the start of 1997, the Czech crown has gained approximately three percentage points against its fixing basket.
The gain in the crown is mainly attributed to foreign buying for financing new crown Eurobond issues totaling about 30 billion crowns.
Analysts predict the crown may hold steady for a short period but could test 5.5 percent above its parity level next week.
Martin Strauch, a dealer at Citibank, stated that he does not expect significant movement in the crown this week.
The Czech crown is fixed daily at a rate that allows for fluctuations of plus or minus 7.5 percent from the mid-point of a currency basket.
On Wednesday, the CNB fixed the crown at 27.712 to the dollar and 16.846 to the mark, which is 5.05 percent above the mid-point.

The Czech economy is showing signs of slower growth and a widening trade gap.
Analysts expressed concerns about the pace of industrial restructuring in the Czech economy.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has been praised for achieving low inflation rates, good GDP growth, and a low unemployment rate of about three percent.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported a record trade deficit of 160.33 billion crowns for 1996.
The trade deficit increased from a 95.7 billion crown shortfall the previous year.
Some economists are concerned about the export competitiveness of Czech industry.
Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka, stated that competition from other transforming economies is increasing.
Since 1992, the Czech economy has transitioned from recession to a consumption-driven real growth of 4.8 percent in 1995.
Unemployment in the Czech Republic remains around three percent, with nearly 70 percent of the economy in private hands.
The current account showed a deficit of $3.1 billion crowns for the first three quarters of the year.

NatWest Markets announced a restructuring of its global debt markets division.
Power has been shifted to managers from Greenwich Capital, which NatWest acquired last year.
The restructuring is not related to a reported loss of 90 million pounds by the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank Plc.
Gary Holloway and Chip Kruger are the co-chief executives of the new global debt markets division.
Holloway will be based in Greenwich, United States, and will oversee U.S. and Asian operations.
Kruger will be based in London and will manage European debt market operations.
Greg Bowes has been appointed head of government bonds, repos, and futures and options.
Frank Canelas will lead corporate bonds origination, sales, trading, and research.
Bruce Snider has been appointed head of asset-backed origination, structuring, and trading.
Phil Lotz is the chief administrative officer for operations, IT, and finance.

Britain's opposition Labour party does not plan to revolutionise the regulatory structure of the financial services industry if it wins the election.
The ruling Conservative government must call the election by May.
Mike O'Brien is Labour's shadow economic secretary.
O'Brien stated that Labour is discussing a developmental process involving reform rather than revolution.
Labour plans to merge the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) with existing Self-Regulatory Organisations (SROs).
The SIB currently supervises frontline regulators that authorise firms to conduct investment business, monitor them, handle complaints, and punish rule-breakers.
O'Brien believes the current regulatory system is overly bureaucratic and expensive.
Labour does not intend to establish an equivalent to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Labour prefers a regulatory system that is flexible and responsive to changes in the market.
Labour is consulting with industry participants about providing financial services to low-income groups.

A group of U.S. and European firms developed a system for money transactions over the Internet.
The team includes AT & T Corp Unisource, Apple Computer Inc, Nokia Oy, and Mondex UK.
The project will run on a pilot basis.
Julian Wilson, Unisource's director of service development, stated that protocols for shopping and banking have been developed.
The system allows users to pay for electronic services via the Internet.
Wilson claimed the system was a world first involving the transfer of electronic cash from one device to another.
The developers described the system as the world's first trial of fast and safe money transactions over the Internet.
The system will use the GSM network for Internet access.
The system aims to allow Internet users to buy services and access information using smart cards.
The initial pilot is being carried out with National Westminster Bank Plc.

China has pledged to open its insurance, stock, retail, wholesale, and banking sectors to foreign investment.
The pledge is part of China's efforts for entry into the World Trade Organisation.
From 1997 to 2000, China is expected to open its insurance and stock market wider to foreign investment.
The information was reported by the China Daily, quoting Ma Jixian from the State Economic and Trade Commission.
The pledge was included in a unilateral action plan submitted by China to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
Foreign insurers will have access to markets outside Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou before the end of the decade.
China's insurance market was previously monopolized by the state-owned People's Insurance Group.
