Currently, only three foreign insurers can write insurance policies in China: American International Assurance Co. Ltd, Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co. Ltd, and a joint venture with a domestic insurer.
Foreign stock companies will be allowed to handle A shares, which are currently only available to native Chinese.
China plans to cut its average import tariffs to about 15 percent from the current 23 percent.

China rejected an invitation for its top policymaker to visit Taiwan on Tuesday.
China stated that Taiwan must first abandon its bid to break out of diplomatic isolation.
A spokesman for the Taiwan Affairs Office said it was impossible for Wang Zhaoguo to accept the invitation.
The spokesman indicated that the time for such a visit was not ripe due to Taiwan's foreign policy.
The spokesman advised Taiwan not to seek entry into the United Nations.
Taipei lost its United Nations seat to Beijing in 1971.
China considers Taiwan a rebel province and denies it official links with other states.
If Wang had accepted the invitation, he would have been the most senior Chinese official to visit Taiwan since 1949.
A Taiwanese business leader quoted Wang as saying he would be happy to visit Taiwan if given the opportunity.
China has increased pressure on Taiwan to lift a ban on direct trade and transport links.

Liu Xiaobo has filed a lawsuit against Beijing authorities for sending him to a labour camp without trial.
Liu Xiaobo's wife stated that he urged Beijing's Xuanwu District Court to overturn a decision by the Beijing Re-education through Labour Committee.
Liu Xiaobo's lawsuit claims he refuses to accept the decision to send him to a labour camp for three years.
Liu Xiaobo stated that he is appealing to defend his right to freedom of speech as a law-abiding citizen.
Liu Xiaobo was detained by police in September and sent to a camp in Dalian for three years of re-education through labour.
Re-education through labour is a form of administrative punishment imposed by authorities without a trial.
Western human rights activists claim that re-education through labour is used to remove dissidents from circulation without trial complications.
Liu Xiaobo's wife reported that the court agreed to hear the lawsuit, but no date has been set.
Authorities at the labour camp rejected requests from Liu Xiaobo's family to visit him.
The Re-education through Labour Committee accused Liu Xiaobo of various offences related to a government petition and a newspaper article.

Coles Myer Ltd is expected to report its first profit rise in almost two years on Thursday.
Improved margins are helping to offset sluggish sales growth and boost first half profit by about five percent.
Analysts expect Coles Myer to report a net profit before abnormals of about A$200 million to A$205 million for the 26 weeks to January 26.
This net profit is an increase from A$194.5 million in the first half of 1995/96.
This will be Coles' first profit rise since 1995.
Coles Myer has experienced a two-year period of board turmoil and controversy over corporate governance.
Analysts expect margins to have improved most at Coles' K-Mart discount department store chain in pre-Christmas trading.
K-Mart's improved margins are attributed to a refusal to discount heavily.
Kmart produced earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of A$50.6 million in the first half of 1995/96, down from A$93.2 million the previous comparable half.
Coles' supermarket division is also seen improving as sales have held up in the food sector.

Papua New Guinea's Australian-listed stocks rallied on Thursday.
Foreign investors reacted positively to the peaceful resolution of a 10-day political crisis in Papua New Guinea.
Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan decided to step aside, which calmed the political situation.
David Walker, Head of Mining Research at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, stated that the parliamentary process worked and avoided military control.
Walker noted that there is an expectation for mid-year elections to be brought forward.
Chan stepped down due to pressure related to his hiring of mercenaries to suppress an uprising on Bougainville island.
Orogen Minerals Ltd closed up eight cents at A$3.10.
Oil Search Ltd closed up 13 cents at A$2.70.
Lihir Gold Ltd rose two cents to A$2.15.
Collins and Leahy Ltd closed up 25 cents at A$3.50.

Natwest Markets Australia Ltd aims to maintain its leading market share in equities broking in Australia in 1997.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd will avoid the mortgage securitisation sector.
Peter St George is the chief executive of Natwest Markets Australia Ltd.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd currently has a 9.8 percent market share in equities broking in Australia.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd plans to broaden and deepen its market penetration.
Natwest Markets Australia Ltd needs to widen its research and distribution activities to adapt to changes in the Australian stock market over the next two to three years.
The privatisation of Telstra Corp and the sale of government-owned airports will change the market.
The demutualisation of The Australian Mutual Provident Society will also impact the market.
Natwest Markets Australia reported a 40 percent rise in operating profit before tax to A$70.5 million for calendar 1996.
Natwest's debt and corporate finance divisions will focus on non-government debt operations and avoid securitised mortgage deals.

Caterpillar Inc is concerned that the continued strength of the dollar could pressure its pricing.
The impact of the dollar's strength was minimal in the first quarter of the year.
Douglas Oberhelman is the chief financial officer of Caterpillar Inc.
Caterpillar Inc has restructured its business to manage an overvalued dollar.
The restructuring includes increased overseas production.
The dollar is at a multi-year high against the yen.
Oberhelman stated that pricing competition from Japanese competitors could occur later this year due to the strong dollar.
Oberhelman indicated that continued strength of the dollar could lead to price erosion later in the year.
Caterpillar expects profits in 1997 to rise from 1996 due to moderately higher sales.
Caterpillar reported net income of $394 million for the first quarter, an increase from $296 million a year ago.

Hyatt Hotels Corp. will spend $1 billion over the next three years to acquire 20 to 30 hotels.
Target properties will be upscale hotels and resorts in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.
Hyatt has already made two deals typical of its expansion plan.
A Hyatt affiliate purchased the Grand Hyatt San Francisco, which Hyatt has managed since 1973.
Hyatt will take over management of the Hotel Nikko Atlanta after acquiring the hotel in partnership with Blackstone Real Estate Partners.
The Hotel Nikko Atlanta will be renamed the Grand Hyatt Atlanta.
Hyatt's plan was facilitated by a recent reorganization of some Pritzker family holdings.
The Pritzker family formed Hyatt Equities L.L.C., a real estate acquisition company.
Hyatt Equities consolidates the family's hotel real estate interests into one company.
Hyatt Equities debt will be rated by Standard and Poor's and Moody's.

Warm weather increased sales of spring merchandise in February.
Flooding in the Midwest may negatively impact retail results in March.
Most winter clothing was sold out by January and early February.
Retailers were adequately stocked for spring merchandise.
Salomon Bros. reported a 4.7 percent increase in same-store sales in February.
The same-store sales increase in February was lower than the 5.2 percent rise a year ago.
January same-store sales rose by 7.3 percent.
Harry Ikenson, an analyst at Rodman & Renshaw Inc., stated that early trends for spring fashion are positive.
William Kellogg, chairman of Kohl's Corp., noted that clearance merchandise levels were lower than the previous year.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc. reported a 6.7 percent increase in same-store sales.

The Busang rumor mill was active on Wednesday.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc extended its review of the Busang gold project.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd announced that Freeport was granted an extension for its due diligence review until June 30.
Freeport requested the extension to consider the findings of the Strathcona audit.
Rumors about Busang began after Freeport's preliminary due diligence tests found insignificant amounts of gold.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of almost C$3 billion or 80 percent of the company's market value last month.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd is expected to deliver a key report on Busang to Bre-X on Thursday or Friday.
Bre-X plans to issue a press release on the report before North American financial markets open on Monday.
Freeport spokeswoman Kristin Lemkau stated that the request for the extension was made within the past week.
Bre-X shares closed down C32 cents at C$3.48 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is considering merger offers at the right price.
Bre-X is currently focused on developing the Busang gold discovery with existing partners.
David Walsh is the Chief Executive of Bre-X.
Bre-X owns 45 percent of the Busang discovery.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. owns 15 percent of the Busang discovery.
PT Askatindo Karya Minerals and PT Amsya Lyna and partners own 30 percent of the Busang discovery.
The Indonesian government owns 10 percent of the Busang discovery.
Bre-X executives estimate that the Busang gold field may contain as much as 200 million ounces of gold.
Placer Dome Inc. stated that its $5 billion merger offer for Bre-X is no longer feasible.
Bre-X's partners do not have rights of first refusal if Bre-X receives a third-party offer.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd's chief executive and senior geologist were recognized as Canada's top prospectors in March.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc withdrew from the Busang gold project after a consultant's report deemed it a fraud.
The consultant's report stated that Busang was the biggest fraud in mining history.
Freeport confirmed its own poor test results from the Busang site.
Freeport's chief executive Jim Bob Moffett noted that the first sign of issues at Busang was from PT Indo Assay Laboratories.
PT Indo Assay Laboratories could not find significant amounts of gold in Freeport's samples.
Moffett attempted to contact Bre-X Minerals Chief Executive David Walsh and Chief of Exploration John Felderhof.
Both Walsh and Felderhof were in Toronto to receive awards at a gala ceremony hosted by the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada.
Bre-X's chief geologist, Michael de Guzman, attended the conference in Toronto.
A report by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd stated that the Busang discovery was falsified on an unprecedented scale.

Chrysler Corp. agreed to sell Pentastar Electronics Inc. to a management-led investment group for less than $50 million.
Pentastar Electronics is based in Huntsville, Ala., and produces electronic test equipment for tanks and military systems.
Pentastar Electronics has about 350 employees and annual sales in the $50-million range.
The terms of the sale to PEI Acquisition Corp. were not announced, but the price is less than Pentastar's annual revenues.
Chrysler hopes to close the sale before the end of 1996, but conditions may delay it into 1997.
A company spokeswoman did not disclose whether Chrysler would book a gain on the deal.
The new company will operate as PEI Electronics Inc. and negotiated changes to the United Auto Workers contract at the plant.
The deal preserved UAW wages and benefits for current workers but allowed PEI to hire new workers at lower wages.
PEI won permission to change work rules and job classifications to improve efficiency.
PEI expects to hire about 200 new workers over the next 12 months as it executes expansion plans.

United Auto Workers leaders will likely choose a strike target among the Big Three automakers in the next few days.
The UAW has less than two weeks to craft a pattern-setting labour agreement.
UAW Vice President Ernest Lofton stated that the UAW is focusing on General Motors Corp. and Ford Motor Co.
Chrysler Corp. is not likely to be the lead company because it is the Canadian Auto Workers' strike target.
Labour contracts for about 400,000 UAW and 53,000 CAW hourly workers expire on September 14.
The Canadian Auto Workers have extended their deadline until September 17.
Lofton indicated that the U.S. target selection needs to happen this week.
Some UAW officials suggested an announcement could occur as early as Tuesday.
Historically, the UAW's target choice has been made before Labour Day.
UAW President Stephen Yokich delayed the target choice to allow a company to demonstrate willingness to meet union demands.

Chrysler Corp unveiled five concept cars on Sunday.
The concept cars include two new versions of the Jeep Wrangler sport/utility vehicle.
One of the concept cars is a new Dodge roadster based on the Plymouth Prowler chassis.
Another concept car is an affordable Neon-based small car with a roll-back top.
There is also a 1940s-style 'dual-cowl' convertible among the concept cars.
Thomas Gale is Chrysler's new product development chief.
Gale stated that no decision has been made to take any of the concept cars to market.
Chrysler will monitor consumer reactions to the vehicles at this year's auto show circuit.
Positive public reaction has previously led Chrysler to put concept cars into volume production.
The concept cars were unveiled at the start of Detroit's North American International Auto Show.

Ford Motor Co's Halewood plant in England employs four and a half thousand workers.
A meeting between Ford management and unions is scheduled for Thursday to discuss the plant's future.
Reports indicate that Ford may announce 1,500 job cuts at the meeting.
A Ford spokesman declined to comment on speculation regarding the plant's future.
Ford has not issued any statements regarding workforce reductions or plant restructuring in Britain.
A statement from Ford is expected at midday on Thursday.
The Transport and General Workers Union is involved in the discussions and will hold a press briefing at the plant.
The unions stated they had not received confirmation of job cuts from Ford prior to the meeting.
Ford's group boss Alex Trotman warned last year about taking drastic actions to address losses in Europe.
Analysts believe it is unlikely that Ford will close the Halewood plant and eliminate all 5,000 jobs.

BAA Plc is a British airports group that operates London Heathrow, Europe's largest airport hub.
BAA Plc reported a 6.2 percent increase in pretax profits for the nine months ending December 31.
The pretax profits for the period were 397 million pounds, equivalent to 636.5 million dollars.
Total revenue for the period increased to 1.06 billion pounds from 987 million pounds.
76.6 million passengers traveled through BAA's airports, which include Gatwick and Stansted.
Airport and traffic charge revenue was 385 million pounds, an increase of 5.5 percent.
Retailing revenue reached 475 million pounds, up 10 percent, resulting in net retail income of 331 million pounds, which is an 11 percent increase.
Property income rose by 8.4 percent to 168 million pounds.
BAA's shares fell by seven pence to 525 pence per share following the report.
BAA is submitting bids to operate overseas airports and has decided to reduce its stake in a bid group for three Australian airports.

Britain approved CE Electric's 782 million pound bid for Northern Electric.
CE Electric's bid is valued at $1.3 billion.
Analysts believe CE Electric is likely to succeed in acquiring Northern Electric.
CE Electric holds a 29 percent market share.
Ian Lang is the trade and industry minister who approved the bid.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy.
CE Electric increased its bid to 650 pence per share from 630 pence on December 6.
The deadline for acceptances of the bid is December 20.
Northern Electric claims the bid undervalues the company and suggests a price of 700 pence per share.
Prudential Corporation owns more than 11 percent of Northern Electric's shares.

A device was introduced that turns a personal computer into an automated teller machine capable of dispensing card-based electronic cash.
Fischer International Systems Corp. developed the device, which costs $60 and can be inserted into the floppy disk drive of any PC.
The device enables PCs to read 'smart cards,' which can perform electronic cash transactions and store bank account balances.
Smart cards are gaining popularity in Europe for store purchases and telephone calls and are beginning to be adopted in the United States.
The device may stimulate home banking by allowing consumers to perform financial transactions without visiting a bank branch or ATM.
Fischer President Michael Battaglia stated that a low-cost, easy-to-use 'bridge' between smart cards and personal computers was previously missing.
The product, named Smarty, connects PCs to banks or retail outlets via the Internet.
Fischer holds key patents for smart card readers that fit into 3.5-inch floppy drives, making Smarty adaptable for 200 million personal computers.
The device allows consumers to use banking cards for purchases, reducing the need to carry cash.
Fischer is collaborating with major U.S. and European financial services firms and is in discussions with home banking software providers like Intuit Inc. and Microsoft Corp.

New York state utility regulators approved the $23 billion merger between Nynex Corp. and Bell Atlantic Corp.
The approval is subject to conditions that must be agreed upon by the companies by the end of March.
Consumer groups opposed the merger and criticized the decision as a sellout.
New York was the last state in Nynex's six-state service region to approve the merger.
The merger would create the largest local phone company in the United States, serving customers in 12 Northeastern states and Washington.
John O'Mara, Chairman of the New York State Public Service Commission, stated that improved service quality and tangible benefits for ratepayers are requirements for approval.
O'Mara indicated that there would be no immediate rate reduction but conditions attached could lead to rate reductions in the future.
The merger is currently under review by federal regulators for its competitive implications.
Bell Atlantic spokesman Eric Rabe stated that the companies expect the deal to close after April 22.
State Attorney General Dennis Vacco expressed concern that the decision did not adequately protect ratepayers.

AT&T Corp. reported a 17 percent decline in first-quarter profits.
AT&T's profits were affected by competition in long-distance services and investments in new businesses.
AT&T warned that second quarter results might also be weak.
BellSouth Corp. reported an 11 percent increase in operating earnings.
BellSouth's earnings growth was attributed to an increase in customer lines and strong wireless operations.
AT&T earned $1.13 billion, or 69 cents a share, on revenues of $13.05 billion in the first quarter.
In the first quarter of 1996, AT&T had a net income of $1.36 billion, or 85 cents a share, on revenues of $12.85 billion.
AT&T's earnings per share for the first quarter met Wall Street's expectations.
AT&T's first quarter revenue increase was driven by growth in local telephone service, business long-distance services, and wireless services.
BellSouth earned $693 million, or 70 cents a share, on revenues of $4.8 billion in the three months ended March 31.

The International Monetary Fund opened a website on Thursday providing information about economic data in 18 member countries.
Jack Boorman is the director of the IMF's policy and review department.
Boorman stated that the IMF has been urging countries to report data more timely and based on good statistical systems.
The 1994-95 Mexican peso crisis emphasized the need for timely and accurate data about developing countries.
The website does not include actual data from the countries but provides contacts for obtaining that information.
Boorman mentioned that good statistical citizenship helps to inform markets.
The purpose of the system is to ensure that markets receive better data in a timely manner.
The website's address is http://dsbb.imf.org.
The site lists information about the frequency, schedule, and types of economic and financial data released by countries subscribed to the Special Data Dissemination Standard.
The countries listed on the site are Argentina, Canada, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico, the Netherlands, Norway, Peru, the Philippines, Singapore, Slovenia, Switzerland, Thailand, Britain, and the United States.

U.S. lawmakers are redrafting a legislative proposal to modernize U.S. banking laws.
The redraft will rely heavily on the Clinton administration's reform plan.
The new draft of the proposal is expected to be finished by Friday.
The House Banking Committee will begin formal consideration of the proposal next week.
Committee spokesman David Runkel stated the goal is to include areas of general agreement in the bill.
Runkel mentioned the intent is to use as much of the Treasury Department's language as appropriate.
The most controversial questions will be resolved during the mark up as lawmakers offer amendments.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin unveiled the administration's plan to overhaul U.S. banking laws on May 21.
Rubin urged Congress to scrap the 1933 Glass-Steagall Act to allow banks to enter other financial sectors.
At least four major areas of disagreement remain that will be the focus of the scheduled June 11 mark up.

Bankers Trust New York Corp. and Alex. Brown Inc. have merged.
The merger indicates that the nation's banking laws are outdated.
Karen Shaw Petrou is the president of the consulting firm ISD/Shaw.
Petrou stated that the banking industry is modernizing despite Congress's slow progress on legislation.
Legislators have debated repealing the Glass-Steagall Act of 1933 for over a decade.
The Glass-Steagall Act prohibits banks from offering certain financial services like securities or insurance.
Federal courts and bank regulators have reduced the impact of Glass-Steagall in the past year.
Larry LaRocco is a bank industry lobbyist and former congressman.
LaRocco claimed that Glass-Steagall is effectively dead and that other issues need to be addressed.
Bankers Trust announced it would acquire Alex. Brown in a stock deal valued at $1.7 billion.

The Prague Stock Exchange's 1997 bull run ended on Thursday as investors took profits.
Analysts predicted little change in the bourse's fortunes over the short-term.
The PX50 index retreated 9.0 points, or 1.43 percent, to 618.6.
The PX50 index had increased over 16 percent since the beginning of the year.
The PX50 index reached a two-year high of 629.0 on Tuesday.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka each fell more than 2.2 percent at the price fixing.
Jan Sykora of Wood and Company stated that the market is thin and profit-taking causes it to collapse.
Analysts expect Komercni to be hardest hit among blue chips after rising over 25 percent since the start of the year.
The Central Securities Registry began publishing stock trade information on February 4.
The Finance Ministry's markets supervision department has been transformed into a Bureau for the Control of Securities.

A wave of high-yielding Czech crown Eurobonds has flooded the debt market since the beginning of the year.
Interest rates have eased and arbitrage opportunities have declined.
Ota Otepka, chief bond trader at ING Barings, stated that the Euro-madness is over.
Issuers have rushed to take advantage of a stable, strong currency and interest rates above 11 percent.
Nearly 30 billion crowns worth of Eurobonds were issued in just over four weeks.
The appetite for crown Eurobonds appeared insatiable due to high interest rates and favorable currency conditions.
Interest rates have eased by 60-70 basis points since the start of the year, leading to a drop in yields.
Jan Pudil of WoodCommerz suggested that lead managers may have been overly optimistic about foreign investors' appetite.
More than 20 bond issues were launched in crowns by top-rated, retail-friendly issuers.
Analysts estimate that about 90 percent of the crown bonds were bought by retail investors from Germany, the Benelux countries, and Switzerland.

The Czech trade deficit for December was 18.0 billion crowns ($650 million).
The full year 1996 trade deficit was a record 160.33 billion crowns.
A Reuters survey forecasted a December deficit of about 16 billion crowns.
The December 1995 trade gap was 14.3 billion crowns.
The overall trade deficit for 1995 was 95.7 billion crowns.
Imports for 1996 totaled 755.3 billion crowns, a year-on-year rise of 12.7 percent.
Exports in 1996 totaled 594.95 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of 3.5 percent.
Machinery imports for 1996 reached 288.5 billion crowns, an increase of 16.1 percent over 1995.
Imports of raw materials, unprocessed goods, and chemical products totaled 327.9 billion crowns, a 10.2 percent year-on-year increase.
Exports in the raw materials, unprocessed goods, and chemical products sector reached 280.6 billion crowns, but contracted by 4.2 percent year-on-year.

British banks have developed a greater understanding of the needs of small firms, according to a report from the Bank of England.
The Bank of England's report was released on Wednesday.
Howard Davies is the deputy governor of the Bank of England.
Davies stated that relationships between small firms and their banks have improved from a low point four years ago.
Davies expressed that there is still much to be done in financing small firms.
The report identified small exporters and ethnic minority businesses as areas needing particular attention.
Bank finance is the main form of external finance used by small firms, defined as businesses with a turnover up to and including a million pounds a year.
Asset-backed finance has been increasing as a proportion of external finance for small firms.
There was a 19 percent increase in the number of firms using factoring services in 1996.
The report noted that term loans now account for around two thirds of the total 35 billion pounds of bank lending to small firms.

NatWest Markets' senior management did not know about the interest rate options pricing problem until three days before the losses were made public.
A NatWest spokeswoman stated that senior management did not know until February 25 that there was potentially something of significance.
The spokeswoman denied a weekend newspaper report suggesting that NatWest knew of the losses before they were revealed.
NatWest revealed that the mispricings totaled 90 million pounds ($144 million).
The mispricings were discovered during normal pricing reviews.
NatWest was unable to estimate the loss until February 28, when it was estimated at 50 million pounds.
The initial discovery of the loss came through a more intensive review across the investment bank's trading areas.
The extent of the mispricings became clear about a month after the initial discovery.
Martin Owen, the chief executive of NatWest Markets, stated he would forgo 200,000 of a 500,000 pound bonus due to the affair.
Kyriacos Papouis, the former NatWest options trader, has not commented on the losses and has resigned from Bear Stearns.

Britain lost an independent corporate finance adviser with the sale of Phoenix Group to Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
The financial details of the deal were not disclosed, but speculation suggested it was worth around 50 million pounds.
The sale would make multi-millionaires of Phoenix's top directors, who are major shareholders.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette aimed to acquire Phoenix's British mergers and acquisitions expertise.
Some experts considered the price paid for Phoenix to be high given its relatively slim revenues and profits.
Phoenix was established in 1981 and was acquired by Morgan Grenfell in 1987.
Phoenix regained its independence in 1990 through a management buyout led by Martin Smith, Philip Seers, and David Reid Scott.
In 1996, Phoenix advised on transactions worth around 2.5 billion pounds.
In August of the previous year, Phoenix was ranked second by Acquisitions Monthly among British-based independent corporate finance houses.
The new firm will be called DLJ Phoenix, with Martin Smith as chairman and all 25 directors and staff retained.

China has jailed two Mongolians for up to 15 years on charges of separatism and espionage.
Amnesty International reported that Hada, 41, was sentenced to 15 years in prison and Tegexi, 30, was sentenced to 10 years.
Chinese courts rejected the appeals of Hada and Tegexi last month and upheld their original sentences.
Hada and Tegexi were held for a year in solitary confinement without charges or a trial.
Amnesty International stated that no evidence has been made public to show that Hada and Tegexi were involved in any criminal activity under international standards.
Amnesty International called for the immediate and unconditional release of Hada and Tegexi.
The Amnesty report could not be independently confirmed.
Eight others were detained in December for alleged involvement in nationalist separatist activities but were subsequently released.
Hada and Tegexi were being detained in poor conditions and their health was suffering.
Hada has a recurrence of tuberculosis and it is unknown if he received any medical treatment in prison.

Beijing's propaganda machine has accused the United States of using the Dalai Lama as a tool to Westernise and break up China.
The Tibet Daily claimed that Western countries, led by the United States, have targeted China with their Westernisation and disintegration campaign.
The Tibet Daily stated that the Dalai Lama clique is used by the West to implement an anti-Chinese strategy.
The Dalai Lama received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989.
Sino-U.S. relations have been strained by disputes over Tibet, Taiwan, human rights abuses, and copyright piracy in China.
China blames followers of the Dalai Lama for periodic unrest in the Himalayan region bordering India.
The Dalai Lama seeks autonomy and freedom of worship in Tibet.
The Dalai Lama fled to India in 1959 after an uprising against communist rule.
The Tibet Daily criticized Western criticism of China's human rights record, stating that sovereign rights are more important than human rights.
Chinese authorities have offered a reward of one million yuan for information on a bomb set off outside government offices in Lhasa.

Chinese police arrested the suspected ringleader of a riot in Xinjiang that resulted in at least 10 deaths and 144 injuries.
Local officials reported the arrests on Wednesday.
Authorities issued emergency circulars to local officials to combat separatism in Xinjiang.
Severe punishment was warned for the rioters involved in last week's events.
Government units were ordered to form vigilante squads in Yining to guard against potential separatist attacks.
Zhang Youlian is the deputy director of the foreign affairs office for the Yili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture.
Police arrested Abudu Heilili, a 29-year-old Uighur, and began interrogating him after the riot.
Heilili was previously involved in a less violent anti-Chinese demonstration in Yining in August 1995.
Following the 1995 protest, Heilili was released after undergoing political indoctrination.
Police rounded up 200 to 300 people after last week's riot, with many suspects released after questioning.

Rural Press Ltd announced on Thursday that it is not confident of an economic turnaround needed to increase its profit for the full year to June 30, 1997.
Managing director Brian McCarthy expressed that a significant turnaround in consumer markets and real estate is some time away.
McCarthy stated that he does not foresee much improvement until at least the middle of the year.
Rural Press reported a four percent rise in net profit for the six months to December, amounting to A$16.96 million.
Rural Press declared an unchanged dividend of four cents per share.
The company warned that trading in the first five weeks of the second half had been below last year.
Rural Press indicated that it needs an improvement in the economy to continue its history of profit rises for the full year.
McCarthy noted that earnings before interest and tax would have fallen marginally in the half year on a like-for-like basis before acquisitions.
McCarthy attributed the slight profit fall on a like-for-like basis to weak real estate and retail sectors, which are key sources of advertising income.
Rural Press' share price closed unchanged at A$4.10, despite an overall market rise of one percent to a record high.

Boral Ltd reported a lower net profit for the first half year.
Boral Ltd stated it is poised to take advantage of an upturn in the house building sector.
Tony Berg is the managing director of Boral.
Boral's building materials division is positioned to exploit the upturn.
Boral reported a net profit of A$93.16 million for the six months to December 31.
The net profit of A$93.16 million is down from A$169.71 million in the same period a year earlier.
The decrease in net profit was largely due to a A$49.5 million abnormal profit from an asset sale in the previous year.
Net profit pre-abnormals fell to A$96 million from A$120 million the previous year.
Market expectations for pre-abnormals net profit were about A$90 million.
Analysts noted that the result was slightly above expectations due to stronger performance from Boral's U.S. building materials operations.

Allan Fels is the chairman of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Fels expressed a neutral attitude regarding Westpac Banking Corp's A$1.435 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
Fels confirmed that he informed Westpac two years ago that the ACCC would be hesitant to allow a takeover of Bank of Melbourne.
The ACCC acknowledged that structural change may occur to allow a future takeover.
Fels stated that the ACCC evaluates mergers on a case-by-case basis.
Fels mentioned that the earlier informal discussions with Westpac occurred in September 1995.
During the 1995 discussions, wider issues about regional mergers were addressed.
Fels indicated that the ACCC had issued a statement suggesting hesitation about Westpac's bid for Bank of Melbourne at that time.
Fels clarified that the hesitation regarding Westpac-Bank of Melbourne only applied at that time.
Fels did not agree with claims of significant structural change in the regional banking sector.

Mercury Finance Co.'s agreement to buy a consumer finance business fell apart on Thursday.
Mercury Finance stated that phony bookkeeping entries had inflated its earnings.
Mercury Finance fired its chief accountant due to the inflated earnings.
The officer blamed for the overstated earnings may be cooperating with federal authorities.
BankBoston Corp. terminated its agreement to sell its Fidelity Acceptance Corp. unit to Mercury Finance.
The deal was valued at 32.7 million shares of Mercury stock.
When the deal was announced on January 10, the stock was worth about $458 million.
Mercury Finance stock closed at $14.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
Traders reported that Mercury Finance stock was changing hands at $4.25 overseas.
Mercury Finance stated that its 1996 earnings would be restated to $56.7 million from $120.7 million.

Hyatt Hotels Corp. will spend $1 billion over the next three years to acquire 20 to 30 hotels.
The target properties will be upscale three- to five-star hotels and resorts in the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.
Hyatt has already made two deals that are typical of its expansion plan.
A Hyatt affiliate purchased the Grand Hyatt San Francisco for $125 million plus $5 million in debt.
Hyatt will take over management of the Hotel Nikko Atlanta after acquiring it for $90 million in partnership with Blackstone Real Estate Partners.
The Hotel Nikko Atlanta will be renamed the Grand Hyatt Atlanta.
Hyatt operates 176 Hyatt hotels and resorts around the world.
Hyatt purchased 12 hotels in the past three years.
The more aggressive acquisition stance is seen as a response to acquisition plans by Hyatt's competitors.
Hyatt Equities L.L.C. was formed to consolidate the Pritzker family's hotel real estate interests.

Kmart Corp. will spend $750 million over the next three years to convert nearly all of its outlets to a new concept called 'Big Kmart.'
The Big Kmart concept aims to help shoppers save time and money by reorganizing merchandise and displaying it in wider aisles.
Chairman Floyd Hall stated that the new store represents a significant change for Kmart.
The Big Kmart concept is expected to increase sales at existing stores by 20 percent per square foot.
297 stores have been converted to the Big Kmart format so far.
Another 333 stores are scheduled for conversion in 1997.
Most of Kmart's more than 2,000 traditional stores will be converted by 1999.
Big Kmart stores are the same size as traditional stores, ranging from 60,000 to 80,000 square feet.
The Big Kmart concept organizes merchandise into three areas: home fashions, children's apparel and toys, and consumables.
Big Kmart stores will feature a new Pantry department with food and household products.

Canada's top securities regulator is probing Bre-X Minerals Ltd for potential breaches of insider trading and disclosure laws.
The Ontario Securities Commission has been investigating Bre-X Minerals since the end of 1996.
The OSC confirmed that the investigation relates to continuous disclosure requirements and insider trading provisions.
The OSC has not determined if there is enough information to begin formal proceedings against Bre-X.
The investigation is focusing on potential breaches of Ontario's Securities Act.
A group of Canadian Bre-X shareholders launched a class action lawsuit on Thursday.
Bre-X Minerals faces five court actions in the United States.
The Toronto Stock Exchange halted trading of Bre-X shares due to heavy order volumes on Thursday.
A report on Bre-X's assay program confirmed the company's original findings but raised new questions.
Panic selling resulted in a nearly C$3 billion loss in Bre-X's market value last Thursday.

Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. withdrew from the Busang gold project.
The Busang gold project was previously claimed to be the richest find of the century by Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
A report by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. stated that the Busang discovery was falsified on an unprecedented scale.
Freeport-McMoRan confirmed its poor test results from the Busang site through the Strathcona report.
Freeport announced it would notify Bre-X of its withdrawal from the Busang project based on its contractual agreement.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh stated that investigators would uncover the details of the scandal.
Strathcona found evidence of tampering with Bre-X's core samples.
Strathcona's tests revealed only trace amounts of gold at the Busang site.
The report indicated that a gold deposit worth mining was unlikely to be found at the Busang site.
Nusamba Group, linked to Indonesian President Suharto, also withdrew from the Busang project.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is based in Calgary, Alberta.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. reported a gold discovery at the Busang deposit in Indonesia.
Doubts about the Busang deposit and the death of chief geologist Michael de Guzman led to a decline in Bre-X stock.
Trading of Bre-X shares was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange due to a report from an Indonesian newspaper.
The report claimed that Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. found the Busang deposit to be smaller than Bre-X's estimate of 71 million ounces.
Freeport-McMoRan stated that its review of the Busang site was not finished.
Bre-X stock fell to a 52-week low of C$14.25 during trading.
Bre-X closed down C$2.25 at C$15.20 with a trading volume of 9 million shares.
Michael de Guzman, the chief geologist of Bre-X, died after falling from a helicopter in Indonesia.
Indonesian officials suggested that de Guzman may have committed suicide, and his body has not been found.

Chrysler Corp. reported better-than-expected fourth quarter earnings.
Chrysler's fourth quarter earnings were $807 million, or $1.12 per share.
Chrysler incurred $279 million in special charges during the fourth quarter.
Excluding special charges, Chrysler's operating earnings were $1.09 billion.
In the same quarter the previous year, Chrysler posted net income of $1.04 billion, or $1.33 a share.
Chrysler's stock increased by $1.625 to $36.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Chrysler reported full-year 1996 net income of $3.53 billion, or $4.74 per share.
Chrysler's 1996 profit was lower than its 1994 record of $3.71 billion due to $347 million in special charges.
Chrysler earned $6.09 billion on a pretax basis for all of 1996, a new calendar-year record.
Chrysler's U.S. employees received average profit-sharing checks of $7,900 in 1996.

General Motors Corp.'s board of directors approved a $2.5 billion stock buyback programme.
General Motors Corp. raised its dividend by 25 percent.
GM shares decreased by $1.875 to $60.625 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analyst David Healy from Burnham Securities stated that the stock market punishes failure to generate positive surprises.
Some analysts had predicted a dividend increase of up to 50 percent and a stock buyback of up to $5 billion.
GM announced that stock repurchases would occur over the next 12 months.
The stock repurchases would reduce the number of GM's automotive shares by slightly more than 5 percent.
GM raised its quarterly dividend on automotive shares to 50 cents from 40 cents.
GM ended 1996 with a cash balance of $17 billion, up from $10.2 billion at the end of 1995.
GM Chairman Jack Smith stated that the automaker will consider additional stock buybacks in the future.

Comerica Inc. announced it will cut 1,890 jobs, or about 16 percent of its workforce.
The job cuts are part of an effort to reduce costs and increase revenues by $110 million annually by the first half of 1998.
Comerica incurred a $90 million pretax charge against its fourth-quarter earnings due to restructuring actions.
Comerica's fourth-quarter earnings fell to $60.8 million, or 52 cents a share, from $106.5 million, or 92 cents a share, in the previous year.
Comerica had $34 billion in assets at the end of 1996.
The actual number of employees laid off may be less than 1,890 due to attrition, a hiring freeze, and reinvestment actions.
Comerica has about 12,000 employees in Michigan, Texas, California, and Florida.
The job cuts will occur in all four states and will take place between now and mid-1998.
Comerica plans to close about a dozen branch offices.
Comerica earned $417.2 million, or $3.55 a share, for the full year, an increase from $413.4 million, or $3.54 a share, in 1995.

Tomkins Plc reported a 34 percent increase in pretax profits for the six months to November 2, totaling 168.8 million pounds.
The dividend increased from 2.7 pence to 3.06 pence compared to the previous year.
Executive chairman Gregory Hutchings stated that the results indicated another period of outperformance for Tomkins.
Hutchings forecasted that Tomkins shares should continue to outperform the sector.
Hutchings ruled out the possibility of a share buyback this year, citing sufficient acquisition opportunities.
Hutchings indicated that the group was likely to pursue a number of smaller acquisitions, potentially worth up to 200 million pounds.
Tomkins shares were down four at 273-1/2p by 1115 GMT on the day of the report.
Analysts had expected profits of around 160 million pounds.
Hutchings expressed optimism about the second half, noting healthy order books and satisfactory market conditions.
Tomkins' acquisition of Gates Corp for $1.1 billion contributed 259.5 million in sales and 20 million in profit in its first 14 weeks.

Talks between the British and U.S. governments on an open skies pact were postponed for two weeks due to the illness of a senior British negotiator.
The talks were scheduled to begin in Washington on Tuesday with representatives from both governments and major transatlantic carriers.
A spokesman for the British government confirmed that the lead official is in hospital and the meeting has been cancelled.
The European Commission began a series of private hearings in Brussels regarding the proposed British Airways and American Airlines alliance.
The British Airways and American Airlines alliance is conditional on the open skies pact being finalized.
British and U.S. carriers expressed regret over the delay of the Anglo-U.S. talks.
Sources indicated that the current round of talks was not expected to result in a final deal.
Scott Yohe, senior vice-president of government affairs at Delta Air Lines Inc, stated that full agreement was not possible in the current round of talks.
The British government aims to link the open skies talks with the BA/AA alliance, while the U.S. wants to keep them as separate issues.
Britain is awaiting a final verdict from the Office of Fair Trading regarding the BA/AA alliance, particularly concerning the divestment of 168 landing slots at Heathrow airport.

Hanson Plc announced the final stage of its four-way demerger will occur on February 24.
The Energy Group division of Hanson Plc will be spun off as a separate company.
Energy Group is considering acquisitions in Britain and America.
Energy Group has started talks with a U.S. power marketing company.
The demerger is subject to shareholder approval.
Shareholders will receive one Energy share for every 10 existing Hanson shares held.
Hanson shareholders will vote on the proposal at an extraordinary general meeting on February 21.
After the demerger, the remaining Hanson group will consist of building firms.
Energy is expected to rank inside Britain's top 100 blue chips and the Fortune 500 in the U.S.
Derek Bonham is the executive chairman of Energy's new management team.

Sony Corp. will unveil an Internet-based staging area called 'The Station at Sony.com' on Monday.
The Station allows consumers to sample, play, and purchase Sony's television, film, music, and video games.
The Station represents a major push by Sony to enhance its presence on the Web.
The Station offers features comparable to a full-scale online network like America Online Inc.
Sony officials believe The Station could make Sony the top entertainment brand on the Web.
Mitchell Cannold, president of Sony Online, stated that The Station brings together the best of Sony's offerings.
The goal of The Station is to be the primary online entertainment destination for users of all ages.
The Station allows users to sample and buy music and film clips and communicate in chat rooms.
The Station features a 'StationPass' that connects users with other StationPass holders.
The Station offers various games and contests, including interactive entertainment for children and online versions of TV game shows.

Nynex Corp. has until Monday to respond to charges of bad faith regarding an agreement with MCI Communications Corp.
The agreement would have allowed MCI to enter Nynex's local market in New York state.
MCI filed a motion against Nynex asking the state Public Service Commission (PSC) to impose sanctions for not signing the interconnection agreement.
The interconnection agreement would enable MCI to provide local phone access in New York state.
State Attorney General Dennis Vacco filed papers seeking to bar Nynex from offering long-distance service due to discrimination against local-service rivals.
Vacco has criticized the proposed Bell Atlantic Corp. takeover of Nynex on anticompetitive grounds.
Nynex operates 11.1 million local service lines, while competitors have less than 100,000 local service lines according to state regulators.
Nynex spokesman Mark Marchand disagreed with Vacco's assessment of their draft application for long-distance service.
Nynex has signed full interconnection deals with competitive access providers, including MFS Communications, Teleport Communications Group, and WinStar Communications.
Most new entrants into the New York local service market focus on profitable niches in the business services market.

Bay Networks Inc unveiled a set of products and strategies to compete in high-speed networking.
David House is the chairman and chief executive of Bay Networks.
House outlined the company's new 'Adaptive Networking' strategy.
The 'Adaptive Networking' strategy aims to make Internet-based networks easier to upgrade.
House stated that the goal is to create networks that are invisible to the user.
House compared computer networks to electricity and water infrastructures.
Bay Networks announced a new application-specific networking chip capable of carrying up to 1.5 million packets of Internet data per second.
The new Route Switch Processor (RSP) integrates the manageability of routers with the speed of switches.
The RSP chip is designed to address the demand for high-speed Internet transmission and reduce congestion on data networks.
House stated that the RSP chip would allow Bay to reduce switch product prices from $5,000 to $500 per connection over time.

The U.S. government is updating thousands of computer systems and software programs to address the year 2000 problem.
Sally Katzen is coordinating the repair effort as the administrator of the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs in the Office of Management and Budget.
Sally Katzen expressed confidence that all major systems will be fixed.
Legislators in Congress are interested in the year 2000 problem and have urged agencies to take action.
Most congressional staff are aware of the year 2000 problem, although some agencies, like the air traffic control system, are lagging.
Representative Steve Horn stated that Congress will continue to address the year 2000 problem until it is resolved.
Steve Horn is the chairman of the Government Reform Committee's Management, Information and Technology subcommittee.
The subcommittee has received testimony from government and private-sector experts regarding the year 2000 problem.
The latest survey indicated that all government agencies are aware of the year 2000 problem and most are prepared to implement fixes.
The Defence Department and the Social Security Administration have extensive plans to address the year 2000 problem before December 31, 1999.

The number of consumers and businesses filing for U.S. bankruptcy protection reached 335,073 in the first quarter of 1997.
This figure represents a 26 percent increase from 266,149 in the first quarter of the previous year.
Consumers accounted for more than 321,000 of the bankruptcy petitions, approximately 96 percent of the total.
This consumer filing figure reflects a 27 percent increase from the previous year.
Samuel Gerdano, the executive director of the American Bankruptcy Institute, stated that the record pace of bankruptcies correlates with growth in consumer spending and debt.
Gerdano indicated that the pace of bankruptcies in the first quarter of 1997 suggests that the total for the year will exceed the 1996 record.
Advanta Corp. reported a loss of 43 cents per share for the first quarter, surprising Wall Street.
George Salem, a banking industry analyst, noted that credit card debt is significantly influencing bankruptcy trends.
Salem mentioned that bankruptcies are negatively impacting credit card company profits.
Hawaii experienced the largest increase in bankruptcies with a 61 percent rise over the 12 months ending March 31, 1997.

The Internet Society announced a plan to provide seven new top-level domains.
The plan was endorsed by Digital Equipment Corp., MCI Communications Corp., and UUNET Technologies Inc.
The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority endorsed the plan.
The International Telecommunications Union, World Intellectual Property Organization, and International Trademark Association also backed the plan.
New domain names such as 'firm,' 'arts,' and 'web' will be added starting in the third quarter of 1997.
The plan establishes an arbitration and mediation procedure for resolving disputes over names.
Hasbro Inc. won a lawsuit to regain control of the address 'candyland.com.'
Internet Society President Donald Heath stated that responsible self-governance is key for the Internet's potential.
MCI Senior Vice President Vincent Cerf emphasized the importance of sound processes for Internet administration.
Network Solutions Inc. currently registers addresses under most existing top-level domains.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) issued forecasts for 1997 predicting a slight economic upturn.
The CSU expects real GDP growth for 1997 of 4.0-5.0 percent following an estimated 4.1 percent growth rate for 1996.
The CSU forecasts average annual inflation to ease to 7.5-8.0 percent from 8.8 percent.
The CSU predicts the current account deficit will grow to 137-145 billion crowns from an estimated 110.6 billion crown shortfall in 1996.
Analysts warned that widening current account and trade deficits could undermine the economy.
David Lubin, an economist at HSBC Midland, stated that the forecasts are credible but not very encouraging.
The CSU estimates the current account shortfall will be between 8.6-9.1 percent of GDP in 1997.
The CSU forecasts the trade deficit to widen to 202-212 billion crowns from a deficit of 160.3 billion crowns in 1996.
The trade gap was attributed to a 12.7 percent rise in imports in 1996, while exports rose only 3.5 percent.
The CSU expects exports to grow 4.5-6.5 percent in 1997, while import growth should ease to 9-12 percent.

The Prague Stock Exchange gained ground on Thursday.
Analysts are not convinced that the fortunes of the Prague Stock Exchange have turned around.
The rise in the Prague Stock Exchange is attributed to thin domestic buying.
The Prague Stock Exchange lost close to 20 percent during most of autumn.
Key investors sold off positions in the Prague Stock Exchange.
The Prague Stock Exchange has gained in 15 of the past 16 sessions.
The PX50 index was up 0.25 percent at 519.5 at its daily price fixing on Thursday.
The Prague Stock Exchange is 8.3 percent higher than its low in mid-November.
The Czech market has inadequate legislation that fails to protect minority shareholders.
The Securities Registry is bound by law to provide services related to securities transactions.

The United States offered the Czech Republic free use of seven Navy Hornet aircraft for five years.
The U.S. Navy representatives offered to lease seven McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet fighter planes to the Czech Republic under a no-cost, five-year agreement.
The offer includes six single-seat F/A-18A and one two-seat F/A-18B aircraft.
The offer also includes the supply of replacement parts, pilot and ground personnel training programs, and support equipment at cost.
Lockheed Martin, SAAB and British Aerospace, and Dassault Aviation are also competing for business in central Europe.
The Czech government is debating decisions on buying aircraft due to proposed cuts in defense spending.
The Czech Republic, Poland, and Hungary are seen as leading candidates for early NATO membership.
Czech defense officials stated they need about 24 fighters to replace their aging Soviet-made MiG-21s.
New western-made advanced fighters are considered too expensive at over $20 million per fighter.
Czech pilots could begin training in the planes in six months, with delivery of the aircraft 18 months after the contract is signed.

Lawyers for Peter Young stated there are no grounds for allegations of criminality against him.
No allegations of criminality have been made in the proceedings served on Peter Young.
Peter Young was suspended by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) due to suspected irregularities in three funds.
Two of the funds with suspected irregularities were managed by Peter Young.
Peter Young's personal assets were frozen after an injunction obtained by MGAM and Royal Bank of Scotland.
Trading in the affected funds was halted last Monday but resumed on Thursday after a cash injection by Deutsche Bank.
The cash injection amounted to 180 million pounds ($280.7 million).
The investigation focuses on the valuation of unlisted high-technology stocks in the funds.
The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) is investigating the situation.
The Serious Fraud Office (SFO) has not taken official action but is in contact with IMRO regarding the developments.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is unlikely to offer Nicola Horlick her job back.
Banking sources stated that the decision regarding Horlick's reinstatement is now in her hands.
Horlick's resignation last week means that DMG's Morgan Grenfell Asset Management is no longer obliged to discuss her reinstatement.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is preparing to launch a campaign to strengthen its pension fund business following Horlick's resignation.
Horlick was suspended for allegedly attempting to lure staff to another firm.
DMG spokesman James Murray denied that pension firms were considering moving their business from DMG's funds.
Morgan Grenfell Asset Management has written to all its pension fund clients to address concerns following Horlick's suspension and resignation.
Some clients, including Westminster City Council, Dumfries and Galloway County Council, and the Merchant Navy Officers' Pension Fund, have expressed concern about events at MGAM.
The Railway Pension Trustee Company, which has 1.25 billion pounds with MGAM, stated it would maintain close contact with MGAM officials.
Horlick denied the allegations of trying to lure staff away from MGAM during an interview with BBC television.

The head of Britain's financial markets watchdog, the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), stated that former Barings treasury chief Ian Hopkins broke precedent by refusing to be bound by SFA rules.
The SFA banned Ian Hopkins from being a director in the City for at least three years due to his involvement in the 1995 collapse of Barings bank.
Nick Leeson, a trader based in Singapore, is serving a jail sentence for his role in the collapse of Barings bank, which resulted in losses of nearly $1.4 billion.
Ian Hopkins was ordered to pay 10,000 pounds ($15,800) towards the SFA's costs after an independent tribunal found him to be no longer a 'fit and proper person' to be a director of an SFA regulated firm.
Nick Durlacher, the SFA's chairman, stated that the situation with Hopkins was difficult because it was without precedent.
Durlacher mentioned that the SFA had never confronted a situation where someone signed a contract to be bound by their rules and then ignored them.
Ian Hopkins is one of nine Barings executives who have been disciplined by the SFA.
Hopkins claimed he attempted to 'blow the whistle' on irregularities in the Singapore operation but that his warnings were ignored by other managers.
Durlacher commented that the tribunal judged Hopkins' whistleblower claims to be weak, noting he had an unreconciled balance of 100 million pounds for three months.
Durlacher denied that Hopkins was treated more harshly than others due to his refusal to recognize the SFA's authority and stated he had only one telephone conversation with him.

Deng Xiaoping is in good health according to Beijing Vice-Mayor Zhang Baifa.
Zhang Baifa stated that Deng may not be able to visit Hong Kong when it reverts to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
Zhang reported that Deng is currently in Beijing.
Deng Xiaoping is 92 years old.
Zhang mentioned that Deng expressed a desire to go to Hong Kong, even if it meant using a wheelchair.
Zhang cautioned that it would be difficult for Deng to travel due to his age and health risks.
Deng oversaw the negotiations for the return of Hong Kong from Britain to China.
Deng has expressed a hope to witness the transfer of power in Hong Kong.
Chinese officials privately indicated that Deng would not attend the handover ceremony.
Deng has not been seen in public since early 1994.

Jiang Zemin is the boss of China's Communist Party.
Jiang Zemin urged Taiwan not to create new obstacles to ties.
Jiang's comments were reported by major Chinese newspapers.
Jiang made his remarks one day after the election of Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive.
Hong Kong is set to revert to China on June 30, 1997, after 150 years of British rule.
Jiang called for Taiwan to return to China, stating that reunification is the will of the people.
Beijing and Taipei have been rivals since 1949, following the Chinese civil war.
Lee Teng-hui is Taiwan's first native-born president.
Taiwan denies ambitions for independence and claims commitment to reunification under democracy.
Jiang warned that forces seeking Taiwan's independence threaten peaceful reunification.

China has pledged to open its insurance, stock, retail, wholesale, and banking sectors to foreign investment.
This pledge is part of China's effort to gain entry to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
From 1997 to 2000, China is expected to widen access to its insurance and stock markets for foreign investment.
The China Daily reported this information, quoting Ma Jixian from the State Economic and Trade Commission.
The pledge was included in a unilateral action plan submitted by China to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Foreign insurers will gain access to markets outside Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou before the end of the decade.
China's insurance market was previously dominated by the state-owned People's Insurance Group.
Currently, only three foreign insurers can write policies in China: American International Assurance Co Ltd, Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd, and a joint venture with a domestic insurer.
Foreign stock companies will be allowed to handle A shares, which are currently restricted to Chinese nationals.
China plans to reduce its average import tariffs from 23 percent to about 15 percent.

Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) Ltd is an Australian-based soft drink bottler.
CCA announced the final details of its share swap deal with San Miguel Corp on Wednesday.
The deal aims to create the world's second largest Coca-Cola bottler.
CCA initially announced the deal in April.
Some San Miguel shareholders protested the deal's terms regarding board influence and cashflows.
CCA confirmed the initial terms of the deal, which involves CCA buying San Miguel's stake in a soft drink bottling joint venture in the Philippines.
In exchange, San Miguel will receive a 25 percent stake in CCA.
The Coca-Cola Co, CCA's parent group, will see its shareholding in CCA diluted from 36 percent to 33 percent.
The deal is valued at A$3.7 billion and will result in annual sales of almost A$4 billion.
The number of San Miguel representatives on the CCA board will increase from three to four.

Brambles Industries Ltd is a transport equipment hire and logistics firm.
Brambles Industries Ltd announced it is on track to achieve a full year net profit of about A$240 million.
John Fletcher is the chief executive of Brambles.
John Fletcher stated that analysts should not assume first half profit growth will continue into the full year.
The existing market expectations for the full year remain stable according to Fletcher.
The average forecast from the Barceps survey for the 1996/97 year is A$240.3 million.
This forecast represents a nearly 12 percent increase from the A$214.8 million pre-abnormal net profit of 1995/96.
Brambles reported a first half net profit increase of 14.3 percent to A$117.2 million.
Brambles expects the rate of profit improvement to slow in the second half due to difficult trading conditions.
Fletcher indicated that economic conditions in Australia are subdued in the transport and logistics sectors.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) announced an 11 percent rise in first half profits.
CBA reported a 33 percent increase in business lending.
CBA's net profit for the six months to December 31 rose to A$602 million from A$542 million a year earlier.
CBA managing director David Murray stated that business volumes were pleasing.
Murray indicated that the results could lead to a better than expected full year result.
CBA had previously expected competition in the home loan market to squeeze margins and keep profits flat.
Analysts had forecasted a profit of between A$535 million and A$560 million for CBA.
CBA's shares increased by 47 cents to A$13.88 following the profit announcement.
CBA announced an interim dividend of 45 cents per share, an increase of seven cents from the previous interim dividend.
CBA cut its variable home mortgage rates by up to 0.7 percentage points.

TCF Financial Corp. and Standard Financial Inc. signed a definitive agreement for TCF to acquire Standard Financial for $424 million in stock and cash.
The acquisition deal was announced two days after Marshall & Ilsley Corp. announced its acquisition of Security Capital Corp. for about $945 million in cash and stock.
Both acquisitions aim to increase market share in the Midwest banking sector.
Marshall & Ilsley expects to increase its market share to 19.2 percent in Wisconsin.
Firstar Corp. is the second largest bank in Wisconsin with 12.1 percent of deposits.
The acquisition of Standard Financial will strengthen TCF's franchise in Chicago.
William Cooper, chairman of TCF, stated that the merger will produce long-term revenue enhancements and meaningful cost savings.
TCF expects to save about $4 million annually after combining operations with Standard Financial.
The combined company will have $10 billion in assets and 276 financial services offices.
Standard stockholders may choose to receive cash, TCF shares, or a combination of both in the acquisition.

Sears, Roebuck and Co will spend more than $500 million to revamp and expand its off-the-mall tire and battery stores under the new National Tire and Battery name.
Sears plans to spend more than $1 billion through the year 2002 on its entire auto group to add stores and convert some existing stores.
Sears sold 25 million tires and 8.5 million batteries through its Sears Tire Group in 1996.
Sears will combine most of its 275 Tire America and National Tire Warehouse Stores under the National Tire and Battery name.
Sears plans to add about 100 National Tire stores over the next five years.
Sears hopes to add about $120 million in annual revenue for the tire group when the expansion is completed.
Sears' tire group had $2.3 billion in revenues in 1996.
The new stores will have a high-tech, open feel, allowing customers to watch the work being done on their cars.
Sears will price competitively in individual markets.
Sears is targeting younger, higher income customers with higher performance car needs for the off-the-mall stores.

First Bank System Inc. will acquire U.S. Bancorp in an $8.5 billion stock deal.
The acquisition will make First Bank the 14th-largest bank in the United States.
The deal will provide First Bank with a presence in the Pacific Northwest.
The acquisition is expected to result in the loss of about 4,000 jobs.
U.S. Bancorp shareholders will receive 0.755 share of First Bank common stock for each share of U.S. Bancorp they own.
The purchase price for U.S. Bancorp shares is $56.53 based on First Bank's trading price of $74.875.
Analyst James Schutz stated that the deal values U.S. Bancorp at about 19.2 times its 1996 earnings.
First Bank expects pretax cost savings of about $340 million from the merger.
First Bank plans to take pretax charges of $625 million for costs related to the merger.
First Bank anticipates an 8 percent addition to earnings per share by 1999.

Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. were active on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday.
Exchange officials stated that problems affecting recent trading in Bre-X stock were resolved.
Bre-X closed down C25 cents at C$3.18 with a turnover of eight million shares.
On Nasdaq, Bre-X fell 25 cents to $2.375.
Bre-X reached a session high of C$3.78 amid market rumors about positive test results from the Busang gold site.
An analyst mentioned that rumors from Strathcona contributed to the stock's rise before it fell.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. has not commented since being hired by Bre-X to audit the Busang gold site.
The final results of Strathcona's review are expected in early May.
Bre-X faced issues after Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. reported low gold amounts in drilling samples from the Busang property.
The TSE halted trading in Bre-X shares three times that week due to heavy order volumes and a computer system issue.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd.'s Busang gold discovery may not be as rich as projected.
The news about Bre-X's gold discovery affected the mining world and Canadian markets.
Securities regulators are investigating the situation.
Gold shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange fell more than 300 points or almost 3.0 percent.
The decline in gold shares impacted the entire market.
Canadian regulators are collaborating with Toronto exchange officials on the investigation.
A spokesman for the Ontario Securities Commission stated that they are working with the TSE.
Bre-X's stock was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange and Nasdaq due to questions about its gold discovery.
Bre-X's stock price fell from C$250 to C$15.50 before the halt.
Bre-X admitted that test samples from the Busang gold property may have been overstated.

Barrick Gold Corp. is the world's second largest gold producer.
Barrick Gold Corp. reported a net income of $55 million or $0.15 a share in the first quarter of 1997.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s net income fell from $72 million or $0.20 a share in the previous year.
Gold production from Barrick's 10 producing mines fell by 88,147 ounces to 712,368 ounces in the first quarter of 1997.
Barrick Gold Corp. expects production to be substantially higher in the second half of 1997.
Barrick Gold Corp. aims to achieve a production target of over 3 million ounces for the year.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s gold production was 3,148,801 ounces in the previous year.
Barrick Gold Corp.'s earnings in 1996 were $218 million or $0.60 a share, including writedowns.
Analyst Michael Jalonen expects Barrick to earn about $0.70 a share in 1997, excluding writedowns.
Barrick's stock rose C25 cents to C$32.85 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday.

Dow Corning Corp. announced it would set aside up to $2 billion for silicone breast implant claims under a $3 billion bankruptcy reorganization plan.
Dow Corning is seeking a trial to determine whether silicone breast implants cause diseases.
The bankruptcy plan was filed with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Bay City, Mich.
Dow Corning plans to allocate an additional $1 billion to pay commercial creditors.
Dow Corning, based in Midland, Mich., is a joint venture between Dow Chemical Co. and Corning Inc.
The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in May 1995 due to lawsuits from women alleging medical problems from implants.
Dow Corning introduced silicone gel breast implants in 1964 and was the largest manufacturer until a FDA moratorium in 1992.
The reorganization plan includes a $600 million fund for out-of-court settlements.
An additional $1.4 billion would be available for implant claims if a trial proves that implants caused disease.
Dow Corning asserts that scientific studies have not shown a link between implants and disease.

General Motors Corp. will consolidate all of its commercial truck production in Flint, Mich.
GM will discontinue some engineering work in Flint and Lansing, Mich.
The consolidation will expand the workforce at the Flint truck plant by up to 3,000 jobs by the year 2001.
The Flint truck plant currently employs about 2,000 workers.
The closure of the truck and bus chassis plant in Detroit will affect 494 employees.
Production will be moved from Detroit to Flint in the year 2000.
About 90 engineers from the Detroit plant will be transferred to GM facilities in Pontiac, Mich.
GM will shift production of medium-duty commercial trucks from Janesville, Wis., to Flint in 2001.
The Janesville truck line employs about 1,000 people.
GM will invest about $500 million in the Flint truck plant to prepare it for medium-duty truck production.

Chrysler Corp. will report record earnings for 1996.
Chrysler's record worldwide sales for 1996 are 2.97 million vehicles.
Robert Eaton is the chairman of Chrysler Corp.
Chrysler's previous annual profit record was $3.713 billion in 1994.
Chrysler earned $2.025 billion in 1995.
Chrysler expects to exceed its 1996 sales results in 1997.
Chrysler plans to produce about 190,000 more trucks in 1997 than in 1996.
Chrysler will unveil the Dodge Durango at the Detroit auto show.
Robert Lutz is the Vice Chairman of Chrysler.
Lutz recently gave up his president and chief operating officer titles.

Ford Motor Co announced it would cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant near Liverpool, England.
The job cuts represent almost one third of the Halewood workforce.
The Halewood plant will not build the planned new model of the Escort car, due in 1999.
Production of the new Escort model is likely to transfer to factories in Spain and Germany.
Ford stated that Halewood could become the European source for a planned new vehicle, which is still a concept.
Halewood will continue to produce the current Escort model through 2000.
David Gorman, European vehicle operations manager for Ford, commented on the future of the Halewood plant.
Local MP David Alton reported that Ford indicated the job losses would occur through voluntary redundancy.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000 from a peak of 14,000 in the 1960s.
Workers expressed anger over the job cuts, citing British labour laws and the absence of the European Union's Social Chapter.

Hanson Plc reported a record 1.8 billion British pounds ($2.9 billion) in pretax profits for the last fiscal year.
Hanson Plc began a four-way split of its operations on October 1.
Hanson Plc spun off Imperial Tobacco and Millennium Chemicals in the fall.
Hanson Plc's energy group is due to be spun off by February.
Hanson Plc's final results showed profits topping forecasts and increasing from 1.22 billion ($1.98 billion) last year.
The profits were inflated by a one-time gain of 609 million pounds ($989 million).
Earnings per share were 25.6 pence (14.6 cents) compared to 18.2 pence (29.5 cents) last year.
A dividend of 1 pence (1.6 cents) will be paid.
The building materials and equipment divisions saw profits slip to 231 million pounds ($375 million) from 237 million ($385 million).
The combined value of Hanson and the demerged companies was 195 pence ($3.17) on December 1, 1995, and now stands at 150 pence ($2.43).

Ford Motor Co announced 1,300 job cuts at its Halewood plant in northwest England.
Ford is switching production of a new model to plants in Spain and Germany.
The new version of the mid-range Escort model will not be built at Halewood.
The proposed job cuts will reduce Halewood's workforce to just over 3,000.
Halewood's workforce peaked at 14,000 in the 1960s.
Workers believe the new model will be built at Ford's plants in Valencia, Spain, and Saarlouis, Germany.
Ford has not confirmed where the new model will be built.
Trade unions blamed the decision on a lack of legal protection for British workers.
Britain has opted out of the European Union's Social Chapter, affecting working conditions.
Ford stated that Halewood would continue to make the current Escort model through the year 2000.

3Com Corp. will acquire U.S. Robotics in a deal valued at $6.6 billion.
The merger will create a counterweight to Cisco Systems Inc.
This merger is the largest ever in the computer network industry.
The combined company will have more than $5 billion in annual revenues.
The combined company will employ more than 12,000 employees in 130 countries.
Each share of U.S. Robotics will be swapped for 1.75 shares of 3Com.
The deal is valued at $6.6 billion based on the $39.125 closing price of 3Com stock.
3Com closed at $39 and U.S. Robotics closed at $61 on Nasdaq.
U.S. Robotics is the world's largest maker of consumer modems.
3Com is based in Santa Clara, California.

Xerox Corp. reported higher fourth-quarter profits from continuing operations.
Sales of digital products rose by 26 percent, offsetting flat sales of black and white copiers.
Xerox agreed to sell part of its Talegen insurance holdings for $450 million, including assumption of debt.
Xerox's board voted to raise the dividend by 10 percent.
Xerox reported earnings of $426 million for the latest quarter, up 12 percent from $379 million in the 1995 quarter.
The 1995 earnings figure excludes a $1.6 billion charge related to the planned sale of Talegen.
Sales increased to $5.08 billion from $4.76 billion.
Earnings exceeded forecasts by a few cents per share, according to First Call.
Xerox stock closed up $1.375 at $59.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Xerox announced the sale of Talegen's Coregis unit for $375 million in cash and the assumption of $75 million in debt to General Electric Co.'s GE Capital unit.

A device that turns a personal computer into an automated-teller machine was introduced by Fischer International Systems Corp.
The device costs $60 and can be inserted into the floppy disk drive of any PC.
The device enables PCs to read 'smart cards,' which can perform electronic cash transactions and store bank account balances.
Smart cards are gaining popularity in Europe for store purchases and telephone calls.
Smart cards are beginning to be used in the United States as a replacement for cash in ordinary purchases.
The device may stimulate home banking by allowing consumers to perform financial transactions without visiting a bank branch or ATM.
Smarty is the name of the product that allows PCs to link to banks or retail outlets via the Internet.
Fischer holds key patents for smart card readers that can be inserted into 3.5 inch floppy drives.
The device can be used in home or office PCs and laptops, enabling wider use of banking cards for purchases.
Fischer is working with major U.S. and European financial services firms and home banking software providers to promote the device.

U.S. Senators criticized a new Securities and Exchange Commission rule requiring companies to disclose their use of derivatives.
The SEC and the Financial Accounting Standards Board proposed increased disclosure about derivatives following significant losses in 1994.
Derivatives are financial instruments like options and futures that derive value from underlying stock or commodity prices.
Derivatives were linked to the bankruptcy of Orange County, California, and over $100 million in losses at Procter & Gamble Co.
The SEC adopted its rules last month, while the FASB is still developing its proposal.
Senators expressed concerns that the new rules would increase costs and complications for companies using derivatives to manage risk.
Senator Lauch Faircloth voiced concerns about unnecessary regulations in the SEC's new rule.
Senator Christopher Dodd stated that the issues in 1994 were due to human error, not the derivatives themselves.
The new rules do not apply to Orange County, which is not subject to most FASB or SEC regulations.
Senator Phil Gramm expressed doubts about the effectiveness of the new rules after hearing from industry representatives.

Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato warned that the Federal Reserve may not be taking adequate precautions for the year 2000.
D'Amato expressed concern after questioning U.S. bank regulators about the year 2000 computer issue in February.
D'Amato was troubled by the responses he received from the Federal Reserve and the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA).
