Problems are expected in computers and software that only record the last two digits of the year.
Such a program might interpret the year 2000 as the year 1900, leading to miscalculations or system crashes.
D'Amato also questioned the Office of the Comptroller and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. in February.
The Office of the Comptroller and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. stated they had detailed plans to address the millennium bug.
D'Amato's office indicated that he was concerned about the responses from the Fed and the NCUA regarding their attention to the year 2000 crisis.
D'Amato sent letters to the Fed and the NCUA asking for additional information.
Estimates for fixing year 2000 problems worldwide have ranged from $300 billion to $600 billion.

The Internet Society announced a plan to provide seven new top-level domains.
The new top-level domains will be added to existing ones such as 'com,' 'net,' and 'org.'
The plan is supported by Digital Equipment Corp., MCI Communications Corp., and UUNET Technologies Inc.
The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority endorsed the plan.
The International Telecommunications Union, World Intellectual Property Organisation, and International Trademark Association also backed the plan.
New domain names such as 'firm,' 'arts,' and 'web' will be introduced starting in the third quarter of 1997.
The plan includes an arbitration and mediation procedure for resolving disputes over domain names.
Hasbro Inc. won a lawsuit last year to regain control of the address 'candyland.com.'
MCI Senior Vice President Vincent Cerf stated that sound processes are vital for the Internet's administration.
Network Solutions Inc. currently registers addresses under most existing top-level domains.

The Czech Republic won both reverse singles matches against India in the Davis Cup.
The victory secured a place for the Czech Republic in the second round of the Davis Cup.
Petr Korda announced his retirement from Davis Cup play after the matches.
Jiri Novak won his match against Mahesh Bhupathi with a score of 6-1, 6-4, 6-3.
Korda won his match against Leander Paes with a score of 5-7, 6-3, 6-4, 6-1.
Novak's match against Bhupathi lasted 90 minutes.
Novak was ranked 67th in the world at the time of his match.
Korda was ranked 33rd in the world at the time of his match.
Leander Paes was ranked 105th in the world at the time of his match.
Korda stated that he would no longer play for the Czechs in the Davis Cup due to the demands it placed on him.

Markets in Eastern Europe are experiencing an autumn slump.
Analysts see little potential for improvement in the bearish trend.
Stock exchanges in Warsaw, Prague, Bratislava, Bucharest, Zagreb, and Ljubljana all lost ground this week.
The Budapest Stock Exchange rose slightly but lost momentum by the end of the week.
The PX50 index on the Prague Stock Exchange dipped 0.8 points to close at 509.3.
The centre-right governing coalition in Prague had a strong showing in Senate elections.
Investors are concerned about poor market regulation in the Czech Republic.
Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka expressed skepticism about the Senate's ability to effect market changes.
The Warsaw Stock Exchange remained virtually flat this week.
Analysts are divided on the future direction of the Warsaw Stock Exchange.

The Czech December trade deficit is expected to rise to 16 billion crowns from 14.3 billion in December 1995.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) will release the 1996 trade figures at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Monday.
Most economists surveyed expect steady growth in the trade deficit with few surprises.
Martin Kupka, an economist at Patria Finance, stated that he expects the figures to align with the development throughout 1996.
The full-year trade gap for 1996 is guaranteed to be a record, as the January-November figure reached 140.1 billion crowns.
The 140.1 billion crowns figure is already beyond the 1995 record total shortfall of 95.7 billion crowns.
Most analysts predict a December trade gap of 15-17 billion crowns, following a 16.6 billion crown shortfall in November.
The consensus forecast for the 1996 trade deficit is between 155-165 billion crowns.
The foreign exchange and money markets are expected to show little reaction to the figures unless they vary greatly from estimates.
Czech exporters indicated a desire for a 20 to 25 percent devaluation of the crown against a mark/dollar basket to boost exports in 1997.

NatWest Bank admitted on Thursday that its derivatives losses totalled nearly twice the amount initially thought.
The problem began in December 1994.
NatWest Bank suspended four senior members of staff as a result of initial findings from an internal probe.
NatWest Bank cut millions of pounds from bonuses to restore confidence.
The total loss reported by NatWest Bank was 90 million pounds ($144 million).
Five million pounds had already been provisioned and eight million pounds had been clawed back by not paying bonuses.
This resulted in a loss of 77 million pounds in the accounts.
Martin Owen, chief executive of NatWest Markets, will forego 200,000 pounds of his 500,000 pounds 1996 bonus.
Derek Wanless, NatWest's chief executive, stated that the losses and mis-pricing had gone undetected for a long time.
The losses were confined to the interest rate options area.

Elizabeth Forsyth is a former aide to Asil Nadir, head of Polly Peck Plc.
Forsyth left court on Friday awaiting the outcome of her appeal against a money-laundering conviction.
Forsyth has been in jail for 10 months.
The London Court of Appeal reserved judgment on Forsyth's appeal after a two-day hearing.
Forsyth, 60, was found guilty last year of dishonestly handling 400,000 pounds ($640,000).
Forsyth was freed on bail on Thursday when the court quashed her original five-year sentence.
The court concluded that Forsyth had already served long enough in prison.
The prosecution argued that the money Forsyth was convicted of handling was stolen by Nadir from Polly Peck.
Nadir fled to northern Cyprus in 1993 after jumping bail of 3.5 million pounds.
Forsyth's barrister argued that her conviction was unsafe for several reasons, including the lack of questioning of Nadir.

Britain's commercial property market is improving but is not yet fully healthy.
Pen Kent is an executive director at the Bank of England.
Kent stated that it would be rash to conclude the market is healthy in all respects.
Lease lengths have temporarily stabilized in the commercial property market.
Clauses allowing tenants to break leases are becoming more common.
Many occupiers are expected to reduce their space needs and demand greater flexibility.
There is a sizeable overhang of unlet secondary property in the market.
The pool of unlet secondary property increases when major users move to new offices.
Kent called for solutions to the issues with secondary stock that is unsuitable for conversion or relet.
Institutional investors may resume their longer-term departure from property if market performance declines.

Beijing has pledged to open its doors to imports of U.S. textiles under a new deal.
Washington does not believe it can close its textile trade gap with China.
Chinese and U.S. negotiators signed a new textile agreement in Beijing.
The new textile agreement ended the threat of a cross-Pacific trade war.
The agreement ensures U.S. access to China's textile markets.
China exported $6.5 billion worth of textiles to the United States in 1995.
The United States imported only $64 million worth of textiles from China in 1995.
U.S. textile exports are sluggish due to China's high tariff rates and non-tariff barriers.
The new agreement gave China a U.S. import quota larger than the previous 1994 textile pact.
China pledged to reduce its tariffs on textile imports.

China warned Britain against challenging it in the World Court over its decision to disband Hong Kong's elected legislature.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that challenging China would damage Sino-British relations.
Shen Guofang said that if Britain acts willfully and creates troubles, Sino-British relations will be damaged.
British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind denounced China's plans to disband the democratically elected legislature.
Rifkind proposed that the International Court of Justice in The Hague rule on the dispute regarding Hong Kong.
Hong Kong, with a population of 6.3 million, will revert to Chinese control at midnight on June 30, 1997.
Beijing's communist leadership promised that almost nothing will change after the handover of Hong Kong.
A Beijing-appointed provisional legislature will take over from the elected Legislative Council after the handover.
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten criticized the creation of the provisional legislature, calling it a 'bizarre farce' and a 'stomach-churning' process.
Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive, defended China's decision and criticized Britain's threat to take Beijing to the World Court.

Chinese authorities sealed off the town of Yining in northwestern Xinjiang.
Paramilitary police patrolled the streets of Yining after a separatist riot.
At least 10 people were killed in the riot, including one policeman.
Approximately 100 people were wounded during the riot.
The riot involved around 1,000 Muslim separatists from the Uighur ethnic minority.
The riot was a protest against Beijing rule.
Yining is located in the Yili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture near the border with Kazakhstan.
Authorities closed the airport and railway station in Yining and imposed a curfew.
Local officials reported a lower number of arrests than claimed by residents.
Yining is 50 km from the border with Kazakhstan, where many exiled Uighur separatists reside.

Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd is expected to report a stagnant net profit for the year to June 30.
The stagnant profit is attributed to soaring newsprint costs and losses from Star TV operations.
The median forecast for News Corp's net profit before abnormals is A$1.343 billion.
The forecasted profit is similar to the A$1.342 billion profit posted in 1994/95.
Analysts believe News Corp may struggle to match last year's profit results.
News Corp posted a A$281 million net profit before abnormals in the third quarter.
The third quarter profit was below expectations of about A$300 million.
Profits for the first nine months of the year totaled A$944 million.
Analysts indicated that higher paper costs and a U.K. cover price war restrained profits.
Star TV is projected to incur losses of US$90 million to US$100 million for the year.

Macquarie Bank Ltd posted a net profit of A$116.94 million for the year to March 31.
Macquarie Bank's net profit rose 25.4 percent compared to the previous year.
The return on average shareholder funds for Macquarie Bank was 25.2 percent.
Macquarie Bank raised its annual dividend to 43 cents from 36 cents the previous year.
Earnings per share for Macquarie Bank increased to 74.9 cents from 61 cents.
Analysts had forecast a net profit of around A$105 million for Macquarie Bank.
Macquarie Bank's Corporate Advisory division had 130 advisory mandates during the year.
Simon Hannes, a senior corporate advisory executive at Macquarie, was charged with insider trading.
Hannes allegedly made a notional profit of A$2 million from buying TNT options before a takeover bid.
Macquarie Bank's Managing Director Allan Moss stated that the Hannes matter did not affect corporate advisory work.

Kerry Packer is a local billionaire.
Packer is interested in acquiring John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
Analysts believe Packer's bid is not guaranteed.
The government must first decide to drop current cross-media rules.
Any legislation must pass through a hostile senate.
Packer would need to offer a takeover premium on top of Fairfax's high share price.
Vince Pepe is a senior media analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Prime Minister John Howard's cabinet is considering changes to cross-media rules.
Howard has stated that the current rules are outdated.
A successful takeover would result in major newspapers being divided between Packer and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd.

Shares of Sears, Roebuck and Co fell about six percent on Thursday.
Sears announced it will voluntarily refund some payments from credit card holders who filed for bankruptcy.
Sears stated that the repayments might have a material effect on 1997 earnings.
Analysts indicated that Sears could not quantify its earnings exposure during a conference call.
Sears stock decreased by 3-1/8 to 47-3/4.
The dispute involves reaffirmations, where Sears seeks payments from credit card holders in bankruptcy.
Reaffirmation agreements must be filed with a bankruptcy court.
Sears reported that some reaffirmation agreements were not filed properly.
Sears had $400 million in reaffirmations from 1992 through February 1997.
Sears plans to offer each affected debtor a $100 gift certificate.

William Brandt Jr. is the new chief executive officer of Mercury Finance Co.
Brandt expressed hope for a short-term credit facility from lenders to stabilize the company.
Mercury Finance Co. defaulted on $17 million of commercial debt.
Analysts reported that Mercury has about $100 million of debt due on Thursday.
Brandt aims to avoid filing for bankruptcy reorganization while stabilizing the company.
Brandt stated he is not prepared to file for imminent bankruptcy.
Brandt has a background as a corporate turnaround and bankruptcy specialist.
Mercury's debt ratings were lowered to default status by major rating services.
The company needed to lower its past four years' net income by about $90 million due to accounting irregularities.
Brandt mentioned that if Mercury cannot re-enter the commercial debt market, it would consider securitizing its consumer loans.

First Bank System Inc plans to acquire U.S. Bancorp for $9 billion.
The acquisition will expand First Bank's geographic footprint to the Pacific Northwest.
Analyst James Schutz at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp described the acquisition price as 'very rich'.
The deal will make First Bank the 14th largest bank in the United States based on assets.
The acquisition values U.S. Bancorp at approximately $59.08 per share, or 19.2 times its 1996 earnings.
U.S. Bancorp shares increased by 6-3/16 to 54-7/16 on Thursday.
First Bank's CEO John Grundhofer is known for aggressive cost cutting.
Analyst Frank Barkocy at Josephthal, Lyon & Ross stated that the acquisition is a 'natural fit' for First Bank.
First Bank plans to grow revenues by offering payment systems services to U.S. Bancorp's corporate base.
First Bank expects to reduce combined operating expenses by about 14 percent, resulting in pre-tax cost savings of approximately $340 million.

David Walsh is the chief executive of Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is a Canadian gold prospector.
Walsh stated that Bre-X has the financial resources to endure challenges related to the Busang gold discovery.
Walsh claimed that an audit will confirm that Bre-X made a significant gold strike.
Bre-X has faced scrutiny following reports that the Busang gold deposit may not contain significant amounts of gold.
Canadian regulators are investigating Bre-X and its officials for potential violations of insider trading and disclosure laws.
There are at least eight class action lawsuits against Bre-X in Canada and the United States.
Bre-X's stock market value decreased by more than 80 percent due to panic selling after the preliminary test results.
Bre-X's stock closed at C$2.67 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
An independent audit of the Busang project will be conducted by Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.

Molson Cos. Ltd. is seeking expansion opportunities in China and Latin America.
Molson has cash from the sale of non-beer assets.
Molson's new President and Chief Executive is Norman Seagram.
Seagram stated that Molson wants to grow its core brewing business.
Molson is not considering a share buyback.
Molson will spend the next three months looking for brewing opportunities.
Analysts and investors are concerned about Molson's track record on acquisitions.
Molson's class A stock closed down C$0.30 at C$20.20 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Molson's stock has remained around C$20 since earlier speculation pushed it to C$25.
Molson's sale of Diversey Corp. added almost C$1 billion to its finances.

Michael de Guzman was the chief geologist of Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
De Guzman co-discovered a significant gold find this century.
De Guzman may have committed suicide after falling from a helicopter.
He fell 800 feet from a helicopter while en route to the Busang site in Indonesia.
Rescue crews were searching for de Guzman's body in the Borneo rain forest.
An apparent suicide note was found by Indonesian police among de Guzman's belongings.
The note indicated that de Guzman had recently learned he had hepatitis B.
The prognosis for de Guzman's recovery was not good due to his history of malaria.
Foul play was not suspected, and Indonesian police were treating his death as a suicide.
Bre-X has agreed to develop the Busang site, valued at $25 billion, with Freeport-McMoRan and Indonesian partners.

Chrysler Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Robert Eaton announced that the automaker will report record earnings for the full 1996 year.
Chrysler's record earnings are based on record worldwide sales of 2.97 million vehicles.
Chrysler's previous annual profit record was $3.713 billion in 1994.
Chrysler earned $2.025 billion in 1995.
Chrysler's sales in 1995 were limited to 2.61 million units due to the launch of its current line of minivans.
Eaton stated that Chrysler should be able to exceed its 1996 sales results in 1997.
Chrysler plans to produce about 190,000 more trucks in 1997 than it built in 1996.
Chrysler plans to unveil the Dodge Durango at the Detroit auto show.
Chrysler has tentatively planned to add a third production shift to its Bramalea, Ontario, car assembly plant.
Eaton expressed that Chrysler can still earn a profit even if U.S. automotive industry sales fall by 20 percent.

General Motors Corp. informed analysts that its fourth-quarter North American incentive and marketing costs were higher than previously estimated.
As a result of the higher costs, analysts reduced their earnings estimates for GM by hundreds of millions of dollars.
GM's product mix in Europe is expected to be weaker than anticipated, with the low-margin Corsa subcompact comprising a larger share of sales.
New product launch costs for GM remain high.
Analysts lowered their estimates for GM's earnings by 45 cents to 50 cents per share.
GM's stock price decreased by $1.375 over two days, closing at $54.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Burnham Securities analyst David Healy estimates GM will earn $435 million, or 52 cents per share, in the fourth quarter, excluding extraordinary items.
GM plans to take a charge of $170 million, or 22 cents per share, for lump-sum payments to United Auto Workers members as part of a new contract.
Strikes in the United States and Canada during the quarter are estimated to have reduced GM's fourth-quarter profit by about $700 million.
In the fourth quarter of 1995, GM earned $1.87 billion, or $1.98 per share.

The Canadian Auto Workers union has chosen Chrysler Corp as its strike target.
This decision creates competition between General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co for bargaining leadership with the United Auto Workers.
Analysts suggest that Ford is gaining an edge in this competition.
Ford has made offers indicating a willingness to collaborate with the UAW on outsourcing issues.
Sean McAlinden, a labor analyst at the University of Michigan, stated that Ford is working to provide the UAW with a framework agreement.
It is unlikely that UAW President Stephen Yokich will select Chrysler as the U.S. target due to the Canadian union's choice.
The Canadian Auto Workers and UAW traditionally select different targets for negotiations.
Contracts for approximately 400,000 Big Three hourly workers in the U.S. and 53,000 in Canada will expire on September 14.
Ford has offered the UAW opportunities to bring some parts manufacturing back into its plants from outside suppliers.
GM is attempting to shift more parts work to outside suppliers to reduce costs.

AMEC Plc is a British building and engineering group.
AMEC Plc's first half pretax profits doubled to 12.1 million pounds for the six months to June 30.
AMEC Plc's sales increased to 1.32 billion pounds compared to 1.13 billion pounds.
AMEC Plc's interim dividend was frozen at 1.5 pence per share.
AMEC chief executive Peter Mason stated that he hopes to improve the dividend at the year end.
Peter Mason indicated that the conservative payout decision was made to ensure the dividend was covered.
Peter Mason expressed confidence that profits would exceed last year's figures.
AMEC's targeted turnover is 2.75 billion pounds.
AMEC's shares increased by 2.5 pence to 98 at 1104 GMT.
Peter Mason aims to increase international sales to 50 percent of total turnover from the current 30 percent.

The United States and Britain ended their latest round of open skies talks on Friday.
The talks resulted in agreement on some technical issues but did not produce a full deal for trans-Atlantic air travel.
No new date was set for future talks.
Industry sources believe the next discussions could occur in weeks rather than months.
Britain's Department of Trade and Industry announced it would block the proposed British Airways alliance with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines unless certain conditions were met.
Airline industry figures stated that the open skies negotiations would remain deadlocked until there was a British verdict on the proposed alliance.
Conditions for allowing the alliance to proceed were outlined by Britain's Office of Fair Trading.
The Department of Trade and Industry indicated that the alliance's approval was dependent on reaching an open skies agreement.
The U.S. Transportation Department expressed disappointment with the lack of progress in the talks.
A British Department of Transport official reported that useful progress was made on several issues, but not all, and no date was set for further talks.

Go-Ahead Group Plc is a UK bus to rail group.
Dale Campbell-Savours is an opposition Labour MP.
Campbell-Savours alleged that Go-Ahead representatives used inside information to secure a rail franchise.
Go-Ahead Group Plc called the allegations 'rubbish.'
Martin Ballinger is the managing director of Go-Ahead.
Ballinger stated that no one made money from share dealings as no shares were sold.
The allegations were made in the House of Commons, where MPs are protected from libel suits.
Ballinger warned Campbell-Savours to be cautious about statements made outside the House of Commons.
Go-Ahead was shortlisted for the Regional Railways North East franchise on November 15.
Ballinger explained that Go-Ahead's bid was adjusted by the franchise regulator Opraf to align with other bidders.

Bell Atlantic Corp. reported a first-quarter net income of $515.6 million.
This represents an increase of 11.0 percent over the $464.7 million earned in the first quarter of 1996.
Earnings per share rose to $1.17 from $1.06.
This earnings per share figure is slightly more than the First Call consensus estimate of $1.16.
Operating revenues grew to $3.4 billion from $3.2 billion.
J.P. Morgan analyst Simon Flannery commented on the strong performance in new growth areas and productivity.
Bell Atlantic Chairman and Chief Executive Raymond Smith stated that demand for services continues to drive performance.
Smith anticipates a landmark year for the company and the closing of its merger with Nynex.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Bell Atlantic and Nynex Corp. are preparing for a legal counter-attack if their merger is blocked.
The latest earnings report includes results from the Mexican Grupo Iusacell SA de CV investment.

Lucent Technologies Inc. earned $66 million in the first three months of 1997.
Lucent Technologies Inc. reversed a loss of $103 million from the 1996 quarter.
Lucent reported net income of 10 cents a share for the three months ended March 31, 1997.
Lucent's revenues for its fiscal second quarter grew by 12.5 percent to $5.15 billion.
Lucent benefited from strengthened relationships with regional Bell companies after its spin-off from AT&T.
Only consumer products suffered a decline in revenues for the quarter among Lucent's four main businesses.
Lucent's gross profit margin for the quarter rose to 42.1 percent of revenues.
Revenues from systems for network operators increased 23.3 percent to $2.93 billion.
Revenues for microelectronic products increased 18.3 percent to $615 million.
Revenues from consumer products decreased 41 percent to $174 million.

Cisco Systems Inc fell more than two points in active trading on Wednesday.
Analysts stated that the decline in Cisco's stock reflected cautious comments by Cisco officials about the traditionally weak April quarter.
Cisco reported strong growth in revenues and earnings for its second quarter ended in January.
Cisco's quarterly earnings were $0.51, which was a penny above published expectations.
The previous year's earnings were $0.32.
Analysts noted that Cisco management was generally upbeat about company prospects during a conference call on Tuesday evening.
Gruntal analyst David Takata mentioned that the one-to-one book-to-bill ratio going into the seasonally weak Q3 may temporarily concern some investors.
Cisco's year-to-year revenue growth was 73 percent, which was above that of rivals but down from an historic growth rate of over 80 percent.
Merrill Lynch analyst Joe Bellace adjusted his earnings estimates for Cisco to the higher end of his previous range for both the 1997 and 1998 fiscal years.
Bear Stearns analyst Eric Blachno described Cisco's quarterly report as very solid and maintained his buy rating on the stock.

A bill to protect homeowners from paying unnecessary mortgage insurance was passed by the House of Representatives.
The Homeowners Insurance Protection Act was adopted by a vote of 421 to seven.
The act would cancel mortgage insurance once the homeowner has built up sufficient equity.
Representative Henry Gonzalez stated that many people are paying for insurance they no longer need.
Gonzalez urged the Senate to quickly pass the measure.
Consumer advocates claim these policies cost homeowners millions of dollars a year.
Michelle Meier, counsel for government affairs at Consumers Union, expressed optimism about the Senate moving forward with the bill.
The mortgage insurance industry warned that the automatic cancellation proposal would raise costs for loans with low down payments.
Suzanne Hutchinson of the Mortgage Insurance Companies of America criticized the bill for imposing unnecessary government mandates and controls.
Currently, mortgage lenders require insurance for borrowers making a small down payment, such as 5 percent.

Sun Microsystems Inc decided to use powerful computer encoding software made in Russia.
The decision increased pressure on the Clinton administration to relax U.S. export controls on similar products made by American companies.
Encryption products scramble information and require a password or software key to be readable.
Encryption is a critical component of global communications and online commerce over the Internet.
Encryption can prevent unauthorized access to telephone calls and credit card numbers sent over the Internet.
Encryption can also be used by drug cartels or terrorists to evade law enforcement surveillance.
Clinton administration officials oppose exporting powerful U.S. encryption programs unless they allow government access to the software keys.
FBI Director Louis Freeh stated that the encryption 'genie' is not yet 'out of the bottle.'
Rep. Bob Goodlatte criticized the current export control policy and introduced measures in Congress to relax these controls.
The bill introduced by Goodlatte was passed by the House Judiciary Committee and is awaiting action by the International Relations Committee.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin outlined the Clinton administration's plan to allow banks to enter the securities and insurance businesses.
The plan aims to eliminate legal barriers that have been in place for 60 years since the Great Depression.
Rubin stated that the lines separating insurance, securities, and banking industries have blurred due to new financial services and products.
The plan would enable banks, securities firms, and insurance companies to compete under a uniform set of regulations.
Rubin claimed that increased competition from the plan could generate savings of up to $15 billion a year for consumers.
The administration's proposal was highly anticipated and was expected to be introduced in March.
House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach welcomed the plan but noted that some substantive issues remained unresolved.
Bankers Trust New York Corp. Chairman Frank Newman stated that the administration plan would provide momentum for reform.
Consumer advocates expressed disappointment that the proposal lacked adequate protections for bank customers purchasing insurance.
Rubin indicated that the proposal did not take a firm position on allowing banks to combine with non-financial commercial firms.

Czech consumer inflation continued its gradual downtrend in January.
Analysts do not expect a loosening of the central bank's tight monetary policy in the short-term.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) reported January inflation at 1.2 percent month-on-month.
The year-on-year inflation rate in January was 7.4 percent, down from 8.6 percent the previous month.
The key sliding average inflation figure decreased to 8.7 percent from 8.8 percent in December.
The key sliding average inflation figure was down from 9.1 percent in January 1996.
Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka, stated that the January number is about one percentage point lower than a year ago.
The CSU reported that food, drinks, and tobacco products rose 1.3 percent in January.
Transportation costs rose 3.6 percent in January, and housing costs rose by 1.3 percent.
The Czech National Bank (CNB) is expected to maintain high rates in the near term.

Czech annual average consumer inflation in 1996 was 8.8 percent.
The inflation rate in 1995 was 9.1 percent.
The Czech Statistical Bureau reported the inflation figures.
The government's original inflation forecast for 1996 was eight percent.
Analysts expressed optimism about the central bank's monetary policies.
Martin Kupka is an economist at investment bank Patria Finance.
CSU reported month-on-month inflation for December was 0.5 percent.
Year-on-year consumer prices in December were 8.6 percent higher.
CSU chairman Edvard Outrata stated that 1996 core inflation remained around five percent.
The CSU indicated that price increases in foodstuffs, leisure, and textiles accounted for 80 percent of the monthly CPI rise.

The Prague Stock Exchange backed off last week's year-high due to profit taking on Monday.
Market sentiment remains bullish for the coming weeks, according to analysts.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, and Komercni Banka fell sharply, dragging the PX50 index down 0.28 percent to 598.0.
SPT Telecom accounts for 20 percent of the PSE's market capitalization.
CEZ accounts for 14 percent of the PSE's market capitalization.
Komercni Banka accounts for 11 percent of the PSE's market capitalization.
SPT Telecom shares closed down 75 crowns at 3,700.
CEZ shares closed down 28 crowns at 1,202.
Komercni Banka shares closed down 25 crowns at 2,620.
The PSE has had a steady uptrend since 1997 after a slump in the fourth quarter of 1996.

Morgan Stanley merged with Dean Witter Discover.
The merger will create a more competitive force in the European investment banking market.
A banking analyst stated that other banks will see a stronger competitor due to the merger.
Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter agreed to form a financial entity called Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
The market capitalization of the new entity is $21 billion.
Both U.S. and European investment banks are seeking more business in continental Europe and Britain.
The merger will provide considerable backing for Morgan Stanley's European aspirations.
Dean Witter's U.S. retail network could serve as an additional distribution network for Morgan Stanley products.
Dean Witter employs about 120 people in London, with around 35 in institutional equities sales.
Morgan Stanley employs around 2,000 people in its Canary Wharf headquarters.

NatWest Markets experienced a turbulent week that ended with a shake-up of its global debt markets arm.
Three senior staff members departed from NatWest Markets during this week.
NatWest's investment banking arm stated that there was no connection between the management changes and reported losses of 90 million pounds ($144 million).
The losses were accumulated over two years due to systematic mispricings of interest rate options derivatives.
Britain's Serious Fraud Office is monitoring the options situation but is not investigating the reported losses.
The Bank of England and the Securities and Futures Authority are scrutinizing the reported losses.
The management shake-up in NatWest's debt markets division indicates a shift in power to managers from Greenwich Capital.
Gary Holloway and Chip Kruger are the co-chief executives of the new global debt markets division.
Johan Hattingh and Alby Cator were among the senior managers who left NatWest as part of the restructuring.
NatWest has created 10 main areas of responsibility within the debt markets division following the internal announcement of changes.

Nicola Horlick announced her resignation from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) on Thursday.
Horlick was reported to have been offered a promotion at MGAM shortly before her resignation.
A spokesman for Horlick stated that she planned to take legal action against her former employer over constructive dismissal.
Horlick was the head of the British pension fund business at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's MGAM.
Horlick was suspended at MGAM pending an internal investigation into a potential breach of her contract.
The suspension prompted reports of unease among large pension fund clients at MGAM.
The dispute with MGAM involved allegations that Horlick attempted to take members of her team to Dutch bank ABN AMRO.
Horlick received news of her promotion to managing director from MGAM chief executive Robert Smith just days before her resignation.
MGAM faced issues last year due to misvaluations in three of its funds and the sacking of fund manager Peter Young, who is under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office.
Horlick indicated that a group of fund managers demanded she be given more authority due to turmoil following the Peter Young affair.

China criticized Britain's protests against proposed amendments to Hong Kong laws.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang stated that the British protest was unacceptable, unreasonable, and unwise.
Shen Guofang claimed that Britain was forcing its will upon others regarding Hong Kong.
Shen asserted that Hong Kong is China's internal affair and that no other country has the right to interfere.
Britain lodged a strong protest against China's plans to dilute laws guaranteeing civil liberties in Hong Kong.
The British Foreign Office reported that junior minister Jeremy Hanley expressed serious concern over the proposals to Chinese ambassador Jiang Enzhu.
Hanley stated that Hong Kong's bill of rights and related legislation were consistent with the Basic Law.
China accused Britain of violating the Basic Law by introducing laws guaranteeing civil liberties in Hong Kong after the handover.
Shen defended China's plan to amend or repeal 25 laws and ordinances as reversing unilateral changes made by Britain.
A Chinese envoy to Hong Kong attributed the British protest to Chris Patten, the last British governor of Hong Kong.

China's stock markets are currently overheating.
The People's Daily newspaper warned of a potential crash similar to the Wall Street collapse of 1929.
China's foreign currency B share market in Shanghai rose by about 80 percent between November 11 and December 10.
The Shenzhen stock market increased by about 100 percent before experiencing sharp declines.
The Shanghai B-share market fell by 12.26 percent on Friday.
The Shenzhen B-share market dropped by 14.75 percent.
The Shanghai A-share index decreased by 5.51 percent.
The Shenzhen A-share index declined by 4.84 percent.
The People's Daily commentary stated that the stock markets are in an abnormal situation with increasing market risk.
The commentary indicated that the government would not intervene to support the markets during downturns.

Beijing has pledged to allow more imports of U.S. textiles under a new deal.
Washington does not expect to close its textile trade gap with China.
Chinese and U.S. negotiators signed a new textile agreement in Beijing.
The new textile agreement ended the threat of a trade war between the U.S. and China.
The agreement ensures U.S. access to China's textile markets.
China exported $6.5 billion worth of textiles to the United States in 1995.
The United States imported only $64 million worth of textiles from China in 1995.
U.S. textile exports are sluggish due to China's high tariff rates and non-tariff barriers.
The new agreement granted China a U.S. import quota larger than the previous 1994 textile pact.
China pledged to reduce its tariffs on textile imports.

Westfield Holdings Ltd is Australia's largest shopping mall owner.
Westfield Holdings Ltd announced that its U.S. arm would list on the New York Stock Exchange in May.
Westfield Holdings Ltd aims to raise US$400 million in an initial public offering.
Westfield America Inc plans to use the proceeds to spend US$500 million on acquisitions in the United States.
The acquisitions will include buying out Westfield's partners in existing shopping malls and purchasing new malls.
The resulting group will be the fourth largest listed shopping mall owner in the United States, according to chairman Frank Lowy.
Westfield America Trust will list its U.S. vehicle CenterMark Properties Inc as Westfield America Inc.
Westfield America Inc will dilute its 67.2 percent stake in CenterMark to about 50 percent.
Westfield America Inc will first purchase Westfield Holdings' 50 percent stake in the Garden State Plaza shopping centre for US$145 million.
Westfield America Inc will have about US$210 million available to buy out partners and acquire new malls.

The federal government will release the Wallis Inquiry's report into Australia's financial system on Wednesday at midday (0200 GMT).
The government is expected to respond to some parts of the report.
The Wallis Inquiry was set up in June last year and is chaired by businessman Stan Wallis.
The inquiry released a 415-page discussion paper in late November that canvassed various options for reform.
The Inquiry's report was presented to the government last month.
The report will make recommendations about the current 'Six Pillars' policy regarding mergers between major banks and life insurance groups.
The six pillars include Westpac Banking Corp, National Australia Bank Ltd, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society.
The report will address whether the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Treasurer should continue to have the power to reject or approve bank mergers.
Wallis expressed a preference for treating the financial sector like any other sector under competition policy.
The report will consider whether to scrap the current ban on foreign takeovers of the big four banks.

Stadium Australia chairman Peter Ritchie stated that underwriters would not sell unsold passes at a discount ahead of the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games.
Ritchie mentioned that the underwriters aim to sell approximately A$200 million worth of unsold passes at prices above the float's offer prices over the next couple of years.
Ritchie expressed confidence that the unsold passes would sell for more as the Games approach.
Ritchie assured existing gold members that the passes would not be discounted as the Games get closer.
Ritchie confirmed a market speculation of a A$200 million-plus shortfall in the A$364.4 million float of Stadium gold and platinum passes.
The float offered 35,000 passes, which included main stadium tickets to the 2000 Olympics, a 30-year stadium membership, and an equity stake in the stadium.
Ritchie estimated that about 40 percent of the passes had been sold.
The underwriters for the float include ANZ Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Macquarie Bank Ltd, and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
The underwriters must fund the project regardless of the number of packages sold to ensure the completion of the 110,000-seat stadium, which is scheduled to open in 1999.
The Stadium Australia float closed after being open for almost six months, which is more than twice as long as most share offers.

Caterpillar Inc. reported a first quarter profit of $394 million.
The profit of $394 million is the best quarter in the company's history.
The profit is up 33 percent from a year ago.
Caterpillar expects 1997 profits to be higher than the $1.4 billion posted in 1996.
The expectation for higher profits is based on anticipated moderately higher sales.
Caterpillar's earnings were $394 million, or $2.08 a share.
The earnings of $2.08 a share exceeded the Wall Street consensus of $1.69 a share.
Sales and revenues for the quarter were $4.26 billion.
A year earlier, Caterpillar earned $296 million, or $1.53 a share, on revenues of $3.84 billion.
Gross profit margins rose to 26.8 percent of machinery and engine sales from 24.5 percent a year ago.

Harnischfeger Industries Inc. offered to buy Giddings & Lewis Inc. for about $747 million.
The offer includes the assumption of Giddings & Lewis debt.
The offer is priced at $19 per share.
The offer values Giddings & Lewis at approximately $747 million based on 33.2 million outstanding shares.
The offer represents a premium of about 40 percent over Giddings & Lewis's closing price of $13.625 per share.
Harnischfeger Chief Executive Officer Jeffery Glade stated that the company would take on significant debt to finance the deal.
Glade claimed that financing for the deal was fully in place with no contingencies.
Glade expected the deal to add to Harnischfeger earnings immediately upon closing.
The transaction would create an enterprise with combined 1996 revenues of $3.6 billion.
Giddings & Lewis did not comment on its discussions with Harnischfeger.

Harnischfeger Industries Inc made a $19 a share tender offer for Giddings & Lewis Inc.
Industry analysts believe that Harnischfeger's offer may be the best Giddings can receive.
Thomas Burns Jr., an analyst at NatWest Securities, stated that there is unlikely to be a higher bid than Harnischfeger's.
Shares of Giddings & Lewis increased by 6-3/4 to 20-3/8 on Monday.
The increase in Giddings & Lewis shares suggests some buyers expect a higher bid.
William Cooke, an analyst at McDonald & Co, believes that $19 a share represents full value for Giddings & Lewis.
Cooke expressed that Harnischfeger is optimistic in assuming it can double Giddings & Lewis's earnings in the near future.
Harnischfeger aims to use Giddings & Lewis to expand in the industrial products aftermarket service business, estimated to be an $80 billion market.
Some analysts noted that acquiring Giddings & Lewis introduces significant uncertainty for Harnischfeger shareholders.
J. Blair Brumley, an analyst at Dain Bosworth, downgraded Harnischfeger's rating from buy to hold.

A consultant's report was released on Tuesday regarding the Busang gold project in Indonesia.
The Busang gold project was previously promoted by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd. as a significant discovery.
Shareholders sold their shares in Bre-X on Tuesday.
Investigators and analysts are examining how the fraud at Busang occurred.
Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. conducted an audit of the Busang project.
Strathcona's report indicated that tampering at Busang was difficult to believe initially.
Bre-X's last resource estimate claimed there were 71 million ounces of gold at Busang based on 16,400 samples.
Strathcona concluded that most of the gold in Bre-X's samples likely came from another source.
The report suggested that tampering likely occurred at Bre-X's storage warehouse in Samarinda.
Strathcona noted that Bre-X officials had previous studies indicating abnormalities in the Busang gold find.

William Resources Inc is a Canadian gold mining company.
William Resources Inc expects to achieve over 200,000 ounces of gold production in 1997.
William Resources Inc has the financial resources to withstand a weak gold market.
The company reported promising early tests of its Ballarat East project in Australia.
William Resources Inc has put its plans for the Ruster's Roost project on hold.
The company provided a favorable update on its operations in Scandinavia and Brazil.
William Resources Inc is selling its disappointing Mexican project.
In 1996, William Resources produced an annualized 100,000 ounces of gold at an average cash cost of US$349 per ounce.
The Bjorkdal mine in Sweden, acquired in December 1996, is expected to exceed 100,000 ounces in 1997 at a cash cost of US$216 per ounce.
The Jacobina project in Brazil is forecasted to produce 65,000 ounces of gold in 1997 at a cash cost of US$285 per ounce.

Bre-X Minerals Ltd. is based in Calgary, Canada.
Bre-X expects to receive a report from Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. regarding the Busang find in Indonesia.
The report is anticipated to be received over the weekend.
Bre-X plans to release the findings of the report on Monday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange is preparing for increased trading activity in Bre-X shares when the report is released.
Steve McAnulty is a spokesman for Bre-X.
Bre-X hired Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. to review its Busang project due to emerging doubts about the gold find.
Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. reported on March 26 that its preliminary tests found insignificant amounts of gold at the Busang site.
Bre-X has estimated that the Busang site contains approximately 71 million ounces of gold.
Panic selling of Bre-X shares resulted in a loss of nearly C$3 billion from the company's market value after Freeport's announcement.

Ford Motor Co. agreed to sell its interests in Budget Rent a Car Corp. to Team Rental Group Inc. for about $350 million.
Team Rental Group Inc. is based in Daytona Beach, Florida, and operates 13 Budget franchises with 155 locations.
Team Rental Group Inc. also leases commuter vans in 22 states and sells used vehicles.
Ford Vice Chairman Ed Hagenlocker stated that the sale is in the best interests of Budget and Ford.
The sale of Ford's preferred stock in Budget is not expected to close until March.
Ford will book an unspecified gain on the deal in its fourth quarter 1996 earnings.
The gain will partially reverse a $437 million after-tax write-off Ford took on its investment and loans to Budget.
The deal will add cash to Ford's finances, moving it closer to a future stock repurchase program.
Ford executives indicated that stock repurchases will be considered after cutting automotive costs by $1 billion and increasing cash reserves above $7 billion.
Ford's decision marks a shift to reduce its rental car holdings and reverses a previous plan to acquire full ownership of Budget.

Ford Motor Co. will restructure its Halewood car plant in England but will not close it.
Some job losses are expected at the Halewood plant.
Susanne Wegerhoff is a Ford spokeswoman based in Brentwood, England.
Ford will announce operating changes for the Halewood plant after a meeting with major unions.
Wegerhoff denied a report that Ford was threatening to close the Halewood facility.
Wegerhoff stated that Halewood has a future and that a plan will be discussed to secure it.
London's Observer newspaper reported that Ford wanted to cut 500 jobs at Halewood.
The Halewood plant employs 6,500 workers and produces Ford's European-designed Escort sub-compact cars.
Ford's losses in Europe increased to $472 million in the third quarter of 1996.
Industry analysts consider the Halewood plant the least efficient of Ford's three Escort plants in Europe.

General Motors Corp. will gain $9.5 billion in value from selling Hughes Aircraft Co.
General Motors will gain about $100 million in annual savings from no longer writing off Hughes' goodwill.
General Motors writes off about $25 million each quarter associated with its 1985 purchase of Hughes' defense assets.
The write-offs will end after the sale to Raytheon Co. closes, expected by midyear.
The deal, known as 'Project Triple Play,' includes the spin-off and merger of Hughes' defense business with Raytheon.
Hughes' Delco Electronics business will shift into General Motors' automotive operations.
Most of the $4.4 billion in cash from the deal will be injected into Hughes' telecommunications business.
General Motors Chief Financial Officer J. Michael Losh stated that the cash will help complete Hughes Electronics' $3 billion acquisition of PanAmSat Corp.
General Motors plans to use the cash to fund the growth of its DirecTV satellite broadcasting business and Hughes Network Systems business.
General Motors stockholders will control 30 percent of Raytheon after the Hughes merger.

GKN Plc is a UK auto-components group.
A U.S. court awarded $398 million in damages to franchisees against GKN Plc.
Analysts predict GKN's shares could decline further if the judgement is not overturned on appeal.
One analyst estimates shares could fall by 6.6 percent from the last closing level of 1045 pence per share if the judgement stands.
GKN's shares have already decreased by three percent to 1009.5 pence during the current session.
Another analyst predicts shares could drop by 50 pence if GKN loses the appeal.
The second analyst believes the judgement is a market shock but not significant to GKN's operations.
GKN stated that damages could increase to $554 million under the North Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act.
The analyst noted that GKN has 240-250 million pounds of free cash reserves unrelated to customer advance payments.
The analyst has rated GKN as a 'sell'.

Britain announced the preferred bidders for two more passenger rail franchises.
The Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) selected Great Western Holdings Ltd as the preferred bidder for the North West Regional Railways franchise.
Great Western Holdings Ltd's bid group is owned 51 percent by existing management and employees, with FirstBus and 3i venture capital each owning 24.5 percent.
The Thameslink franchise was awarded to GOVIA, which includes Go-Ahead Group Plc and VIA-GTI.
There are three remaining franchises to be awarded before the British election deadline in May 1997.
The remaining franchises include ScotRail and North East Regional Rail.
The privatisation of Britain's rail industry began in 1995 and included the sell-off of rail infrastructure under Railtrack.
Chris Moyes, Go-Ahead's commercial director, stated that the Thameslink line has significant potential for revenue.
Trevor Smallwood, chairman of FirstBus, mentioned that the winner of the Central Trains deal could see revenues of around 70 million pounds.
Go-Ahead's shares increased by 36 pence to 515, National Express's shares rose by 26 pence to 547, and FirstBus's shares increased by 12.5 pence.

Nissan Motor Co announced a 215 million pound ($357 million) investment in its British plant at Sunderland.
The investment aims to build a new model and will create 800 jobs at Nissan UK.
An additional 2,700 jobs are expected to be created in British supplier firms due to this investment.
The announcement followed Ford Motor Co's decision to cut 1,300 jobs at its Halewood plant in Liverpool.
Nissan plans to add a third model to the production line at Nissan Motor (UK) Ltd (NMUK).
The investment will be used for production equipment, including moulds for the new car.
Nissan will produce models in the Pulsar range, known as the Almera in Britain and elsewhere in Europe, starting from 2000.
The decision to build a third model in Europe was reviewed internally by Nissan's European vice-president and Ian Gibson.
Ian Gibson, chief executive of Nissan UK, stated that the investment is a vote of confidence for Sunderland.
Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang welcomed Nissan's decision as a significant development in their European presence.

Shares of 3Com Corp slid on Monday.
Shares of U.S. Robotics Corp slid on Monday.
Traders reported that prospects dimmed for a new suitor for Robotics shareholders.
The merger agreement between 3Com and Robotics is valued at $7.3 billion.
The merger agreement requires either party to pay up to $160 million if the deal falls through.
3Com closed on Monday at 32-13/16, down 19/64.
U.S. Robotics shares closed at 55-3/8, down 7/16.
The merger terms require 3Com to exchange 1.75 shares of its stock for each Robotics share.
The value of the 3Com offer to Robotics shareholders has decreased from $68 to $57-27/64.
Analysts indicated that shareholder dissatisfaction extends into mid-level management at Robotics.

AT&T Corp. withdrew its application with the U.S. government for a license to launch new communications satellites.
AT&T's decision to cancel its application to the Federal Communications Commission followed the disposal of several existing satellite businesses.
AT&T has completed its exit from the satellite operations business.
AT&T stated that investment in new Ka-band satellite technology was a drain on capital resources.
AT&T's renewed focus is on its core long-distance business and key growth areas like wireless, online, and local services.
Ka-band refers to radio frequencies that handle two-way voice and data communications.
The new class of satellites would have allowed AT&T to offer next-generation communications services such as video, data transmission, and high-speed Internet services.
AT&T spokesman Gary Morgenstern stated that satellites are not core to the company's focus.
AT&T continues to offer satellite-based services through its minority investment in the Direct TV venture of Hughes Electronics Corp.
AT&T's Ka-band project was formally known as the AT&T VoiceSpan Satellite System.

New York State utility regulators are set to approve the Bell Atlantic Corp/NYNEX Corp merger.
The approval is subject to several conditions that will be set forth prior to a final vote on Thursday.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to permanently locate its headquarters in New York.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to reduce rates.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to issue $300 million in rebates.
Regulators will consider requiring the combined company to improve customer service.
The merger would create the nation's largest local phone operator.
The merger still faces hurdles in Washington and New York, which is currently withholding its approval.
The Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission are conducting increased scrutiny of the merger.
New York State Attorney General Dennis Vacco is conducting an ongoing anti-trust review of the merger.
